review_headline: Plug and play, best selection of channels, cell phone app replaces the remote.  What more can you ask?
review_body:
This Roku stick is giving me access to Acorn TV and many other online channels, which is great for a BBC junkie like me. I can see Netflix and Amazon too, along with HBO and many others. The reason to buy a Roku is that they have the best selection of channels compared to every other similar device, and they don't force you into a particular vendor, the way that the Google and Amazon devices do. Each company's stick has a particular set of channels they support and if the device you have doesn't do the channel you want, you're cooked. You kinda have to choose your device based on the channels you want to watch. I have a Sony Blue Ray player that has a fixed set of online channels and that's it. It doesn't add channels when it upgrades and it doesn't do Acorn. So, the Roku stick. By the way, there's a cell phone app for the Roku, that is far superior to the Roku remote. The app has an actual key board and will listen to voice commands. So you probably don't really need the Roku 3, unless you really need games and headphones. And I always buy refurb's. Low price and high quality every time.

(Also, Roku will send you a free bendable HDMI adapter, if you have a hard time hiding it behind your TV)

This didn't bother me because most of the games like this do the same thing. The second was it was slow on the kindle. Again, I have not had that  at all. I have enjoyed this game to this point. I cannot speak of the length because I am only on chapter two, but like what I have experienced so far.

I'm disappointed in the creators. They do not give you any hints to start out with nor enough coins to get hints on the puzzles. They don't even tell you how much the hints cost.
There IS in app purchases, so the creators want you to buy coins for hints or other puzzles. It feels like the creators only care about getting money from their consumers.

One thing I do like, however, is that you can skip over troublesome puzzles for free.
Also some of the puzzles are challenging, so it makes you think. I wish it weren't as challenging in level one, but for a free app it a good game.

It's basically the same game as the more popularly known as "4 Pics, 1 Word," "Four Pics," and games of that type. You get four pictures and the number of letters the word contains. You study the pictures to figure out what the word is. You can then use the letter bank to type in the word. If you don't know what the word is, however, you can (if you have enough coins,) use coins to buy one of two hints. The first is to remove letters, from the letter bank, that aren't used in the puzzle. The second hint places one of the letters, from the letter bank, into the word you are trying to solve.
I'm sorry if that sounds confusing.

Overall, you get what you pay for, no pun intended. It's a pretty popular game and the app is good quality, but don't expect to be able to use the hints very often.

review_headline: GREAT app with GREAT features. But only use it on a rooted phone where you've protected your privacy properly.
review_body:
░░░░░GREAT APP IF YOU ARE ROOTED░░░░░

The permissions on this app are insane, and completely unacceptable. But it's a GREAT app to be able to check prices while you're in physical stores.

The dodgy permissions are a prime example (get it..prime..see what I did there? ) of why all Android phones should be rooted. With root capabilities you can have privacy guard features that lock this app out of the ability to use all those permissions it's requesting. If you deny those permissions the app can still ask the phone for your SMS and call history all it wants, but the phone will tell the app there is no data. The app will continue to work properly. This same thing will repeat itself for every piece of data you don't want to share with the app.

Every phone should come with this kind of privacy protection built in, but none do. You have to root the phone and install customer software to utilize this level of security. But it is completely worth it because it allows you to use permission hungry apps like the Amazon app that want to know scary amounts of data about you...and use them worry free because the app has no access to all that data.

I use this app all the time and I absolutely love it. But I run it with those privacy protections and feel secure doing so.

Also, this version of the app is different and better than the version available on Google Play.

Being a fan of the original Oregon Trail I though I would give this a try, but I was disappointed. It was not like the original at all. It changed way to much for this day and age. It has become more of a city builder than what it was. I though I could look pass that and just play a fun game but for one reason it made me stop playing it. Do not let the free to play trick you. In the game your character has an energy bar. It goes down when you do activities in the world. I realized very fast that the bar goes down very quickly. Before I new it, my energy bar was gone and my character couldn't do anything. Then every 1 to 3 minutes it goes up by 1. Which means if you want you energy bar to go back to full you have to wait like 30 minutes or longer. But there is a way to buy energy with REAL money. So basically the game depletes your energy fast and it gets back energy very slowly. So to actually enjoy the game they are forcing you to use real money to actually be able to play the game instead of every 10 to 15 minutes waiting 30 minutes to an hour to play the game. Don't get me wrong I know FTP games need to have some sort of real money purchases for them to profit, but when they make the game unplayable, that's just wrong in my opinion.

So I would not recommend this if you want to play it for free and don't want to wait around all the time. If they got rid of this one thing, then I truly believe I would enjoy this game for a while. But for now I'd rather play a game I actually paid for so I don't have to go through this.

Bottom line: While the game is short on content (I finished it in around two hours, two and half hours max), the puzzles are very good. So good, in fact, that I finished it all in one go! At a tenth the price of a movie ticket and much more satisfying, you can't go wrong with factory balls (although the name is admittedly not very catchy). It is well worth the asking price, even at three times the price it'd be a steal.

A lot of the puzzle games on mobile are very weak, where the puzzles are more about willpower than brainpower; this one is different! Instead of just making the puzzles more tedious+time consuming as you go on, this developer gets that puzzles are supposed exercise your mind instead of your patience.

Things start off slow to ease you into the mechanics, but each level increases with complexity (the difficulty curve is fairly gentle though, so don't shy away if you aren't exactly a puzzle maniac like I am!). There is no timer and you can't fail (there is a button to instantly reset your ball on levels that have operations that can't be undone), so it is never frustrating, and the last few levels in both sets are extremely satisfying when you beat them.

The basic gameplay involves taking a blank ball and matching it to the picture given to you. You are given whatever colors necessary, which when used will color the entire ball, along with various tools that can prevent certain parts from being colored (there are also tools that alter shape, as well as seeds that take the place of colors, but the core of the gameplay remains roughly the same). You are never given anything you don't need; this game doesn't rely on cheap tricks or misdirection.

While it may seem straightforward, these puzzles won't disappoint. Especially compared to the other offerings on mobile (flow, lyne, pipes, etc, if they can be considered puzzle games. It is more similar to the quell series or Splice than those games), factory balls is asuperb standout of the genre.

I really loved Goldfish and several of the other games included in this app. BUT, I have come to dislike it now, especially after the updates.  I don't like that the minimum bet keeps changing to higher amounts the more I play! When I play Goldfish in the casinos, the minimum bet NEVER changes!  I decide when and if I want to change the amount of the bet. In this game, I don't have that option! The minimum bet keeps increasing as I reach higher levels of play. Warning! After you play this version of Goldfish for a period of time, be prepared to bet a minimum amount of $8,000 a spin or more! That's crazy especially since you already know that the odds of actually winning are so low!  Do the math. Let's say I have $200,000 in coins to play and add in $25,000 bonus money that the game gives every 4 hours. Sounds like a lot, right? Not! You have approximately 28 spins at $8,000 a spin! If you're lucky, you MIGHT get a bonus that will allow you a few more spins. That's a big IF! Apparently my luck has run out because, with each update, the bonuses show up less frequently; and I typically go through $225,000 in a matter of minutes! Of course, conveniently, the App store pops up offering these "splash sales" to buy more coins. I bought into that scheme a number of times but finally realized that I was spending a substantial amount of "real" money to play Goldfish and had nothing in return to show for it! I no longer enjoy playing this game on my Kindle!  I might as well go to the casino. At least there, I have control over "how much" I am willing to bet. Plus, when I start losing, I can move to another machine. I don't have that option with this game; except turning it completely off!  Where's the fun in that?

review_body: Wow, I feel like a voice in the wilderness. So many 4-5 star reviews I was hesitant to write anything negative for fear of embarrassment. With that said...I spent the 2 bucks on the paid version of this app. Normally I test the free version of anything before the paid, logical right? I blew 2 bucks on this. The reflexes necessary to control my avatar in the jump/float process to get thru a world was for me at least, virtually impossible. After 234 failures to advance in PRACTICE mode I gave up. As I write I have no idea how there are no negative reviews on this game. Logically I suspect that I must have been doing something wrong. How could this many people love this app while I could not operate it successfully at all??? I simply decided that I owe it to those like me out there that might be afraid to comment on their failure because of the massive overwhelming positive reviews. Yep, I hv the courage to do this. I may be an idiot. I may of course be the only one brave enough to describe this game's difficulty for many like myself. The games will keep them entertained for awhile. So, in summation, if you want more interactive story apps featuring the Peanuts gang, choose the Loud Crow apps. But for someone who enjoys reading along with a story and playing games to go along with the story, then this app will do just fine. This game has some big problems. Here are some of them:

When it loads a board, it puts the tiles in random positions. This means that the letters needed to make a word may not be adjacent to each other. For example, it might give you the letters DKUC for the word DUCK, which you can't possibly join without going outside the borders. If you exit the puzzle and reload it, the letters might be CDKU.

The tiles are supposed to drop down when you get a word (on the multiple-word puzzles). Sometimes they do, sometimes they don't. (It doesn't matter that much because you don't exactly have to choose adjacent letters--it's a little weird...)

Finally, If there are multiple instances of a letter, you have to use each letter in exactly the right place. HAPpY isn't the same as HApPy. (Where P and p are the two instances of P tiles and are indistinguishable.)

Honestly, these things alone probably wouldn't break the game (although when the words are "BALL" and "BELAY" you're in for a tough time). What's really wrong with it is that it has a finite list of puzzles that you can (must!) work through. If it had a built-in dictionary and could generate a large number of random puzzles, then that would make the game playable over the long term (although still very frustrating).

(There are also some possible bugs that make it easier to crack the code on some levels. I'm not sure if they make it better or worse.)

review_body: It's a really fun game. The controls are simple, and there are no complex menus or options, like in other pet games and simulations. The Derp is adorable and fun to take care of, even though it's hard to keep it alive. The Derp only has two stats- the heart meter (health) and the chicken leg (hunger). There are many amusing foods to feed your Derp, such as birthday cake. When you first hatch a new Derp, you start out with 3 Cheetohs, but these will be depleted quickly. You will also need to use bug spray to prevent Mosquitosis, and use the bucket to put out a Derp on fire. You will need to buy lots of food for your growing Derp, which you can purchase with Derp Coins, which you can get by tapping the block at the top. Be careful, though. When the block starts to shake, it will turn into a skull, and if your Derp hits this, it will become momentarily stunned and the block will take a few secons to come back. The Derp has 4 stages, Baby, Toddler, Kid and Adult, and each has an interesting and amusing description in the Album, accessible from the main menu at the top right corner. The game is simple and good for everyone of all ages.

review_headline: Bit Fuzzy on a 5.5" Screen, But One of the Best Hidden Object Games I have Played
review_body:
It is one of the best HO games I have played. The added "customization" play of decorating rooms with money earned is a unique element of interest, and an extraordinarily robust venue of game modes and matching styles keeps play value going where other HOs snooze. Time and thought went into this game, and the effort isn't hidden.

Evaluated on a generic Android smartphone, 5.5" screen, KitKat 4.4.2 - and it played fine. However, I would definitely say this is best on larger screens, or at least not on an IPS display. At smaller resolutions, the scene and objects are on the fuzzy side, a bit hard to focus on. Yeah, I had to grab the reading glasses by the second level. There is zoom and pan, though, which helps.

Sometimes the object to be found will be in a different orientation that what is pictured. Objects themselves are logically places, e.g. no mid-air hanging llamas in the bathroom. A "Relax" mode is available at any point under the pause menu; otherwise, there is a element of Time Management with the customer tabs to the left. They show up, wanting an object ($13 bucks for a fly? lol), and you need to very quickly decide which objects are easiest to find, tap it, collect money from the customer, and get a brand new customer tab and demand. All this as the timer bar dwindles.

With cold cash in the hot hand, you begin giving rooms a face lift. Not a massive selection of décor, but still rather neat sense of continuing accomplishment.

No concerns in the Code: Amazon GameCircle and Google Play Services providing score leaderboards and achievements. Amazon's own dashboard analytics, Insights, which is a necessary component now of GameCircle, Adobe Air, and a C/C++ dev library. Network Access for the online leaderboard submission, and Read/Write External Storage. I moved the game to my SD Card, initially leaving approx. 19MB on my Device Memory. However, as the game is played, Game Data does increase that Device Memory amount (I am currently at 22MB on my Device Memory).

The game runs OFFLINE, and it does exit cleanly, but not by the back-key. On the main menu, there is an red door exit icon that will cleanly quit, but getting to the main menu from play is a little involved. During play, pause the game, choose "Décor Room" and "Save & Exit". From there, tap the settings icon in the lower left... THEN tap "Main Menu". Now you can finally cleanly exit. Like I said, a bit involved. If you home-screen out at any point, the game continues to run in a paused manner.

I saw no pushes or nags while I played, but a few More Games links are scattered about - one being a large HOME MAKEOVER 3 banner over the "Start" button.oes increase that Device Memory amount (I am currently at 22MB on my Device Memory).

I picked this game up when it was a Free App of the Day and had it sitting in my cloud library for a while. I personally enjoy object finding games, so I finally downloaded this to give it a try.

This app has three games on it, although I only played one, Himalayan Adventure. The price for this app seems fine to me, since each 'adventure' is rather short and could be completed in one sitting if dedicated. The visuals are nice and don't suffer from bad blurring when I zoom in unlike other object finding games I've played. The difficulty appears to be fairly low, since most items it wants you to find are right in plain sight or large. Only a couple times have I been stuck and restarted.

As you expect, you collect objects from a given and mostly randomized list. You move along a map going through about 36 levels, a few of them repeated three times, and about half way through you start doing these timed match three games. They seem to only be there for point making and don't work all that great. There's been many times when I select a tile to move up and it goes to the side.

The plot is next to non-existent and putting it all together would barley make a proper paragraph. As a person who enjoys stories, I felt this game was really lacking. If you enjoy gameplay more, then I guess you'd be alright. I finished the first 'adventure' and decided I had enough. The game could have potential if given an actual story and tweaked, but for now it's going to be sitting on my cloud again.

REBALL is a challenging and addictive game that requires moving a colored ball along a free horizontal, vertical or diagonal path to group three or more balls of that color together.  Those balls are then removed, which frees up more paths.  The object is to remove all the balls from the board and advance to the next game.  The challenge is that there can be multiple ways to remove some of the balls, and an incorrect choice may not free up paths that block the removal of other balls.  Or you may have 7 balls of a color, which requires you to remove four of them in one play; and your initial choice may leave one ball left over.  You receive a score for each game that you clear the board based on the time it took and the complexity of of the board.  You can restart a board or undo moves.  If you're unsuccessful in clearing the board, an option allows you to be shown the steps needed and you can advance to the next game. review_headline: Works OK - problem with accessing downloaded files if offline
review_body:
I've been listening to the BBC Radio4 All Things Considered podcast for a long time - began listening to it with my old iPhone (long out of date). I've had a great deal of trouble finding it and listening to it from my android tablet. This app works pretty well for this particular show - though a couple of things are problematic. Note: this app isn't put out by the BBC, or by "Media Applications Technologies Ltd" which seems to be owned by the BBC. It's put out by a company in Hong Kong that seems to be completely unaffiliated with the BBC.

For those who want to try it, here's what I found useful / problematic:

I was able to find the show I wanted, make it a favorite so that I can go to it quickly, see which episodes are available, download the podcasts and listen to them with excellent sound, etc.

However, although you can download the podcasts, you can't actually access them unless you're online. The app shows the icon for the show and the title, but if there's no network connection it gives you an error and tells you to try again later. Once you get connected and it brings up the podcasts you've downloaded, you're good - you can lose the connection and it will continue with no problem. But this is still a problem for me, as I often don't have connectivity for my tablet. It's frustrating to know you've downloaded something but not be able to get at it. I tried searching for the raw files, thinking perhaps I could listen to them with a different app, but was unable to find them.

Keeping track of where I left off seemed to be a problem, though this may be due to my not doing something properly. When I did a Pause and Resume, it continued where it left off. But when I stopped and then went back to run it again, it seemed to always want to start from the beginning.

There are two buttons, labeled "A" and "B" that seem to create start and stop points for looping...

More useful (for me at least) there's a "sleep" button that allows you to set the app to shut off after some number of minutes.

There is an impressive variety of podcasts put out by the BBC - but I was disappointed to see how many of them are only available to listeners in the UK. I understand that there are licensing issues, etc. But it would be kinder for the app to just ask me up front whether I'm a UK listener or not, and then block out all the ones I can't listen to - rather than making me click on one after another and be disappointed over and over. Eventually the disappointment was too much and I gave up even looking for any more "available" podcasts.

review_headline: Set your own reminder for the 30-day trial and be prepared to purchase equipment
review_body: This service was very disappointing. Like other users, I encountered a lot of issues with the streaming quality and was unable to make it through a full workout with out waiting on the video to buffer. What's more, many of the workouts required the purchase of home gym equipment from hand weights to resistance bands, medicine balls, and steps. Very frustrating when looking for a low cost, home workout and gym alternative to feel like I need to outfit a full gym in my living room. Daily Burn just happens to sell all this equipment, and they also push vitamins and supplements.  Daily Burn did not send a notification that my trial was ending and I would be billed. Yes, shame on me for not making note of the 30-day deadline, but a notification would have been both a kindness and a good faith gesture. Instead I was charged and they do not offer pro-rated refunds.  Streaming video service for at home workouts is a great idea, but I walked away feeling like this company was all about selling the add-ons and making a quick buck. I regret not having done my research.  EDIT: So, the DailyBurn honored my request for a pro-rated refund. I feel better about the company (and raised the rating from 2 to 3 stars) yet stand by my recommendation to make sure this is what you want before starting the trial and make a note on your calendar to remind you to shut it off if you choose not to continue.

review_headline: Most puzzles too easy, but a pleasant distraction all the same
review_body:
This is yet another in a long line of "escape" games. You're presented with a room, and based on clues in the environment you have to figure out what buttons to push, colors to match, actions to take, etc.

Unlike others in the genre, each room only contains a single puzzle rather than a series of interconnected puzzles, making this one feel a little simple and rushed. In addition, most of the 100 (as of this writing) puzzles are easy enough so that you can blow through 10 floors in a few minutes. If you are stumped, try shaking your device. Many of the puzzles rely on shaking the device or flipping it upside down -- too many, to be honest. And if you're TOTALLY stumped, which may happen since five or six of the puzzles are pretty baffling, search Youtube. All the solutions are on there.

The game is nothing special, but as a free distraction it does exactly what it's supposed to do. And yes, it's actually free. I played all 100 levels without having to pay, and the ads were not intrusive.

Fun enough for what it is. If you like escape games, give it a whirl.

Boom Dots has gone from one of those games I play every so often to kill time to one of those games I turn to when killing time, travelling, and more. The idea is really simple; you have a shape that floats at varying heights and speeds on the screen above a smaller shape you control and you have to release your shape and hit the bigger one. If you hit it anywhere, you get one point. If you manage to hit it center-mass, you get extra points. The board below you moves as well, so you cannot simply sit all day and aim without timing out and dying.

The game keeps statistics on you so you can see how you are doing both all-time, within so many weeks, and within so many days. I personally like that it keeps how many times you have played, your all-time high score, your all-time average, and then averages for this for the past week. When I started, I had a fairly low average because I was not playing and trying, but when I noticed it kept these I kept trying to improve my aim. Another thing that helps with this is upgraded shapes, which you get for missions.

Missions within the game are really straight-forward. Hit "x" amount of minutes played, score "x' amount of points, and so on. As you complete missions, you unlock different types of boom dots. I personally like the one where your item looks like a saw blade and you are trying to hit skull. There are others such as the heartbreaker, with heart being shot at, other ypes of shapes, and so on. This gives you another incentive towards completion.

All in all, this is a really good game. It does have advertisements within the game but they are not terribly intrusive, not compared to most "free games" hitting the market now. Check it out, kill a little time, and compete with yourself and others you know.

review_headline: So desperate for content they are fear-mongering
review_body:
I started using this app the day I found out I was pregnant. I wanted something fun to read about the developing baby and a way to count down the days as I go. Instead, what I found was a bunch of daily advice that is ridiculous. This is my fourth baby, so I know what to expect from pregnancy. At first I was amused by some of the crazy advice they gave and shared it with my husband so we could chuckle. But now, in the middle of week seven, I am no longer laughing. Some of this advice is just going to scare new mothers to death. It seems they were so desperate to have something to write every day that they wrote about a bunch of stuff that will make a first-time mom fear that she is one grocery bag away from causing a miscarriage.

Day 43 says "If you have a history of miscarriages, your obstetrician will probably recommend that you refrain from lifting heavy objects. Not only is your center of gravity changing, but lifting something with improper form can cause you to pull a muscle or a ligament. To avoid being overloaded, divide up your grocery list and make more frequent trips to the store so you aren't purchasing as may items at one time. If no one is at home to help you bring them in, buy non-perishable items only and leave them in the car until you can get some help. If you absolutely have to lift, pay careful attention to your stance and keep your core muscles tight. Try to lift things that are level with your core so you aren't reaching up, down, over, or under. Clear other items out of the range of motion so you have ample room and control."

This makes me so angry. I have a history of miscarriages but I can tell you that it's not because I bought too many groceries! While I agree that you probably shouldn't be hefting 40 lb bags of dog food, it will not harm you or the baby to take in bags of groceries, one or two at a time. I can't imagine how this could mess with a woman's head if she had a miscarriage and wondered if she'd lifted too many heavy things. Irresponsible.

There is other dumb advice, including recommending hitting the stores to buy baby stuff like "newborn-sized sleepers" at week 5 1/2. That's crazy. You don't even know if you're having a boy or girl yet! I mean, if someone is wanting to go buy stuff that's fine, but an app shouldn't be telling you to do it. On day 37 they tell you that if you have too much caffeine you could cause a miscarriage due to some unsubstantiated studies (which they admit) or that your baby will experience caffeine withdrawals after birth. Now, I don't drink caffeine at all but it annoys me how this app throws out all these scare tactics that aren't proven and are just going to put a new mom in a frenzy.

review_headline: Great UI, VERY Easy to Navigate...
review_body:
This app has so far surpassed my expectations in just about every way. One of the things I appreciate the most is its flexibility. This product is great for a quick cleaning, but there are many other features that I've just recently taken the time to check out-and was pleasantly surprised.
There are 4 basic sections that I feel are wise to get familiar with when the app is first installed--Junk Cleaner, RAM Booster, Memory Booster & App Manager. Basically, just tap to clean.
It tells you how much space you've opened up, and more. Then if you are interested in more personalization, there's the ability to back anything up, delete things (another good thing is that it tells you if you're about to delete something that you shouldn't).
It also gives you a list of apps that you rarely/never use, details of how much space each app takes up,etc. I was surprised by how many apps I had on my Kindle Fire HD that I NEVER use!
I do believe that I'm at least beginning to ramble, so I'll add one more favorite feature and say Goodbye:-).
You also have a security system. You can manually run it or set a schedule. There are SO many details available...BUT, remember- it's totally up to us how in depth we want to get with these things.
One more thing lol!! I'm not very knowledgeable about technology in general, and I've found many comparable apps intimidating b/c the technical jargon is overwhelming. I end up afraid to do anything with them b/c there's no explanation available for people who may not totally understand all the terminology.
Totally not the case with this app. We are told what's being done, the results, and if we're talking freeing up space, the numbers to let us see just how much more productive we've made our device!
Thanks to anyone who actually read this, and I wish you all a great day.

I never once had to purchase any tokens as I won at least several thousand daily, and sometimes even won much more when the "bonus spins" on Wheel, etc. produced high winnings.

However, I no longer have the daily challenge screen, and have been ripped off of my daily bonuses several times, even though I log in daily. I have discovered that the Wheel bonus spins no longer allow me any higher multiplier than 50 or 75, and I lose more than I win on regular spins on all the slots. Occasionally I get lucky on one of the games but I have noticed that it seems as though GSN has gone in and changed the odds more to their favor, which will eventually force people to purchase tokens. review_headline: Mario Kart meets NFL Blitz in a fun, challenging, and very addicting race car game!
review_body:
For starters, I don't play a lot of video games anymore. I'm in my early 30's and outside of throwing a game in my Xbox every few weeks, I don't pick up a controller very often. Even then, it is more for the social element, as I'm often playing with friends.

I was looking for something to watch on my Amazon Fire (a truly awesome device) when I saw this app as a recommended download. On a whim, I hit download, went and poured some coffee, and came back to what would come to be known as MY ENTIRE SUNDAY MORNING! This game is my new definition of addicting! It is so much fun, and it has the perfect challenge level. If you've ever played the old NFL Blitz video games, this feels exactly like them in that you're never out of a race, but you're never going to run away with one either. I would seriously celebrate when I won a race, which is something I haven't done while playing a video game alone in many year.

The game was free, which is incredible for how detailed and involved the game is. With that said, this is one of those games where you can pay as you go to buy tokens to download add-ons for your vehicles. I have not done this, as I like the difficulty factor, but I can see how this can add up quickly if you want it to.

I have only played the racing events, but I guess there is also a drifting mode that I have not tried. I'll have to check it out next weekend when I'm burning through another cold Wisconsin Sunday.

review_headline: HBO GO app better RESOLUTION & FASTER than HBO NOW app on my Amazon Fire TV!
review_body: Today 4-24-2016 I got the free month of HBO NOW on my Amazon Fire TV 4K on a 1080P TV for Game of Thrones "GOT", and it was slow to load (near 9 seconds), didn't remember my place, and had a great amount of juddering, macroblocking and pixelization in the previews and then macroblocking and pixelization in the GOT S1/E1.   I have TWC Internet, at 200mbs.  Because I'm a videophile and like things in high resolution (can't wait to buy a 4K TV!). I went ahead and activated HBO on DirecTV (3 months free of Cinemax), and went to the HBO GO app that I have used in the past on the Amazon Fire TV.  In the HBO GO app, GOT loaded  immediately, and the resolution was perfect - no juddering, macroblocking, or pixelization.  Just a 1-2 second ramp up to Perfect resolution - believed to be true 1080P.  The HBO GO app remembered my place when I went between the HBO GO and NOW app.  If someone has a similar configuration that I have, I would suggest signing up for HBO through DirecTV, and then getting the HBO GO app for the Amazon fire TV. The resolution and experience is simply perfect.  I hope this helps.  :-)

review_headline: A free game done right. Addictive gameplay, responsive controls and charming visuals. Particularly great on the Fire TV.
review_body:
Crossy Road is a simple, yet awesome game. Basically, it plays like an updated version of the old arcade classic Frogger: guide your character across lanes of traffic, logs floating across a river, even train tracks. At first things start at a slow, easier-to-navigate pace, but as you progress, the cars and trucks get faster, the logs get smaller and the highways have more and more lanes. The game also forces you to keep pace with a slow, forward scroll, so if you try to be too patient, and eagle flies down and takes you away, ending your game. As you go, you collect coins that allow you to unlock additional characters in the game. This is where I really appreciate Cross Road, because while the game gives you the ability to purchase the characters outright through in-app purchases, it doesn't force that upon you as the only option. If you can collect enough coins (100 to be exact), you can unlock the additional characters randomly that way (through an arcade-style sequence where you use a vending machine to buy the random character with your earned coins). Some characters (like the developer mascot Hipster Whale), can only be unlocked by doing something specific in the game (for that character, you have to hop on him as he briskly swims past among the logs in the river). Hipster Whale also gives you chances for bonus coins, with free gifts at timed intervals (starts off at 10 minutes, but eventually maxes-out at 6 hours rather quickly...this includes non-play time between sessions, so it's not as long as it sounds like) and chances to earn more by watching videos.

The characters are all pretty great too. You have a selection of fairly generic animals, but some (like the Doge meme, Poopy Penguin and alien Specimen 115) are downright hilarious. My favorite is probably the Doge, which plays like any other character, but as you progress, messages pop in up Helvetica font straight out of the meme (Much cars. Many hop. Such wow.). There are also some non-animal characters, like the Grave Digger, Celebrity and Crazy ol' Ben, all of which have some funny bit that happens as you play. review_body:
I've been playing this game since last year (first on Google Play and now through Amazon app store) and this is a really cool game.
It's F2P but the developer usually gives you free jewels (the in-app currency) that you can use to buy the paid content without actually requiring to pay.
Also, you can practically get many of the top rewards by just playing without using jewels.
Now for the proper review:
Graphics:
The game has a nice design for the menu. The fonts are easilly readable and the general presentation of the map is done quite good.
But the best aspect are the artwork for the cards. The cards are extremely detailed and the use of colors and layouts is really good.
Sound:
There were a few musics on the game a year ago. However, Nubee increased the soundtrack, so you have several music according to where you are (your castle, the world map, etc).The soundtrack is really good overall.
Gameplay:
This is a very easy to learn game, but it becomes more complex as you play it.
The game is a combination of a map builder (a la Farmville) where you create building and create resources and a card game, where you form a deck of card to fight on the world map or against an opponent.
One of the best aspects of this game is that your deck doesn't lose power with time. Usually on card games as the time advance the power of a deck tends to be diminished as new cards are made more powerful.
On this game the attack and defense stats are kept constant which means that you can play with a deck and don't worry about losing battles.
Final words:
This is a very enjoyable game which has a really big userbase that plays the game constantly.

review_body:
First off I’ll explain the few things I don't like about the game. I think i made the same mistake other people have mentioned in their reviews. I started the game without linking it to facebook, and when you try and link it to facebook, you end up having to start over again. luckily i only made that mistake when i was at level 5. Annoying? yes. If that’s the worst thing that happens to me this year, I’m doing good. The game will also lag on the phone - although in the games defense I think it may be more about when trying to sync my progress to the cloud and has a bad signal on my phone. (I'm in a parking ramp which is a little sketchy on signal)

But otherwise I really enjoy the game. The candy crush and normal match 3 type games bore the heck out of me after just a few minutes. I like how you have a little more strategy to choose. Which characters to select? Do i make a bad combination this turn to clear out the items to set up a better combination on my next turn? Do I generate my shield, or launch another attack with my last turn? They're not huge mentally challenging decisions, but it's not just mindless matching three like those other games.

Last but not least, I can play this game for as long as I want and it appears I don’t need to spend a penny. Sure I did spend a few dollars to get more coins so I could quickly purchase one character, but otherwise I play it at least once a day, get my daily prize and fight my fights.

I'm glad the app exists, and I do use it, but it has severe problems.

1) Does not save your progress. If the app crashes or you lose network connectivity, you have to fast forward to where you were. This is pretty challenging since fast forward, at least in my setup, really doesn't show you video in pace.
2) Fast forward often crashes the app. In combination with problem #1, this stinks.
3) You must watch live events live. If I want to watch a 3-hour event, but I join an hour late, I can't start from the beginning.
4) Not enough "replay" events. For some reason, the app on my iPad has a much longer list of replay events available than the list on my FireTV.
5) Doesn't remember favorite sports. I have to page through a long list of sports I don't watch to get to the sports I always watch. Why?
6) My videos are MESSED UP. I don't know why, but the videos I've been watching from TSN are often missing large chunks (as much as 30 minutes) at the beginning or end of games. I've also had videos with defective audio--sometimes dead silence, sometimes certain channels absent or mixed down so low as to be barely audible.

It's better than nothing, but right now it's my least favorite way to watch sports.

review_body:
If I watched ESPN it might be worth the money, but otherwise it's a bunch of stuff I don't watch. HGTV, FOOD channel, CN, Disney (tv shows, not movies), TBS, and TNT. CNN is good, but it isn't worth $20 a month for CNN. TBS and TNT and American Family aren't bad, but most of the content is already available to me via Netflix, Prime, or Hulu+. On the PRO side, the picture quality was terrific and I never had any issues with buffering or stuttering of the video.

I'm currently getting all the shows we watch free OTA with a TABLO TV 4-Tuner DVR/Receiver, a cheap antenna and FireTV. I can watch the HGTV channel as an app, and HULU+/NETFLIX/PRIME provides me with all the other content. I'd be happy to pay a lower price for just news channels. I do miss having access to the cable news channels since I've been a cord-cutter. I would pay $8 a month for CNN, FOXnews, and maybe one other cable news channel, and Weather channel.

This is a good effort, I like where they are going with it, but give me more a la carte control over what I want vs a basic package with a bunch of stuff I don't want and then add-ons for news channels. Thanks, but no thanks. I can add basic cable to my Internet only subscription and get the news channels for about 8 dollars more than I pay for internet .

Think of the demo as a free trial; if you end up liking the game, buy it and play the whole thing. review_headline: Five Stars - Must have for all Readers and Book Worms.
review_body:
Love this app!
LOVE LOVE this app....

I have been using this app for several years now and I have had a terrific experience with it. To me it is like the "facebook" of the reading world - a place where I have been able to connect with authors, bloggers, other reviewers, readers, and fans. GoodReads allows me to write reviews, recommend books, find new reading materials, become friends with much respected authors and reviewers, and generally get a feel for any book I want to research and/or read. I have been able to easily locate every searched book, determine how it has been accepted by the reading community, and clearly understand if it is part of a series and where it belongs in that series. Often times when I have a question or issue with a book, I have been able to utilize this app to get my answers.

GoodReads is a great place for me to track my read books and still pending to be read books. I can track which books are more desirable for me to read and which are less by simply moving them on my to-read shelf in the order I want. It is also easy to remember and track those books which I have read. Often, young adults and kids approach me for a recommendation on a book to read and I can easily log into my account and look through the books I have read to give them suggestions.

Overall, this has been the single most valuable app I have download and used because I am an avid reader and like to know all things book related. Thank you GoodReads for being so awesome.

I installed the game "Paradise Island" in June 2014 on my Kindle Fire, because I was looking for a game similar to "Coconut Queen," that I play on my computer, and the game "Paradise Island" was suggested to me by an Amazon Kindle representative. I must have started to play it a little and then stopped for some reason, because I don't remember a Tutorial or experiencing any glitches as mentioned by some reviewers. Then, in the first week of January, when I noticed the icon picture of the game & wondered what it was, I was pleasantly surprised.  I began playing more often, and I started to build accommodations at once.  I have built on all the space of the 1st half of the island, and I am now on level 15 & that's where I will stay until I get 2300 more XP (experience points) to advance to the next level which will take forever to acquire.  I honestly enjoyed the game UNTIL I realized that the objective of the developers of the game (and Amazon) is to make you SPEND REAL MONEY on virtual reality.  < I DON'T LIKE THAT hence the rating of 2 stars.  Not only do you have to spend real money buying these "Piastres" in order to progress, but the game is slow-moving and takes hours to repair and upgrade buildings, and to accumulate enough game money, pearls, golden rings, and energy bars to accomplish the set tasks.  Someone said you could play it without spending any money at all, yes that maybe true, but it would take you SEVERAL MONTHS, EVEN YEARS to get enough money to buy more land i.e. those Regions, in order to make progress because the prices they set are ridiculous. Sadly, one day, I was so frustrated at waiting on the game to accumulate money to buy Regions, that I bought some Piastres. I got a deal that doubled my Piastres but still, that was not enough. I was about to get suckered a second time into buying a triple Piastres pack deal when I decided to do a search for the availability of this game for the PC, but the game is only available on Android devices and Apple products. My search led me to the developer's webpage, Game Insight, & they said the game was "free to play" & I laughed out loud.  In conclusion, if you game-players have a lot of real money to spend or several years to play a game, then by all means, Paradise Island is for you; but if not, I strongly recommend the game "Coconut Queen" which has the same theme & setting as "Paradise Island" but without the high costs and after your initial purchase of $19.99 will be truly "FREE TO PLAY."

review_headline: Not worth the money for this ripoff.
review_body:
I "bought" this via 99 free Amazon coins and I wish I could take it back. This game doesn't have anywhere near enough features to justify the cost. Since no one has bothered to talk about the gameplay, here it is:

The screen always pans north, and you, starting with the blue car shown in the screenshots, gain 1 point for every vehicle you pass. You lose 5 points for every duckling you squash. Trees regularly appear in all the grassy lanes. You can swipe up twice to accelerate and manage a total of 3 different speeds; you can swipe down to brake, which always brings you down to your vehicle's lowest speed, regardless of which of the two faster speeds you were previously at. You can move left and right on the road and the grass to avoid cars, ducklings, and trees, and to collect coins that are used to unlock more cars.

I suppose your car must be loaded with drugs or something because every now and then a police car will come from behind and chase you down and try to hit you; it can catch up to you if you're driving at anything other than the fastest speed. Coming into contact with anything other than ducklings and coins (so trees and other vehicles), as well as veering off to the right into the water or smashing into the railroad on the left, ends the round. If you slow down and move out of the way so that the police car is in front of you, it tries to block you by moving in front of you. This prevents you from earning any more score because you need to drive faster to discover new cars to overtake (all vehicles drive at the same speed as your slowest and middle speeds). If you're fast enough and have enough trees and cars to your advantage, you can deftly get around the police car. If you can make it smash into other cars or a tree, you get 25 points for the destruction.

It is very hard to unlock more vehicles. There are notably fewer playable vehicles than there are characters in Crossy Road (probably less than a quarter of Crossy's row in total), so it takes 200 coins to get a chance at unlocking a new vehicle.

The other reviewers are also correct: there is no landscape mode (but there is no reason to want that since the game pans vertically very fast and the entire screen is easily visible in portrait). The swiping response is a bit delayed, so it is tough to control the car. The game is more difficult than Crossy Road though it has fewer features; you're only driving on those same 7 lanes pictured (there are no bridges or anything else interesting). The car's hit-box is very large, unlike characters in Crossy Road, so it is easy to die, and the car shifts comparatively quite slowly from lane to lane—as opposed to Crossy Road characters who can hop fairly quickly. The game is very difficult and so far, for the few vehicles I've unlocked, there are no terrain or even sound effect differences for any of them. That's quite disappointing.

The physics of the game are also incorrect; some vehicles that you incapacitate in your own demise can be pushed by other vehicles after the round ends, and those vehicles that are supposed to be disabled can keep pushing forward on the lanes at basically the same speed as other functioning cars. That doesn't make any sense at all! And if you're wrecked on grass, dirt tracks keep actively flying from your car's wheels as if it was still driving (that might make sense if your car didn't EXPLODE in multiple fireballs each time to pitch-blackness). But I did like the fact that your vehicle visibly tilts when falling into the water on the right.

The coding for the police car behavior is pretty nice, and the train and the innovative Ferris wheel-like gift box are original and pretty enjoyable, but otherwise, this guy has stolen directly from what seems to be the duckling sprites or at least one definite exact sound effect from Crossy Road. review_headline: Does exactly what it's supposed to.
review_body:
It simply makes checklists of any kind. I keep lists of gift items as I encounter them, groceries, things to remember when shutting the house down for vacations, camping supplies, etc. This list allows you to enter a master list, then select only those you need (this time). Those not selected can either be hidden or pushed to the bottom of the list so that only the items you need are shown on the top of the list. You have simply to touch the item to hide it or push it to the bottom...a way of "checking off" each item as it's done!
It exports and imports these lists as ".CSV". You can archive, back up, or even modify the lists separately from the program.
Finally, the only permission is writing and reading USB. I assume that's related to the import and export function, but at least there's no unnecessary permissions, no ads, and no in-app purchases. It simply does what it says it does.
I gave it 4 stars instead of 5 because of one minor flaw: it forces you to use categories for each list. If your list is short or doesn't lend itself to categories, you have to open the list, then open the "category", then finally get to your list. If they made categories optional, it would be a solid 5 stars.

product_title: Minion Rush: Despicable Me Official Game
review_headline: where did the good game go?
review_body:
First off, thank you to anyone taking the time to read this review. It won't cost you any bananas, nor any tokens. Any reviews from before the game changed to the current level format should be deleted. They are not representative of what the game is now. Once the raves and awards started for this game, the developer$ got really greedy. Previously, if you didn't want to do one of the three goals, you could use tokens to bypass it. Now you have to earn at least one fruit in order to proceed to the next level AND perform all required actions in one run. Once you earn all the fruits you continue running and can get tokens. But only one at a time. Why not have an increase with each successive token found? Say the first found is one, the second is two tokens, the third is three tokens? If you don't acquire free revives ( which are much harder to come by since The Change) the token cost of the revives increases ridiculously. You can use power ups to help along the way, but few upgrades for the power ups are purchased with bananas. All the additional upgrades available after The Change can only be obtained by spending more and more tokens.
The daily and weekly challenges are fun. The prizes for those are now achievable for more participants. The token rewards are better depending on where you finish. HOWEVER, any prize that is bananas, whether an outright prize or from a prize pod, is an insult. Bananas are easily achieved so it's ridiculous to award them.
Also, having the booster prize pods to buy with all those millions of bananas (I'm surprised Donkey Kong hasn't shown up to get in on this banana action) you obtain was a great idea. Here's the but, why can't a player choose which booster to buy??? I got a boatload of, you guessed it, randomly awarded banana multipliers!!! Woo hoo, I guess. Why not have these booster prize pods available all the time? Oh right, that would cut down on players spending real money on fake tokens. Of course, with these boosters,the difficulty achieving the goal is increased. If you don't have the booster for that goal, eventually you are offered the booster, maybe, for a whopping 40 tokens. Really guys, how about 10 tokens, or 100,000 bananas?
I'm not keen on being forced to reach goals on predetermined locations either. Yes, you can only throw drones at Vector in Gru's lab, but the A V L is not the level of choice for rolling under obstacles. Sure, on the question mark levels you can re spin, yep you guessed again, for 5 tokens.
More tokens are rewarded than before, but more things cost more tokens.
Now, let's address the holiday mission joke. I got sucked into that along with thousands of other players. I can see having a time frame to complete the goals. The amounts of objects to gather started to get ridiculous. And the final rewards! I still have a red mark on my face from the slap the developer$ gave all of us players. Instead of creating a new character, the award was the snowboarder character that many players most likely had already. And 60 tokens. Yes, I will repeat. A lousy 60 tokens for the final goal, and a few boosters thrown in along the way. Did you break the crowbar trying to open your stash of rewards to give out??? Unfortunately these bozos are patting themselves on the back for hood winking trusting players. Should we refer to ourselves as fools from now on? I also contacted customer service on this issue, but did not receive an answer. One day, and one day only, the daily rewards showed snowboards for all ten days during the holiday mission. I thought that was a great idea. However, the next day, the daily rewards returned to, yes sir, bananas and tokens.
The game is mostly still fun to play, but is less so because of the greed that interferes with the game play.
I caution you on playing this game as it can turn into a money pit if you allow yourself. Even Candy Crush Saga now realizes the value of their players and how to keep them interestedin their game.

This is a boring program, and the app is even worse than the computer based program.

Imagine a game where you want the penguin to go from one side of the screen to the other. But nothing ever changes. He just walks across. There's no change in scenery. No plot. No purpose. The questions you're asked are repetitive and keep getting harder. You start at a level so low that it's inane and stupid. There's no way to tell the penguin that you're past using blocks and want to use numbers, or that you really have no issue with time-lines, no way for the teacher to tell the penguin that these are areas you need work on and these are areas you've mastered. No, you have to plod through every boring thing you've mastered. There is no reward. No finish line since most kids don't finish it in the year.

Now imagine putting it on a tablet where making sure you hit the right number is difficult. You can't zoom in to make sure you hit the right number. This was a bad program, and even worse adaptation on the tablet. After my daughter hit the wrong number several times with one of the number charts, she was ready to give up.

The actual program I'd say is about a 2-3 star program. It does get the job done for some kids. Not all, but some. But the adaptation to tablets? Awful.

review_headline: For those looking to use the Prime Instant Video app
review_body:
I'm copying and pasting my review of the Prime Instant Video app over here for those looking for help:
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
I've gotten this to work perfectly fine - even if its UI is clunky and the whole thing is very slow - on my Samsung Galaxy Tab 2 and my daughter's Acer whatever-it-is 7" tablet. Thing is, you have to start with the Amazon store app for phones - NOT the one for tablets - the immaculate genius of Amazon's tech will not allow the Prime video app to work with the version for tablets. Follow these simple steps:

1. Install Amazon Store app - regular Android version for phones
2. Once installed, try to watch a prime video, then follow the link to install the Prime Instant Video app.

Once these two apps are aware of each other, everything should work fine. Now, of course it's nonsense that one MUST have the Amazon store app installed in order to run the prime video app, but such is the decree of the Amazon gods.

I give Amazon 5 stars for finally putting this thing out, 1 star for their wonky implementation, and the actual app itself gets 4. It's not as user friendly as Netflix and it's deathly slow to load at times, but overall it actually works.

review_headline: OneNote beats Evernote in my book
review_body:
OneNote does a nice job organizing my bits of information. I tried Evernote, but I found it less structured. If you'd rather just dump notes into an app, and rely on searching to find your data, Evernote may work better for you. The OneNote structure of Notebooks, Folders, and Pages allows you to have a coherent structure to find things fast, and yet still allows you to just search the entire app if you wish.
I will recommend that you have OneNote for your laptop (or desktop) if you have it on phone. Things like moving pages and changing that structure are harder to do on the phone. I mostly set up my notes on my laptop, and then reference or add info via my phone.

review_headline: Good Grief - Outstanding Mixed with Dross
review_body:
**While shooting my Free App of the Day video for my YouTube channel, I was demonstrating the page selection screen. Sprinkled through this selection are little scenes marked as \\"Free\\" - I tapped on one of them, and it took me right to the IAP store. No lock, not even the bare bones one from the main menu. And no explanation on how that particular scene I tapped on was \\"free\\" in a $5 dollar activity... just a listing of all the IAP packs. I am even more disappointed now than I was before.**

Well, I downloaded the app on a new 2014 model, 10.1\\" Quad-Core 4x1.24ghz, 1gig Ram 1800x600 HD (IPS) tablet running KitKat 4.4.2 with an stripped down Running Process listing - I make mention of this because it crashed out 1/3rd of the way through the story. This is not a good thing...

And as for the IAP - well, as many as you may know, I tend to be slightly more lenient on such things than others, even in a premium app, as well as not often taking account of regular pricing of a Free App showcase... but it is rather ridiculous. They only offer Christmas Tree ornaments for tree decoration. That's it. Not more stories or mini-games... trees and tree ornaments. Uh, okay. And there is a LOT of them. You'd think for the already hefty price this app normally commands, any additional IAP would be some serious content. Then add in the fact this is indeed a primary target of young children and children with a mere slide-lock as the \\"Store\\" safety feature. Good Grief!

So aside from the crashing on a powerful tablet and the head-hanging IAP, the rest of the permissions and code are clean. You can take pictures from with the app, thus that Camera permission, and the code is clean from any kind of analytics. Does contain Facebook and Twitter code just in case your six year old wants to post his real life tree. Yo yo yo, check out Little Johnny's Christmas Bling!

The app itself is extremely polished - a sheer delight to the eyes and possibly the best, hands down, read-along app I have ever seen. Just an awful, ugly shame it had to have IAP (and a lot of it) for fluffy content, and the irregular crashing.

I want to say grab it, in spite of the IAP, because as long as you are aware of it, you can ensure the tablet is Offline and/or Parental Lock is on the Amazon Appstore In-App Purchasing. The presentation is just that supreme. Yet that crashing - I just don't have the heart to recommend something that may make a young child upset that something \\"broke\\".

review_headline: Evil!! (In a good way)- Something for Everyone. Just Try It!
review_body:
I'm gonna gush about this game, which I never do. The day I downloaded it, I was up all night playing. It's probably the most addictive app I've come across. I love trivia games, but the last one I played had limited categories: A separate one for every sport known to man, but often single categories for other subjects. Not so here; There are five or six hundred subtopics under various categories like Lifestyle, Literature, Art, etc. (14 of those.) And new topics and questions are added frequently. (Some are submitted by players.) So far, I've encountered very few repeat questions. Topics vary from broad things like, say, Math, to very narrow things like specific books: The Hunger Games, Harry Potter, and such. So everyone will have topics they rock in and others that are super tough. You end up learning a lot. I'm not sure of the level cap for subjects, but I've seen people with 100+ !

You're matched up with someone else playing in a topic and compete. Games are short (7 questions), so you can easily play for just a few minutes (if you can tear yourself away!)

QuizUp has a ton of achievements available. Some of them are quite strange; They require a combination of (usually unrelated) categories to unlock. For example, one requires levels in both Star Wars and Star Trek categories. Most achievements come with fun titles, and you can choose among all that you've earned for one to display. You can also earn special badges for being a high-scorer in your state, country, or even the world.

The game is very stable and seems to have many players. I've never had to wait more than a few seconds for a match, regardless of time of day or subject. And you'll see players from all over the world. (Playing people from various countries is an achievement. I'm at about 50 now. )

QuizUp truly offers something for everyone. It's ridiculously addictive. It's satisfying to achieve goals. And it's just really fun! And free! I'd willingly pay for it, so that's impressive. Try it. Unless you just hate trivia games, I can almost guarantee you'll enjoy it a lot.or it, so that's impressive. Try it. Unless you just hate trivia games, I can almost guarantee you'll enjoy it a lot.

review_headline: Streamlined Mobile GUI of SONGSTERR's Website - OFFLINE Use IS Available - Inherent Limitations Yet Still Well Done
review_body:
ONLINE VERSUS OFFLINE
SONGSTERR does require Internet Access in order to primarily run.. and I pretty much fully expected that when I saw how small the download/install was, only 12mbs. So this acting as a rather nice GUI front end of the website, this is a very cool app.

Now according to the SONGSTERR description of their app, there is an OFFLINE method - and here it is as best as I can work it. Establish a connection, go into the app, find the stuff you want to view, and once they are loaded in, you can mark them as a favorite - later, when OFFLINE, you can enter the app offline and navigate your already viewed history or favorites OFFLINE, anything you already tapped into is saved to a specific app CACHE, upwards of 500mbs worth, and thus BLAMMO- Offline viewing. And the individual files themselves aren't that big.. the handful I marked came out to be 9mbs. So that's a lot of offline material.

And I do have to say, this app actually is far better than using the website's rather heavy-handed use of various add-on scripting, especially on mobile devices. In fact, I would go far as to say this is fundamentally a Mobile Version of SONGSTERR's Premium Member presentation. Everything works smoothly, really smoothly, on my Samsung Tab 3 10.1\\" screen - I purposely downloaded it to my largest screen tablet to get the largest viewing area possible.

And here comes in the formatting bits I would improve / change:

I can switch from the tablature to guitar chords, but I can't adjust the text size (neither settings nor zoom) nor put it in portrait mode to get as much as possible on the screen at once. Having to constantly swipe up to scroll kind is a bit BLEAH.

**UPDATE: I just stumbled across an auto-scroll feature for the chords... well, that fixes the main issue I had. LOL I kicked in the extra, 5th star. I can even adjust scroll speed. :) **

PERMISSIONS & CODE
Now taking into account that this indeed is primarily a very mobile friendly version of the full-blown website, and thus also allowing SONGSTERR account holders to sign in to access their account favorites and such, nothing is amiss in the permissions whatsoever. Not even the Cloud to Device Messaging, which will alert you to \\"Just Added Tabs\\" as well synching your SONGSTERR account via PCs, and other remote account notifications.

(ACCOUNT IS NOT REQUIRED)
You do NOT need an account with SONGSTERR to use this app. It's just an option, such as uploading tabs, synching PC/Other Mobile Device accounts, that sort of thing. And account creation in itself is technically free, whether on a PC or here.

As for code, it does contain a couple analytics, Google Analytics and Mixpanel, and of course if you do sign in with a SONGSTERR account, identifiable tracking will ensue. Yet, this is no different from the actual website. Without a SONGSTER account, the analytics a pretty much limited to anonymous feedback to the devs. Beyond that (and the Cloud2Device code module), the coding is just fine.

THE INHERENT UNDERSTANDING OF WHAT THIS APP IS
Here is the real deal: SONGSTERR has a \\"premium\\" membership on their website that removes advertising and such... and that is what this app basically is, a PREMIUM edition of their resources. Actually registering an account itself is technically \\"free\\", you just get an ad-free, \\"support the SONGSTERR folks\\" front end on your mobile device.

And as a mobile version of the website itself, this is very nicely done indeed. Trying to navigate the website on a poor WiFi connection or a less-than-speedy mobile browser is a major hassle - this app ready does streamline it into a easy format. In fact, the entire time I was poking about in the app, I only had 2 bars for WiFi, and everything still loaded in very quick. Plus, the website is filled with ads and all that - this premium version does away with all of that.

CATAGORY LIMITATION - ONLY \\"POPULAR\\" (NO TAB LEVEL SEPERATION)
There is an interface limitation: it currently has POPULAR as the only category, which really ought to be expanded into included tablature levels (Beginner, Intermediate, Advanced), but since I can still search the database, it's more of a GUI convenience than functionality hit... well, unless you really want only a certain level of tablature. In that case, what you will want to do is access the website, pick your songs while logged in, then synch the songs to your mobile device.

TO BUY OR NOT TO BUY
Finally, as trying to decide in purchasing this when it is not a Free App showcase? I recommend you go to the SONGSTERR website, poke about, see how you like the general feel - and if you dig it, then this mobile version will certainly give you value on your mobile device.

They didn't rinse and repeat 3 but they did change some aspects that were good in the third zombie assault.

Pros:
Better detail put into zombies
New zombie types
Decent length missions
New mission types
Skill tree with A LOT of skills

Cons:
No more private lobbies
Can't buy weapons
Strongboxes are the only way of getting items
Restricted to being only capable of carrying 3 weapons instead of 6 from sas 3 or all of them from 1+2
Very hard enemies even when a low level

This game took what made the others great and just scrapped them and tried to take a new approach which isn't always the best. Multiplayer is still fun but it just isn't as good if you can't play with your friends but we have to make an attempt to get into the same lobby to play which is completely irritating.

Final verdict: 6/10

You should give this game a go if you enjoy the series like I do, but don't expect it to be sunshine and rainbows all the way through.

review_headline: We Love Our Prime Membership & Instant Video
review_body:
My husband and I decided to get rid of cable tv about three years ago. It was a HUGE montly expense (in relation to the product provided at least), and we had medical bills to pay down. We began to use our laptop as our tv and streamed videos from a few different sources online instead for our entertainment. We found out that without the cable tv around we became happier, more productive, and a bit more creative in our thinking to oddly enough. Freeing ourselves from so many darn commercials alone was AMAZING!!

After flirting with the idea of getting Amazon Prime membership for about a year we realized that it would be a great cost savings with all the perks it offered. With Amazon instant video in particular we are able to stream most shows/movies that we would like to watch for free with our membership. The cost of Amazon Prime in its entirety for a FULL year (with music, videos, shipping, etc) is equal to ONE MONTH with the cable company!!!! Seriously! We found that Amazon Prime Instant Video offers us just as many videos to stream roughly as we get with Netflix, but we get more varied perks with the other areas of Prime membership benefits.

Ergo, we are totally hooked on our Amazon Prime & its instant free videos! It was a great choice for our family to sign up. Do the math yourself and consider checking into it...

review_headline: A random Tap,tap tap search game: Illogical and frustrating
review_body: Played on Kindle HDX 8.9. No HO scenes. Minimal puzzles. Gave it 2 stars because graphics are comparable to other escape games. You are required to do object placements to escape various levels. Game play starts out pretty basic and is almost too easy. But as levels open, it gets trickier. Just as I was beginning to think the game could be good, actions required started getting too random! It didn't require logic or deduction in the thought process but rather just tap,tap,tap and see what happens. Objects don't always combine in realistic ways. To get a hook to use somewhere else, you brought a random pillar to that hook and it smashed the pillar, then you got the hook. Objects in your inventory had to be combined in strange ways to form more usable objects- like combining a rock with a glass lens to make a rock usable... huh? Clicking on objects didn't always show you that object. I clicked a pillar and got the desk!  Relationships between codes and puzzles are often illogical. For example,  colors on cats were supposed unlock a box puzzle, but it was impossible to see the corresponding relationship.  I watched a walkthrough 3 times once to see how the player arrived at a solution and still thought how? All in all, it got too frustrating to be enjoyable and I deleted it. The Can You Escape series is of the same graphic and play design of this game but far more enjoyable.

Tracing letters is a great way for children to learn to write their letters, while tracing with their fingers.  I know how it is important for children to learn to spell.  The first words game allows children to duplicate the words that are seen on the left side of the screen.  There is also a game called coloring book.  I think our favorite game aside form the pumpkin maker was the memory game.  With a Halloween twist this is a fun way for children to learn.  Yes, the game can be downloaded for free, but after playing each game a few times you are given the option to purchase the full version.

review_body:
feel I must emphasize, in spite of all the rather silly assertions to the contrary, there is ZERO issues with the Permissions OR Code concerns in THIS game. Rovio does have a well deserved ill-repute, practices I have attacked without restraint, but I take game offerings as they are, and TINY THIEF is relatively clean (more on this later).

It's been a year since this game by ROVIO STARS, a sub-publication adjunct to ROVIO, has been out, and no "scary stuff" has been added, so I personally take that as an indicator that there won't ever be. In fact, I'd go as far to say that ROVIO STARS is almost a completely different animal... a five star past time. I frankly enjoyed it myself. :)

My impression is a kid-friendly Espionage Style game, like the METAL GEAR franchise and all the other sneak/hide style of games made popular on game consoles. The first five levels are tutorials of sorts, getting you used to the mechanics, and then it begins to slowly ramp up in difficulty once you get into the chapters proper. Sneak about, time your approaches and hiding spots not to get caught, manipulating various objects to steal from the rich to give to the poor. There is even "hidden object" subtheme as you try to find the bonus objectives: your pet ferret who pops his head and a hidden object for your treasure chest. It's all very well done with pleasant 2D graphics and sound effects.

Yes, the game itself isn't fast paced, but once again, the Espionage genre isn't fast paced (have you ever spent 20 minutes with Solid Snake trying to get past the guards? lol).

CLEAN PERMISSIONS AND CODE (Ignore the other Ignorant Rants to the Contrary)
Minimal Permissions, only Network Access, with Flurry Analytics, which is restricted to anonymous data reporting in app performance, but zero other issues. Nada. The game does run OFFLINE, and although I grimace at the social links tucked unobtrusively (YouTube, Twitter, Facebook), I give it a pass for two reasons: this is more of a pre-teen and older game, so social media isn't a hit as it would be for games for ages 8 and under, and it does play offline without a problem, obviating any parental issues if it comes to that. Of course, however, your own judgment is paramount. There are NO pushes, NO popup ads, NO In-App Purchases, and the one other external link (under the pause menu) is one to Rovio Stars' Webpage (not Rovio itself).

Installed at 57.92mbs with an option to move it to my SD Card. Game does exit cleanly with the back-key prompting a Quit popup.

review_headline: We are Android tab owners.  We are legion.  Freakin' learn to deal with it already!
review_body:
Hmmm... I'm thinking the Disgruntled Prime Member font will do nicely for tonight's rant...

Having been a Prime member for over 8 years now, it would be nice to be able to enjoy the increased perks that have been made available over the past few years to members...well...providing they aren't among the lowly android tablet users. Well, I just wanted to let you know that I'm typing this on the Samsung Galaxy S3 I PURCHASED FROM AMAZON. The same tablet I used to place yet another order utilizing your app for tablets earlier today. The same tablet I will use to renew my Prime membership this Spring, should I so choose to do so now that the price has increased considerably for perks I can't make use of besides shipping. This year, as I carefully weigh what I'm getting for what I'm spending, Prime Instant Video could very well be the deal breaker for me. Continuing to pay for a cheap streaming site or two, and a couple of extra days wait for a package certainly won't kill me. In fact, it'll probably help me cut back even farther, particularly now that you'll be local and charging taxes and using shady delivery services like LaserShip more often...

Fascinating how Amazon directs its nerd pool to deliver fully functioning $tore apps and updates, but can't manage to deliver to its paying membership what it promises. The nerds certainly aren't to blame here. At this point in time, why should which device I prefer to use to access Amazon sway what services are provided, particularly when they have no issue with selling said device? It's not like android devices started falling from the sky a month ago. If you get to choose to limit who gets to access a service they've paid for, then Amazon needs to offer a subPrime membership account for shipping only at a substantial discount for the rest of us; or go à la carte with what it will grant access to in lieu of the obviously impossible task of commisioning functional apps. This sorry effort is not only well over a year too late, it's an embarassment.

product_title: Hidden Objects Secret Forest & 3 puzzle games
review_headline: I hate trying to find objects in the dark with only ...
review_body:
I have purchased about a half dozen hidden objects games from this company. They all follow the same formula. You have to find objects using 4 different methods: visual, silhouette, description, and in the dark. I hate trying to find objects in the dark with only a small circle of light, but I like the other formats. In the other formats, I can zoom in on the screen to have a closer look. It is helpful since some of the objects are small and hard to find.
There are three mini puzzles in each game and they are different most of the time. the only puzzle I hate is Sudoku. I can't seem to get to first base with this math oriented puzzle. The other puzzles are memory matching, hangman, picture jigsaw, and my favorite where I move around ships to try and clear a path for the sailing ship to get through. It is the most challenging one besides Sudoku.

My only complaint is the games are too repetitious. The objects to find and the format, tends to be the same in each game. All in all, an enjoyable game.
