review_headline: Tools work great but loses files
review_body:
The app works great for reading and annotating PDFs. I have a Samsung Galaxy Note 10.1, and I'm finding it fairly intuitive to use the tools to mark up PDFs with the stylus. But there is a bug or some other problem that has caused me a big headache. Twice, my marked-up document has disappeared from storage, causing me to have to redo hours' worth of work. This happened with two different documents. I carefully saved after each change I made, and I made note of the file name and location, but the next day, in each case, the file was completely gone. I searched through my entire file system and did not find it, and the storage location itself (PDFMax folder on the internal storage card) had been wiped.

Until I find an alternative app, I am saving to my Dropbox account, which is slower and very clunky, and apparently has not saved the changes I re-made after losing the original file. I really need an app that will reliably save changes and not delete files. I thought this was it. It is not. Too bad, because other than that big deal-breaker, it works very well.

I have never seen  anything so awful as this tactic for artifically raising the number of games downloaded.    I am not a fan of reviews of apps that people have never played... yet this is a unique situation. There is no possible hardware problem; this issue DEFINITELY lies with the app itself.  I open this game...it is new, was free so I expect ads and stuff but that's ok, it looks fun, I haven't played it yet. Well I open it and I get a pop-up screen which I will quote directly for everyone's edification:  FREE COINS If you enjoy \\"What's the Saying?\\", you'll love \\"What's the Difference?!\\" [punctuation theirs].  Download it for free now and we'll give you a bonus 1,000 coins to use in \\"What's the Saying?\\".  Then there is a big green button that reads OK.    Ok me again. I don't KNOW if I enjoy \\"What's the Saying?\\" because I have never played it. I can see the ghost of the main page but there is literally NO POSSIBLE WAY to advance without pushing that big green OK button and literally be FORCED to download this other second game... I think it is despicable.  I never imagined that I would do as others I have seen, announcing that I have deleted this game without playing it.  Again I think this case is exceptionally awful and .. well I hate when people say they do things on principle ;)  - I know the game designers aren't going to see this and say \\"Oh no we lost a customer *on principle*!\\" I would really like to play this game, but this shilling is the WORST EVER tactic I have seen to drum up the number of downloaded copies. I will not add my one single voice to that horribly, misleadingly large number of downloads made SOLELY to play the game in the first place.  I wish there was some kind of app-world version of the Better Business Bureau because this developer should be on the list. Unfortunately the best I can do is to write what I have here. I am considering contacting the developers directly.  Dreadful dreadful despicable despicable. Yuck. Never seen anythingso awful as this tactic for artificially inflating the number of games sold.    -Edited to fix minor punctuation issues.

review_headline: Great app, my 4-yr-old is learning from this.
review_body:
I have the paid version of this, and I don't know the limitations of the free version. But here is my review of the paid version:

My 4-year old son LOVES this app. It shows how to trace through letters and numbers and then asks the user to try it freehand. it also has the ability to capture a photo of the attempt so you can document your child's development or hang onto them just for fun. I am teaching my son how to draw letters and numbers and showed him how to use this app. Over the past few days he has surprised me by walking up and showing me letters he has drawn freehand. And thank goodness it does not say "Zed" for the letter Z as many of these apps do.

I'm not sure why it needs to read phone identity or network access, but if you are worried about privacy invasions with this or any other app you should have a firewall installed. Rooted is best (Android Firewall or AFWall+) but not rooted works too (Mobiwol or NoRoot Firewall). In fact, if a young child is using a tablet I strongly recommend one of those "kid safe" launchers. The one I settled on was Kids Place by kiddoware, but there is another good one called Play Safe by Play Safe Labs. There are probably some other good ones I don't know about.

review_headline: There and back again, a hobbit's journey into bad customer service
review_body:
Kabam's customer service is amazingly bad. They need to take some lessons from Amazon on how to provide customer service. I've had to open multiple tickets to Kabam for items, troops, and resources going missing in game. I get a mixed bag of responses from them, with one of the comments being, "This is the first time we've seen this and will escalate this internally." Then they closed the ticket.

Our most recent experience has been with the release of 11.0 on the Kindle. They wiped out all of our characters and we can only see three game worlds. Going to their forums has proven to be a waste of time and effort. It should be rather easy to send an in game message to all kindle users in those three worlds with an update of some kind, but alas, we are to sit in the dark wondering what is going to happen.

Thankfully, Amazon's customer service has been fantastic and I've received refunds on my in-app purchases and I will not be playing this game anymore. In my opinion, Kabam is going to consistently lose paying customers and will most likely act surprised about it to their own venture capitalist when their bottom line continues to dwindle down.

review_headline: Great game! But is it worth it?
review_body:
This is an addictive game, for sure. You collect "units" and level them up in order to get stronger and eventually evolve them. I guarantee this app is loosely inspired from Pokemon video games. Not only do you have multiple areas and maps to travel through, but everyday there are different dungeons and special events in which to participate. It's apparent the makers of this app are always at work and making sure there is something new for their players.
There are a few reasons I'm not giving this app a 5 star rating. One, because the app will unexpectedly crash, although (thankfully) it seems to wait to crash until you've finished what you started. Two, the newest update included the right to record audio. This bothers me. I mean, why would a game want to have the ability to record audio from my device whenever it wants? There are no speech functions to this game, so I can only speculate this to be an invasion of privacy. In fact, I've been so doubtful of this that I've been considering of deleting this app entirely.
Overall, this is a fun game! But I'm not sure I'm comfortable knowing someone could be listening in on my life.

review_headline: Nice checklist app. But too spastic.
review_body:
What this dev has decided to to is take a really nice and we'll developed checklist app and sell it for different needs under different names. This app is very capable of being a checklist for ANYTHING you want, not just camping. You can create a new list titled whatever you choose and enter in your own information. It's titled camping checklist because the starter template he has added is camping related.

The dev does have a checklist app they sell for $2.50 which I assume has different lists pre-made instead of just one like this app.

What's obnoxious is taking a perfectly good checklist app and breaking it up into slices based on the template you include. Camping checklist should just be called "checklist" and include all the templates (or if you want to charge more than 99c include none, instead charge IAP for each list or have a pro version).

It's perfectly plausible you use this app as a shopping checklist, which is another app this dev sells and is the exact same app but with a different start template. Because the app allows you to create your own template, it can be whatever you want. Again, this is what I find obnoxious, why should I need a separate app based on the start template; sell me one app that does it all instead of chopping it up into pieces based on pre-made list types like you have done.

review_headline: Grab A Rifle, We're Going Fishing.
review_body:
Played on a Samsung Galaxy Nexus i9250

A simple enough sounding game, Ridiculous Fishing is actually a pretty straight forward, very accessible game of fishing. The idea is simple; drop the hook into the water and (depending on the type of hook you've chosen) and tilt your device to move the hook left and right to avoid touching anything, the object here is to get the hook as deep into the water as possible. Once it's gone as far as it can go, or if you happen to hook something, the whole thing goes into reverse and you have to tilt left and right to catch fish instead of avoiding them! Once you have them at the surface of the water they go soaring into the air, again affected by power ups, and you touch tap, or glide a finger over the flying fish to blow them out of the sky with various types of weapons like shotguns and machine guns.

This game is a real surprise for me, I really didn't think I'd have this much fun. The tilt controls take a little getting used to, but were tight and responsive on my now aging device. This game never stuttered or felt like it has hanging for any reason, and it was challenging but never unfairly so. Unlock-able power-ups really change things up and keep the game even more interesting with each play-through.

Visually this is a 16bit era throwback with a lot of bright colorful charm. A lot of variety in items you can purchase (not with real money but with money earned by blowing fish out of the sky), plenty of colorful areas to visit via a selectable map, with different fish available to collect (the fish you catch appear in a collection book accessible in game).

My only gripe, and why I didn't give this fantastic game a five star rating was the sound options were oddly designed. There is a volume slider for sound only, but not for music. In fact the music option is totally non-existent. When you play the music plays as your hook sinks deep into the water, then once you catch something and the hook reverses course, the music does the same and starts playing backward. It's a novel approach, but after a while the music becomes annoying and I kind of just want to turn it down or off. The sound effects are fine, and they have a slider, but the music will play no matter what you do. A strange design choice.

review_headline: This is the app for anyone who has experienced "sticker aftershock".
review_body:
This morning, my 3 year old downloaded a $2.99 game without our knowledge...until I got an email thanking me for the order. When I checked my parental controls in the Amazon App Store, I found that they only cover IN-APP PURCHASES, and that there is nothing for actual app purchases. After looking for hours for some sort of parental control that covers app purchases within said app store, I tried logging out of Amazon. This led to all Amazon-downloaded apps not working. I sent in feedback to Amazon, since Apple has a means to keep unauthorized purchases from being made. That said, I did more searching and found this app. After downloading it and putting it on my husband's phone (where the offending purchase was made), I played around with it, and found that it turns the device into a benign, kid-friendly handheld that requires a PIN (or a hard restart of the device, though it can be set to start Kids Place UI upon turning on the device) to get to the original interface. You can choose which apps are available through the Kids Place UI, as well.

There are also in-app purchases that can be made from the menu (after entering in your PIN, of course), such as a kid-friendly browser, a kid-friendly video player, a child-lock program that is for multiple users, and a program to mete out how long the system or certain apps can be used for. All are varying prices, but all the prices are reasonable.

This is more than I was looking for from Amazon, who failed to provide a means in which kids can play on their parents' Android devices [where Amazon App Store is the most oft-used download site]. Kiddoware saved the day, and they did it at no charge, with no ads. I just wish I could give it more than 5 stars!

review_headline: You may not remember how you got on with life before it.
review_body:
This is one of the best programs out there. It is simple and reliable, it is what I want.
Evernote allows you to store notes, pictures, and audio recordings in a cloud-like environment accessible from anywhere on most devices with a connection to the internet. It might do more but realistically this is all i use it for.

And it excels at it.

Primarily I use it to store lyrics. Other lyricists can attest to this: You will inevitably think of some cool line at the most inconvenient of times and it is very important (perhaps to none but you) that the line get written down or recorded as soon as possible. Previous methods of walking around with a notepad in my back pocket proved useless, for one I didn't ALWAYS have it (i don't always have my kindle but I do almost always have my phone which has evernote as well). Also, if your phone explodes in a fire, provided that the last sync is up to date (and the program syncs often) you will loose no data. The ability to record audio is very useful as for my purposes I may also not only want to remember the lyric but also the melody.

I'm not quite sure if it shares well with other users, I may have tried it once but it may not have been super easy or obvious and I didn't have the motivation to look into it. Regardless, this program seems geared toward a single user anyway and that is how i use it; any music/lyrics/etc.I do with a group seems best managed (as of now) by drop box.

review_headline: No challenge, but great new features.
review_body:
This game has great potential to surpass it's older brother with awesome new features, but it fails to do so with ridiculously easy missions. It's almost embarrassing how simple the missions are.

Cons:
- When you can beat a high level mission in 3 turns with no challenge, you can't help but ask "where's the beef?"
- The AI is stupid... I mean, dunce-cap wearing, stuck in the classroom corner, stupid. For example, the enemy will ignore your troops and only target worthless buildings as you advance across the map, and it seems to be preprogrammed to over-recruit Bazooka troops (even if you have NO vehicles on the map!)
- There's no difficulty setting in the game... it only has one level: SUPER EASY
- As others have noted, many maps are just too small!
- I LOVE the new feature of unlocking and upgrading troops, but with how easy this game is, I quickly stopped upgrading anything because it was already too easy. Making my troops/vehicles stronger would only add to the problem.
- There's no "reward" for completing all 60 missions. I was really hoping that it would unlock a harder level (expert mode or something), but no such luck. I went back and tinkered with earlier missions, upgraded everything, but still no change in the super easy level setting.

Pros:

- New features are awesome! As a fan of the earlier Great Little War Game, I loved the splash damage, new units, upgrading features, etc...
- Quick turn starts. I was always annoyed at the earlier version's slow start time as it ka-chinged through each and every oil rig. This version has a simultaneous money payout that greatly speeds things up.
- Great graphics, good humor, and overall an "eye candy" little war game.

Summary:

To the developers: PLEASE send out an upgrade to this game, adding in some difficulty/challenge! Please! The ealier game had some challenge to beating thosemissions, involving real planning and strategy and tactics. If you can add some meat to this version, you'll have a LOT of happy campers.

To potential buyers: If you're looking for a challenge, buy the older version of this game. I just can't recommend this one until the concept of "cake walk" is removed from the gameplay. If you already own and loved the earlier version of this game?... You'll love the new features, but will hate the insultingly easy missions.

review_headline: From a Crazy Woman Teaching Herself Chinese
review_body:
I have downloaded several Chinese learning apps, and though none of them are perfect, this one has a variety of tools to assist in various aspects of learning the language, including speech recognition, word usage, and character writing. One frustration with this and every character writing application is that the character practice is in a more decorative style (somewhat like calligraphy, with little flourishes, etc.), while the text is all in a block style. For someone like me, who is kind of "literal" in her visual interpretation, this requires learning two images as the characters, especially with some of the mouth radicals.

This app doesn't teach everything, but is great for various types of practice that make learning the language and assimilating it easier for the student. I did find HSK flashcard apps on Amazon that have the same block-style characters, and it has helped greatly with my word recognition.

review_headline: This could potentially be useful, but happens to be much slower that just ...
review_body: I will say that it totally worked as advertised,  Unfortunately, I was really looking for a simple interface to transfer files between my PC and my Kindle, and this software does not do that.  What this does is allow your supported tablet to act as the display and keyboard for your PC, allowing you to run software and view files that are hosted on your PC, but displaying the output on your tablet.  Its as simple as that.  The tablet is not actually receiving and using the PC's files and programs, it is just displaying what the PC would be displaying.  This could potentially be useful, but happens to be much slower that just working on the PC.  Also as other comments have noted, there are some security risks if used over the internet.

Not enough good things can be said about Plex, in my opinion. I have been using it for about two and a half years now, and wow, what an incredible service! When paired with a streaming device, such as a Roku or Kindle Fire TV or Tablet, this service is incredible.

Plex has been instrumental in helping me to "cut the cord" with my cable companies, something that I did a good three and a half years or so ago. With it, I am able to stream videos, music, and photos from my computer to my tablet, phone, and streaming boxes, and it works fantastically. Each and every new update to Plex simply seems to increase its usability and stability, with no bloat to speak of.

Now, in my opinion, this is where Plex really shines. Plex has a number of extremely useful "Channels", which you can add for free. For instance, when Netflix dropped all of their Nickelodeon shows, my children were devastated... until Plex came to the rescue, allowing me to continue to stream episodes and clips of all of their favorite shows. Also? History Channel, Comedy Central, CBS, Disney Channel, and the Food Network, just to name a few of the other channels I now have at my fingertips once more.

It also works cross-platform flawlessly. I have used it to enjoy shows in Google Chrome while at work and on the go.

All in all, Plex is THE media streaming service to get, and the price point is incredible... especially since you can get started right away for free. I absolutely recommend Plex to anyone with a tablet, smartphone, laptop, computer, or streaming box. You simply cannot go wrong with it!

This app is an excellent implementation of the board game Suburbia and I will be reviewing how it works as a digital edition. If you want to find out more about the game itself, I would suggest reading up on reviews of the board game elsewhere on Amazon. Keep in mind though, this app is great and could be in an inexpensive way for you to try out the game.

Bottom line, if you are a Suburbia fan, this is very close to perfection and excels in allowing you play anywhere without fuss or setup. The gameplay fits the medium perfectly. A few taps get you in a game and then you simply drag tiles to your board with your fingers or stylus. That's it! All the bookkeeping and scoring is done automatically, and you are even able to compare options before placing a tile. Your play can be as quick or as deep as you want it to be. As a bonus, this app even implements a challenging single player \\"puzzle\\" campaign in addition to traditional play against different AI. This adds value to solo play.

There are a couple issues I noticed that prevent this from being a 5 star app, if only because there are a few other companies that have set the bar high in terms of translating board games into apps.

-No online multiplayer. You do have local pass and play, but you can also get this from the board game itself so there is a missed opportunity here.

-No expansions offered at the time of this writing. (except for the Essen tiles which are a reward for completing the single player puzzles)

-Goals for the single player puzzle levels can sometimes be unclear. It took me a while to figure out what the game meant by \\"connect all tiles\\" in some situations.

-No quick restart of games. If I am playing a puzzle level and I realize I have no chance of winning, I have to exit the game back to the menu before I can restart.

-Also when playing against the AI, personally I wish I could slow down, pause or replay their turn, just so I could analyze and compare their moves better.

-Finally, the app displays a ton of information about gameplay and your stats and other players stats. Information that is not easily available when playing the board game. It took me a while to figure out the iconography and how to best read the info.

Despite these observations this app delivers a solid experience of Suburbia on your Kindle and is definitely worth the price. :-)er. -Finally, the app displays a ton of information about gameplay and your stats and other players stats. product_title: Inference Ace: Reading Comprehension Skills & Practice For Kids Who Need Help to Become Stronger Readers
review_body:
My seven year old wanted to share her review on this app:
You have to pick the correct words when it asks you a question. It’s really fun and kind of easy. If you don’t know the answer to the problem there is a question mark which will give you a hint.

My review as the parent:
My daughter sat for two hours straight playing the game Inference Ace. She is in first grade and her reading skills are at grade level. Her favorite aspect of the app was answering the questions. I asked her why? She told me because I like earning coins to buy clothes, different faces, shoes and hats when I have enough coins. That explained everything to me. My child Allison is one that works well with a reward system and it motivates her to keep going.

Reward’s is a fun place to visit. You can spend coins which are earned by a child from answering questions correctly and then buy prizes to enhance the main character. If you haven’t played the game long enough the store will not open. It will let your child know that more play is needed in order to open it.

It was awesome that she could work the app program herself. We played the game together. I loved the questions and how there were four choices to use to find the correct answer. It’s a fun challenge to read a question and try to solve it while using your reading skills and comprehension to process the correct answer of how, why, when or where something happened.

While this app is aimed for kids in grades 2 through 5 who may be struggling with reading comprehension. I can also see the benefits that this app would present to a first grader who is learning to comprehend what they are reading. My daughter and I experienced fun quality time while playing this learning game together. Recommend.

I love this game as do my children (6, 8, and 10). We have spent many hours huddled around my phone playing this game together.

The core game is amazing in it's own right...but what makes it even better are the little laughs we get when we see a state look a certain way or a stack fall after a long battle w/ gravity and physics. Those little things make us keep going back for more...not to mention the add-on games are great too. It really gives the kids something to strive for, an achievement to work towards and a reward for continual pressing. I know they've got a better knowledge of State Flags than I do now!

Like I said, we love this game. I hope that they continue with it after they hit their 40 states (the level to attain the last game), but know that they'll just have to learn Stack the Countries afterwards!

A couple things i'd suggest for consideration...
- Zoom - I think this would be a lot more enjoyable for things like map it, i'd rather fail knowing I stuck Vermont in the wrong place than just mash my fat finger in the North East and get it right. If ease of use for children is the concern, have easy and hard mode?
- Accelerometer - Just a wish/dream mostly! But I think it'd be great fun for me and for the kids, if during stacking, you could present an option for the user to counteract the balance/gravity/physics. Not completely, but just a subtle nudge that might let them win by tilting the phone away from the sway. I mean we're doing it anyways, haha, you might as well give them something for the effort! haha

review_headline: New App Not In Touch With the Small Screen
review_body: Changing and improving apps is expected in a digital world, but making an app that is more difficult to use defeats the purpose. In size alone, the new CNN app trades glitz for utility. Before the upgrade, a convenient list of stories with a snippet of content provided readers with the option of selecting only those stories they cared to read. All stories in each topic fit on one screen. Now, the page is full with a large image and a small amount of text garnering three to four stories on small screens -- in my case, a Kindle Fire HD -- requiring so much scrolling as to cause dizziness and nausea. Using the app on my DROID Razr is even worse. More testing and user input might have made this new app palatable for mobile devices. As it is, I will be looking for a news source that focuses more on news and less on window dressing.

When grandma calls and can't get to her online games, it is so much easier to remote in and resolve the issue for her instead of trying to explain everything to her blind. I have also found it much easier to explain things if you can control the mouse on the remote screen while explaining. Also no one has to beat their head against the wall because of misunderstandings. Let's face it.  We can't all be technology geniuses. I'm a firm believer of getting someone that knows what they are doing to perform the service and either pay them for their time and expertise. Or there is always the barter system which works well for me. Personally, I can't can pickled peppers to save my life, but guess what... grandma does. As far as the subscription price being too high for the disillusioned... Well in the south we call the God's special little projects... $17.00 for a years worth of trips to help mom or grandma fix an issue that takes 3 minutes and $10 worth of gas each trip, well that seems like a bargain to me.

That is why I have given this app a one star review because this is totally frustrating and incorrect.  After all, GMT (Greenwich Mean Time) is very important in getting the correct natal chart set up with the correct Acendant sign.  As this sets up one's whole natal chart and planetary positions.  If the GMT is off by an hour, the Ascendant sign will also be off by that one hour and this moves all the planets into incorrect positions in incorrect houses, unless it is a very slow moving planet such as, Pluto, Neptune, Uranus and Saturn.

review_headline: pretty good... at first. a warning to buyers.
review_body:
At first it was shaping up to be a very good game. The story was interesting, the gameplay was fun, the mechanics worked well, and there is NO In-App Purchases. But past that it pretty much goes downhill.

The first thing i notice is that it prompted me to rate 5 stars to get 500 coins, and while a rare rating reminded i don't have a problem with, i absolutely hate when games make you rate 5 stars in order to get a prize, its just sleezy. you should want honest ratings. And while this only happened a few times, its definitely worth noting.

Also, there is in-game money, and at first you earn in-game money by going to a casino, witch is absolutely terrible. The flip a coin is simple enough, but its definitely not a 50/50 chance, witch is good if you want money, but its definitely not a gamble, in these money earning sequences you have about a 9/10 chance to win, so its kinda pointless and boring. Next there is a dice game, witch makes absolutely no sense whatsoever, the "instructions" if you can call them that don't explain anything, so basicly you are just rolling and dropping dice and hoping you get a randomly selected higher number then your "opponent", again, you win this almost every single time so its both confusing AND pointless AND boring. Later you unlock a car race / betting game where you can either bet on a car similar to horse race betting, or drive in the race yourself. Again, the car race betting is pointless and boring. while much simpler, it still has about a 9/10 maybe a 8/10 chance of winning, and there is always only 1 lap even though there is a lap counter. The car racing at first is absolutely terrible with the controls, but if you get the hang of it its just basically the same thing as betting but you have to drive AND be bored.

and past that, probably my biggest complaint, is content. the game is VERY short, i was able to beat it in probably an hour. Sure that hour was pretty fun, but the story gets so rushed, and it leaves a sour taste in your mouth. Just by the way, not a spoiler, but the game leaves off on pretty much a giant cliffhanger that leaves it open to future dlc's / a sequel.

Speaking of DLC, there is a free DLC witch again, i am very glad that its free, but the thing is, to unlock it you have to rate the game 5 stars. witch again, is so incredibly frustrating to me. i wouldn't mind rating it 5 stars, if it deserved it. and it doesnt. luckily my game had somehow glitched and i was able to play the dlc without rating it 5 stars, as you can clearly see, and this dlc is so short, i beat it in under 10 minutes, its only about 4 or 5 missions. it tries to link the story of the main game to the story of a police sniper, but it does so very terribly and with no explanation or backstory. it seriously felt as if i was missing something. and again, it leaves off in such a stupid way i wonder why they even made it in the first place.

So while the content that is there is enjoyable, and the missions are pretty diverse and fun, it feels like an unfinished game. its took some thinking, but i say it is still worth the 99 cents. it will have you entertained for an hour and a half or so, and having no in app purchases is very refreshing to see. but as a game itself its only worth the 3 stars.
I understand they have to make money, provide ads and up-sell their apps, but these stupid flashing ads are truly annoying! Change them or people like me will use some other apps for sure.

review_headline: Great game for preschoolers to learn how to know and write their letters, numbers, and shapes.
review_body: I was able to get this app to review it.  My three year old and 5 year old love this game.  There are eight different games in this app:  Three of them teach your child the numbers and how to write them correctly.  There is one game for numbers 1-10, one for numbers 11-20, and one for 10-90, counting by tens.  Then there are three games dealing with letters.  Two games teach the child how to trace uppercase and then lowercase letters.  The other game tells the name of the letters and shows and says words that start with that letter.  The last two games have the children tracing shapes.  One game is specific shapes like square, triangle, etc.  The other shape game are tracing robots that have shapes which helps develop fine motor skills.  It is a way to encourage educational learning while the child thinks he is playing.  I would recommend this for any 3-5 year old, especially if you are wanting to teach these concepts.

review_headline: A light and straight dice roller
review_body:
Just like it was already said, it's a dice roller that does exactly what it is supposed to do, in a simple and direct way. With no technical flaw. No bugs, no strange behaviors, no hard-to-see numbers, no counterintuitive menus. Neither there are background images, dice rolling animation or visual effects. Instead, it runs light and fast, with virtually no battery use. Almost like the device is in stand-by mode.

The Stored Dice feature is nice. No short limit for the name of the stored set. That's good. But I miss the option to edit the sets already saved. If you have stored some common rolls for your character, when it levels up, you have to rewrite a whole bunch of sets, instead of just editing each one.

Another nice option would be the ability to sort the stored sets, putting the most important rolls first, for example. As it is now, in alphabetical order, you may use numbers before the names to create your own sort. But, to change the sort, you have to edit some sets (rewriting them all over again). If you are a perfectionist like me, you end up with a lot of work. :)

I also missed the d3 die (for the unarmed damage of a medium creature in D&D 3.5). With no dice animation, it shall be easier to create custom dice like d3, d7, d17 or whatever impossible dice you would want.

Someone complained about the "toolkit" name. I kind of agree, because there is no other RPG feature besides the dice roller. But that's a problem with the name, not the app itself. A minor issue to me.

I know I complained more than complimented. Don't get me wrong. That's just minor suggestions to make better something that's already good. Very good, indeed.

Bottom line: if you want a dice roller to impress your friends with beautiful graphics, Prime Dice is your best shot. But if you want something that works fast, straight and flawlessly; D20 Toolkit is the one. And it's really free. No ads at all.

review_headline: Don't let the graphics put you off
review_body:
In this case, the book is better than the cover. The graphics are not the best, but the Dev already stated that he made the game by himself.

But honestly, the game is pretty solid for an rpg. Been on it for a couple of days now and it is more fun than a lot of the other free rpg's out there.

And the controls are pretty unique and work great. Your hero moves where you drag your finger. How I've been playing is that I put my finger right on top of him and he just follows which ever direction I want him to go. To fight you just tap on the enemies. The spells are fun to cast, too. Just release your finger from the screen and then your spells pop up for you to use. Then you just drag the spell down the person you want to cast the spell on.

Give it a day and I'm sure you will get past the graphics and be more focused on the storyline, mechanics, and the leveling up of your hero.

review_headline: Two months later - a free players perspective
review_body:
I play the game roughly every two hours. After about two months I have reached level 66. The highest level is 120. Gaining levels is as fast now as it was at level 20, so long as you use your energy wisely.

The only requirement is to log in throughout the day to spend the energy -like all other energy games. But even better, this one gives you hours to log out and do other things as you gain 1 per 10 minutes. This is great for me as it allows me to maintain a steady pace in leveling and obtaining good units, while juggling real life. Other games take up too much time.

I have not needed to spend any money to have a team of good units. You get enough in game currency through playing to get several of the premium units as you level up. The ranking system is mainly bragging rights, another casual point.

Since I began playing there have been too many events to count.
New content has been every 1-2 weeks.
Constant internet not a requirement! I can load a mission and it will allow completion before needing a connection again.

And about those who complain about errors : yes they happen but it happens in every game. The difference here is they often compensate for any problems with valuable items, so I only see it as a good thing. A little web searching can help most resolutions for app crashes etc. Most people would just rather complain than look for help.

-tldr :

Pros:
In app purchasing tempting, but not neccesary
New updates often, New units, events, etc.
Casual daily player friendly. None of that hourly to remain competitive junk.
Steady leveling pace and game progression.
Company cares enough to admit to server errors and compensates well! A rare quality in a game developer.
Constant internet connection not a requirement~

Cons:
Infrequent crashes. Usually only last a few hours but doesn't remain an issue long.
Not much in game help for new players, so a little research is advised.

If you are looking for a way to rack up your Swagbucks and earn more rewards this is definitely the way to go!

review_headline: Challenging game in need of some improvements
review_body:
This is a fun diversion if you like crossword-style games. I took away a star for two flaws:

- The game doesn't prevent the screen from dimming, which quickly becomes annoying if you're sitting there thinking about the next clue and have to keep poking it awake
- Some of the clues are kind of "off" and some even appear machine-generated. For example, the clue will be in past tense but the answer won't, or an archaic spelling of a common word will used instead, or the answer will actually appear in the clue (e.g. ""Having more than one story" = "Multistory")

Two more notes:
- Most puzzles have at least one very obscure word. I used to think this was a flaw, but as long as you can solve the rest of the words, the last one can be puzzled out by process of elimination an intelligent guessing, so I guess it's just a challenge.
- It would be great if you could drag the answer bits around to pre-form your guesses. It has the ability to randomize their order, but that's not as helpful.

I'm 35 years old, so I grew up on side scrolling platform games.  While I've moved on to mostly FPS and RPG games these days, I do still quite enjoy these old school games.  Sonic has always been one of my favorites.  The first Sonic game came out in 1991 to give Sega a \\"mascot\\" character to rival Nintendo's Mario.  Though, I actually prefer Sonic to Mario.  This particular game came out for Sega CD, an attachment for the Sega Mega Drive/Genesis.  This means it's bigger than your standard Genesis games and has graphic and sound improvements.  It also means it's a larger file, 260MB.  The graphics on this port are great, just like the original graphics but in a 16:9 widescreen, to fit most tablets and phones in \\"landscape\\" mode.  Only the movies are in 4:3 \\"fullscreen,\\" likely due to the fact that there was no way to change that without stretching them, which would have looked bad.  Play wise, it's just like Sonic was back in the day.  The controls are very simple:  left and right on the on-screen  D-pad to move, the button on the right jumps.  That's all you need for classic platform games.  Permissions wise, I don't know why a 1990s video game port needs the Internet, but it does.  Other than that, the permissions seem normal.  Overall, this is a great game for anybody who loves Sonic, old school side-scroller games in  general, or who just wants to play a fun, fast paced game without a lot of story to slow things down.

review_headline: Just okay for reviews and such, but GREAT for being able to link your UltraViolet account
review_body:
If you have a lot of UltraViolet digital movies and a Kindle Fire HD...this is the absolute best way to be able to see all those movies on the go. It links directly to your UV account so anything that you register there will be available on your Fire. (If you buy movies on the different services like VUDU though, you won't see them, so keep that in mind.)

You have to enable location services for the reviews and suggestions to really work well, and if you have a WiFi-only tablet, you know that your WiFi might give your location as being many miles away (it will give the location of the server farm you're connected to)...so it's not very useful. (As an example, I live in Southeast Indiana, but my WiFi location is often listed as Troy, Ohio!)
The app does let you manually input your location, so it's not completely useless...but it really doesn't work the way it should if you are on a phone or tablet with GPS location service.

Being able to download your movies for off-line viewing (an absolute necessity if you're on a WiFi-only tablet and want to have some movies for the kids to watch on a car trip) more than makes up for any deficiencies in the other area, so it's a firm 5-stars.

The theme of the app is endangered wildlife, and the 20 levels have some great artwork of endangered animals on land and in the sea. I recognized most of the animals, but I had to look up some of them, including a tarsier (a type of primate), pangolin (scaly anteater), and a leafy seadragon (a fish). The app developer has camouflaged many of the objects into the background, making them tougher to find (also watch for objects along the edge of the screen). Each level has 9 hidden objects which you have to find before time runs out, or you lose. I'm not always fast enough to find them all, so my favorite mode is "Nice and Casual," with no timer and unlimited hints. To score a lot higher, play the Normal or Challenge modes, where a timer is running and hints are very limited. You can choose which of four ways to find the hidden objects, but I recommend "Find by Picture" unless you're very good at this. You can also choose how well hidden the objects are.

With a total of 24 different modes and options to select from, you can tweak the game to be anywhere from very easy to very difficult, which makes it a very playable game for almost any age.

The concept is pretty basic – grow your own aliens in space on a planet / asteroid and then try to take over another populated planet.

If you turn the full graphics package on (you can adjust it), the graphics are pretty detailed; I leave it on as minimal as possible as this game is a huge drain on your Kindle Fire battery: after about an hour and a half of play (I know, it sounds like I have a problem), starting with a full battery with the 8.9” HDX you will be down to about 10% power.

I originally picked this up for free as a free app of the day vs. its normal price of $4.99; despite my discussion of the instructions in the first paragraph, I will say I’ve received a heck of a lot more entertainment value out of this and would recommend it.

product_title: Free Calls with magicApp by magicJack
review_headline: A cheap pre-paid smartphone with limited minutes is all you need with this app
review_body:
As with any app (particularly free ones) you have pros and cons. So I will try to break down this app according to each.

Pros: Airtime Free Calls to any US or Canadian Number, No data, text or voice service required to use this app, all you need is wifi access, You can also use this overseas to make free calls to any US or Canadian number as long as you have wifi access, It will never use your minutes.

Cons: You can only shut it down by doing a force stop, it is a battery hog, not super practical for incoming calls due to the aforementioned reasons as well as the fact that number that shows up on the caller ID tends to alternate. Calls can be spotty at times (especially if you have another demanding drain on your wifi ie video streaming).

Summary: Given the fact that it's free and that it doesn't have the limitations that other wifi callers have (ie requires data and/or minutes, limited to only members who have the same app) it's really hard to judge it too harshly for it's faults. I find it simply amazing that my wife's deactivated smartphone can still place calls with this app for 100% free as long as she can get a wifi signal. Good luck getting that with any other app paid or otherwise. I have T-Mobile and don't have to pay for data (which most other wifi callers require) and as such this was the perfect answer for what I do (smartphone that I use only with wifi and then regular pre-paid minutes only cell service). Many complain about not being able to shut it down but it is only a minor inconvenience as you can go into your manage apps and force stop the app. It won't cause the app to misbehave. I do it all the time after I get done using it and have had no adverse side effects from doing it.

Memo Cars is very much like Memory except you don’t have to hand-sift through the cards to create a smaller playing set for varying skill levels. The options are built-in: Easy, Medium, Hard, and Insane.

I played this on my phone and the screen is only 4 inches, so I didn’t attempt to load the Hard or Insane levels. The developer suggests using a tablet for those levels and I agree it would be better because there are so many cards and the graphics would be larger.

But your phone is perfect for the Easy & Medium selections. The resolution is great and the graphics are cute. Since you’re scored by the time it takes you to complete a board, it’s a competitive thing. Even after you work up the levels, you can play again to try to beat your previous score.

Fairly quick download and easy interface. All-in-all a great app.

But after a while, the game becomes increasingly challenging to the point where it's nearly impossible to complete specific missions without in-app purchases. The prices of weaponry is so outrageously high compared to the low income from missions that it would take even a skilled gamer days to acquire a new weapon. And by the he/she does get the money, that weapon is already going to be too weak for extended use.

The above mentioned things are traits of all Contract Killer games. I have played them all, and found the same scenario in Contract Killer 2 but not so much in the original Contract Killer. Please take my advice and just buy Dead Trigger. It's extremely fun and has very very good in-app purchase rates. ($6.99 is the highest in-app purchase price and for an extremely generous amount.) It has very fun gameplay, is easy to get into, and has very user friendly controls. It's also FREE.

Overall, this game is fun to play in the beginning. But if you're going to play extensively, then you better have a good amount of cash set aside for in-app purchases.

review_headline: Packs some punch, but not a KO.
review_body:
The game evokes nostalgia by mimicking the Punch-out!! series, complete with cheezey international stereotypes. The game's rules are easy to understand, it starts out very easy to play and gradually becomes more challenging; yet it gives you new hints along the way.
However, the gameplay is quite choppy and difficult; the graphics seem like a cheap flash game from the early 2000's; it often involves 'button-mashing' more than skill; the layout of the game seems hastily designed, and in fact, the overall silliness could be enhanced.
In essence: Punch-out!! fan will play this game for its thematics, and s/he'll find an even balance between pro's and con's. The new-comer will likely either find this game very enjoyable or very disorganized.

review_headline: CUTE HYGIENE practice for small children - Very BASIC though - Just OK, Not Great.
review_body:
Pepi Bath has a nice concept with simple Interactive Hygiene activities for kids to practice. Graphics and Sounds are Cute but the required Tasks are very Basic and too simplified compared to other apps of this type. There are around 4 to 5 Tasks to be completed in each of 4 areas (Wash Room, Toilet, Sink and Bathtub activities). However, the Interaction is minimal and keeps you wanting more. It does have some interesting and important teaching features like Water getting TOO HOT in tub if you don't open both faucets and Filling washing machine Soap before washer can start. Basic ideas get across but in a Crudely basic way. It could use some more Interactivity with Boy or Girl to increase the Fun.

Overall, somewhat Interesting and Fun Interactive play at first but lacks any strong Replay Value. Can get boring fairly early since interactivity is limited to specific Tasks that have to be done exactly the way they want it or it will not complete each section properly. App is JUST OK! Other games like (DR. PANDA Beauty Salon) have more Versatile, Interactive features and activities to keep players engaged Satisfied.

Negatives: Imposes FLURRY ANALYTICS Addon without telling us about it. Also lacks a Complete Shut Down feature. Probably kept active so FLURRY can continue to get Real Time Data off your device unless you shut App down with a Task Killer. Sadly, it does not compete well enough with other, better apps on the market, fails to EXIT Completely and has Flurry Analytics to Data-Mine info. I Cannot Recommend it.

review_headline: The ads BLOCK the letters... makes it hard to play.
review_body:
You are given 4 pictures and you have to guess the movie title that the pictures are representing. It's difficult to play because the ads block the bottom row of letters. You are given two rows of letters to choose from to spell out the movie title but the ad literally cuts off the bottom of all the letters on the bottom row! If you pay $1.99 you can get rid of the ads but I don't want to pay... I wouldn't mind the ads if they weren't blocking the game! Please fix this!

Besides the issue with the ads I do like this game. Don't let the screenshots fool you. It starts off very easy but soon gets challenging and I like that. If you guess correctly you get coins which you can use to help out the harder ones. The main issue I have is that when guessing I can't tell if the letter I'm choosing is an "I" or "L" because again the ad is blocking the bottom half! I've somewhat learned hot to manage and will just erase the letter if it's not what I thought it was but I really hope the developer reads my review and fixes this issue.

I recommend this to anyone who likes movies because after all the whole point of the game is to guess the movie title!

If you enjoyed the first Weird Park game and/or Stray Souls, both from Alawar, you will definitely enjoy this one. The game is long, and with each section only having 3-5 scenes you don't have a lot of the going back and forth between scenes that are too far away. Everything you come to expect from Alawar is here. Nice graphics, fun ho scenes (each one played twice and includes one object where you have to do something to find it first), fun challenging puzzles with a skip if needed, and an enjoyable storyline. This is truly a five star game, but I deducted one star because three times it froze on me and then the game would exit and do the whole extra download stuff again. I have a decent enough device (kindle fire hd 2012 model) and fast enough wireless that it only took about 5 minutes each time. Thankfully upon returning to the game my place would be saved. This only really happened in the first one or two sections. But after that I then had many times when the next scene would show up black (with the exception of the pause, hint and inventory/journal buttons) and seem to freeze again. After anywhere from 30 seconds to 1 or 2 minutes the  game would pop back up for play. I am going to uninstall and reload the game. If the above does not repeat I will consider it a rare glitch and change my rating to 5 stars.

review_body: Beginner levels do not require friends.  However, as you progress, you will be dependent on friends for gifting purposes.  The game is lots of fun. You are only allowed to receive a certain number of gifts each day.  Some items cannot be gifted to you.  You must earn them by playing the game. Those items are VERY hard to obtain.  I am at level 54 and am still learning the game.  I would recommend / request that instructions be provided and that gifting be made easier.  As I play, I hear good and bad comments about the game.  It is hopeful that Administers of the game are listening to this feedback and using it to make the games more enjoyable.  I am addicted to the game now and do not plan to quit.  Just hoping my comments will reach those who have the power to improve the game, not only for current players, but for newbies also.

review_headline: Good tool for people with neurological issues
review_body: I had a stroke.  You can actually see tiny pinholes in my brain on the scans, showing  where the blood clot traveled to the brain and 'shattered' into little bombs.  My memory is like swiss cheese.  I write EVERYTHING down.  When I discovered Evernote, I put an old -- but wireless enabled -- kindle fire on my kitchen counter.  I keep my smart phone with me all the time.  My laptop is always on and always beside my chair in the den.  I am never far from an Evernote 'portal' and  i enter notes to myself all day long.  Voila, the to-do list stays current and in my face until I mark items off. One day i envision this type of technology being reduced to a chip that is embedded into the brain, serving as augmented circuitry to compensate for damaged neuro pathways.  Until then, Evernote is a good start.

When you move, your Wi-Fi modem just might be having problems because everyone in your neighborhood is on the same channel. This game is very well done and enjoyable, but I was only able to hunt about a dozen times before it started asking for money.  Now, I understand that in today's world 'free' has a different connotation, but I think the market is becoming keenly aware of 'teaser' games.  For instance, there is a timer error that cannot be resolved, but you can always buy credits to hunt more; the timer is supposed to refill every ten minutes allowing you to hunt more.  Developers should charge up front for unlimited play, but I suppose some sales person has convinced the industry that there is an unlimited well that can be tapped into with pay to play service.  Well, it has undermined the public trust in the gaming industry who once made games for a love of it, but it seems now that they are more interested in the money.  Everyone needs an income, of course, but it has gone to far.  Stop the pay to play practice, charge a fair price for games, and return the industry to the games and away from the bankers and salespeople.

I've been trying out various bingo games to find the right one for me. Not too loud with annoying graphics or boring with low payouts. Many have been boisterous rather than lively and most are joined at the hip to slots with 20+ payout lines. Not everyone is looking for both. Other bingo games and slow and monotonous and could only be useful as a sleep aid. Bingo Blast is fun with great background music. The caller has a clear, pleasant voice; since we have to listen to her, that is huge! The game rewards nicely and allows the player to use more than one card after introductory play. If a 10 sec game ad is shown, you are compensated. Every few hours you are given more bingo tokens and motivation to keep playing is there.

Bingo Blast sets itself apart by a allowing you to "pass to the next number" with a manual button rather than wait until the next number is called. That alone is a great feature as you are playing a timed game and you can use this to your advantage. By the way, you do get more time if you are playing more than one card. I have not yet graduated to three card or four card play, but I would assume that the providers of this game will have all four cards on the same screen. The last two games I tried expected the user to A) scroll between card #1 and card #2, and scroll from #1,2 then down to #3,4. When playing against others, the scrolling gives unfair advantage to people playing a single card. Also, as I am playing on a 8.9" or 7" Kindle Fire HD, it is ridiculous to think that at least four cards would necessitate scrolling up and down during play.

I am impressed by the setup so far and hope there are no snags going forward. Great features, no lag time and does not nag me to connect to Facebook or invite anyone. Will be glad to update as I progress. I have already tried and deleted at least 10-14 bingo games already. This one I absolutely recommend.

review_headline: The Cave is a great mix of puzzle solving, platforming, and item hunting. Warning: plenty of stability/compatability issues.
review_body:
EDIT: Updated and re-written on 4/1/2014 after some more compatibility and performance issues have been resolved.

Ron Gilbert is a great designer and after hearing that he will be releasing a new adventure game, I went a little nuts. I mean after such great titles as Maniac Mansion, Day of the Tentacle, and the Monkey Island games (not even going to mention his non adventure games), I had VERY high expectations. I actually bought this game on Steam and for Android as soon as they became available.

First of all let me get all this crash talk out of the way. They have obviously been making progress from when the game launched, but there are still issues.
It runs flawlessly on my Nexus 5 and my wife's Nexus 4. I went through the game thrice on my Nexus 5 (with one crash), and my wife ran through it once on her Nexus 4 (with no issues). HOWEVER it does crash (is unplayable) on my friends Galaxy S3, and LG G2. No idea what the cause of this strange behavior is. After he rooted his S3, and installed a custom ROM (Cyanogenmod) - it worked fine. He does not want to root the G2, so I have no idea if it would work on that (while rooted).

If the game is crashing for you, maybe try updating your version of Android (OS), or if you are at all tech savvy, root your phone and install a custom ROM (WARNING this will void your warranty and may brick/break your phone).

Finally when you download the game from here, open it and let it run for a while - as it needs to download some more files and update. It may look like it's not responding, but it's actually downloading some data.

With that out of the way, lets get on to the game.
I will TRY to make this as spoiler free as possible, and I ask that you keep it spoiler free in the comments section as well.

The Cave has a vast and varied cast of characters (7 to be exact), each having their own unique ability that will come in super handy when trying to solve puzzles. You form a party of three of these and head into *ominous voice* THEEE CAAAAAAVVEEE.

While inside you solve various puzzles and interact with the denizens that thrive within. Using your character's unique abilities you get access to areas that others can't reach, so in order to get the full story you will need to beat the game 3 times. Don't worry, puzzles can be solved in different ways and every character has unique areas, which cuts down on the tedium.
The game is also fairly short, clocking in at about 2-3 hours per playthrough, but much shorter your last time through. All in all I finished the whole thing in about 8 hours.

Both the graphics and sound are excellent, with crisp visuals and some memorable tunes (and sound effects) throughout.
Special mention goes to voice acting, with some very familiar voices that gamers will surely recognize.
Another mention goes to the touch controls (that take a while getting used to, but are quite good after the initial hassle). This game proves that adventure games benefit greatly from the touch screen. Really, being able to play the game with such ease is pretty amazing. I thought I would miss the mouse, but I do not.
See something? Simply touch it! That's all there is to the controls! Great job Double Fine!

My only complaint (other than crashing on some systems) is that the areas you explore seem underpopulated, and the lack of tough puzzles (and puzzles in general) is a downer. I expected a bit more from Ron.

My minor gripe is that once again there are unnecessary permissions (for a single player game) in the form of:
Open network sockets, Access information about Wi-Fi networks, and Access information about networks. But that is most likely for the following reason: Allows verification of Google app Entitlements.

Still, no IAP or extremely dangerous permissions (and classic gameplay) prevent me from giving it anything but an almost perfect score.

Simply put this is (currently) one of the best adventure games on the Android platform, and well worth the $4.99 asking price.

If it did not crash so much on different Android hardware, I would make it a 5 star game - that said, my friend managed to get a REFUND from Amazon after proving that it kept constantly crashing on his G2 and Galaxy S3, AND he got to keep the game to boot.

review_headline: Fun but very time consuming (or expensive)
review_body:
I came across this late last week and installed it onto one of my kid's Nabi tablets to check out. At first glance, the graphics make it look like some cheesy 1980's/1990's 8-bit home console port. Don't let the graphics fool you, it's still a challenging and fun game to play. After playing for quite a few hours on my first game, I reset it and started over using some of the knowledge I gained playing the first game. Here are my thoughts:

Pros:

- It's fun (If you like strategy/building games).
- It's addictive
- The limited \\"holiday\\" update I installed today adds another level of fun to the game (I got a chuckle out of watching an Imperial Probe Droid putting up Christmas lights).
- It'll keep you busy and out of the bars. :)

Cons:

- It's EXPENSIVE if you hit the store
- One you get through the initial few levels, it's painfully slow to get the resources needed to expand (I currently have 28 levels built -- 20 levels of apartments, shops, restaurants, etc., and another 8 Imperial levels. The cost in coin credits to build another level is $101,400. I am currently raking in around $10,000-$12,000 per hour on tips and goods, so as you can see, I have a nice boring 8+ hours of playing elevator operator to do before I can advance any further.
- Once you do build a new level, it's incredibly slow to watch the level get built. Really guys? At the point in the game where I am now, it currently takes 10.5 hours to build a single new level.. WOW!
- Watching golf on TV is more exciting that waiting to accumulate the \\"bux\\" needed to upgrade elevators. I could never imagine blowing bux on anything else or I'd never, ever have the possibility to upgrade elevators.
- There appears to be no way to STOP the game when you want to be done for the night. Even if I power cycle the tablet, the game awards me coin credits for the activities that have happened in my absence such as store stocks being depleted.

Tips:

- DON'T spend any bux except when you get enough to upgrade elevators
- DO use the \\"Upgrader\\" VIP several times on the same shop to increase the amount of supplies that the shop can carry so that you can build up your stock levels in order to use the \\"Big Spender\\" VIP to buy large stocks of items (thus gaining you big $$). What I do is upgrade a shop several times and then only stock the inventory in that shop for the item that costs 3 coins and then once the inventory is freshly stocked with like 3600 items, I'll unleash the \\"Big Spender\\" VIP to that shop and cash in for $10,800.
- Don't pay much mind to the Emperor's tasks -- they aren't worth the bother for the token coin credits you earn in return.
- Expand the Imperial levels as quickly as you can.
- Use the \\"Supply\\" VIP on the Imperial levels as often as you can as the more stock of each item you have in your inventory, the more $$ you can earn when you start chasing the \\"Darth Vader\\" tasks.
- DO upgrade the elevators whenever you can -- not only is it faster to move people around, you earn more \\"tip\\" $$ as well.
- DO build extra residential apartments. You will need workers on hand when you build shops. It also helps to have a stock of workers you can swap into better jobs based on their skill set for a given task and/or their dream job.
- DO evict workers with low skill sets.
- Unless you are building a residential level, don't save the \\"Recruiter\\" VIP as she will waste space on the Arrival level that could otherwise be used to hold a Big Spender or Supply VIP for when you can use them.
- DON'T get mad when the Rebels escape your grasp -- you get 2 bux for when they escape versus 1 bux when you capture them.
- Characters with a \\"?\\" on their heads will show an animated sequence if they are sent to the right level.
- Characters with a \\"?\\" on their heads also award 2x tips (at least on the new \\"holiday\\" upgrade that I got today) -- if you have a 2x or 4x elevator, then you get those as well (ex: I have a 4x elevator and I transport a Bitizen with a \\"?\\" to the 25th floor, I get a $25 tip x4 ($100) then that $100 gets a 2x award, so I end up with $200 tip for the trip.
- The \\"Darth Vader\\" Imperial tasks can get out of hand. My current \\"task\\" is to build 12 Control Panels (@ 1 hour each), create 10 \\"salvages\\" (@ 25 minutes each) and create 5 Rebel Traitors (@ 2 hours each). If I complete these, I get $80,700 coin credits.
- You can send Bitizens to levels under construction to reduce time building time for that level. Each Bitizen sent to a level under construction will subtract 1 minute from the time to build the level.

Optional:

- I like to use the \\"Level Mover\\" VIP to arrange all of my levels by type. I have all of my apartments grouped together. Then the food joints, and then the recreation places, etc. It makes it a little easier for me to monitor shop inventory levels having all of the shops grouped together.

Finding the animated sequences can be fun but I don't go out of my way to find them.

What I would like to see:

- Ditch the bux and just charge for the App -- say, $3.99
- If they won't abandon the bux, then add the ability to convert credits (coins) to bux

UPDATED 12/18 -- I was able to buy the \\"Ultra-Lift 3000 Extreme\\" elevator for $125 bux, so I now get 4x tips. The next elevator upgrade is @ $499 bux. Um, yea, right. I'll never see that one.

Cost to build the next level is now $117,600 coin credits and time to complete the current level under construction is 11.5 hours. Jeez.

The Imperial Probe Droid decorating the levels with holiday lights hadn't yielded much in the way of credits or bux. It did unlock a special \\"holiday\\" Fett at 20 levels decorated -- big whoop.

The faster elevators are at times difficult to stop on the correct floor -- especially in the Imperial levels.

UPDATED 12/25 -- I haven't been playing much this week. I currently have 36 levels (27 apartments, retail, service, etc, and 9 Imperial levels). The current cost to build another level is $173,400 and it takes 14.5 HOURS to build. Um, yeah. I will load the game, fully stock all of the shops and restaurants, send workers or service guys to where they need to go and then walk away from the game for a few hours and then check my progress and reorder supplies, collect any awards and then repeat the process. Since the cost to build and time to complete are so outrageous now, I can't imagine sitting here \\"playing\\" the game for hours on end like I did in the beginning. While the game is fun, the stupid cost and time to build levels paired with the unrealistic cost to buy bux, has in a way crippled the game for me. The game concept is good, but somewhere along the way someone at Disney/Lucas ruined the game with the credit/bux/time formulas.

I've noticed more and more bugs lately. The software seems to randomly crash. The Imperial level \\"Darth Vader\\" tasks have changed on me just prior to completing them -- the previously mentioned set of tasks that would have earned me $80,700 never materialized as with 2 tasks remaining, the group of tasks changed on me without any notice. VERY frustrating to say the least. As a side note, using the \\"holiday special\\" Imperial Probe Droid to decorate 35 levels awarded me with a bonus level -- The \\"Panna City Medicines\\" level.

UPDATE 12/28 -- I have down graded my star rating on this app. I have spent many hours building my Death Star over the past few weeks. I was up to 41 levels, $150,000 in coin on hand, $100 bux and a ton of tasks completed. I loaded up the app today to see where I was at from the overnight shutdown, and found that it has reset itself back to start. I am in the process of uninstalling it from the tablet as I type this. The app has been very buggy since an update was installed a few days ago, so I have to assume my game resetting was due to a flawed update from Disney. I'm officially done with this app. It was fun while it lasted, but I'm not about to invest any more of my time in the game.

I can tell you that I will never regret this purchase so let me make this quick and simple. The GRAPHICS: are one of the best you will ever see on a tablet, it is definitely up there with Dead Trigger, and Shadow Gun, mabey even better! The smoothness and frame rate: Don't worry if your playing on a kindle because it runs like a champ, consistent frame rate at 60 frames a second, only drops when at very lighted areas, or when there are lot of npc's/AI on screen. Control's: they are fairly well not the best they could've been fleshed out a little better then they are here, it kind of puts you in a weird position when your right thumb is reaching out for all the touch buttons like reload, run, and more. Multiplayer: I like the deep system they have here, connection could be a bit laggy sometimes, but every multiplayer mode in any game has its problems. Campaign: I got to give it up to the developer here they really must of took there time with this one, I won't spoil anything but the actual story telling is kind of weak, but the good side is you do get immersed  in the experience you get, dealing with terrorists and U.S. soldiers trying to fight them off. Voice Acting: Not lack luster its actually very good, each moment has their different types of voices and emotions that come with them, nice job voice actors. Sound: Great audio, no complaints explosions, guns, and environments all sound realistic. My Final Verdict: Out of everything I said you probably think I'm going to going to give this game a perfect score. It's not completely perfect, but it's still a HELL of a game and I'm enjoying it still today. It shows the power of the Kindle tablet I have and Mabel yours too who ever you are. review_body:
Going into today I was really REALLY annoyed with the update that came out in December, because it made it so I couldn't read any books on my phone without setting it back to the factory version, re-registering my account, and then re-downloading all my books. The work around I did on my phone to be able to actually use this update was I disabled the Kindle app on my phone (I can't actually un-install the app) and went onto the Google Playstore and clicked the update button for the app from there. I'm wondering if the issue comes from the auto-updating.

review_headline: It's OK, but there are better journalling/notebook apps out there.
review_body:
If this app looks familiar, it is because it's a variation of Diary Pro, which was the FAOTD about a week ago. My issues are the same with this app as with the prior app. This one lets you create multiple notebooks as opposed to a single diary. But the same problems as in the earlier app still exist.

You can create a password, but in creating it, the password is hidden, so if you're not watching as you actually type, you can't tell if you mis-entered, and there is not a confirmation field where you enter it again. So, once you set it, test it right away before actually entering any data, because, as the app warns you, you cannot recover your password.

To test it, or if you use this app, to make sure your info is private, make sure you go back to the main page of the app before exiting; if you are on a page of a notebook and exit, you are able to go back to that page without entering a password. So, so much for the password. I've left the app, gone into other apps, and then gone back and right into the page I was working on.

You can backup to Dropbox. The export is only usable to import back to Notebook Pro. You can also convert a notebook or a page within a notebook to PDF.

There isn't much in the way of instruction, though there is a help page on the main menu. Touching the icons reveals what they do pretty quickly.

You can add drawings and photographs to entries; however they do not show within the page but as attachments.  You can have different fonts in different notebooks, but not within the notebook itself. You can search entries.  

Settings consist of a limited number of color themes, backup and restore settings and fonts.  It is very easy to use, and if all you need is a very basic diary and hinky ability to password isn't a problem, this isn't bad.  I've tested worse journals.

I prefer DIario, which may be found here: [[ASIN:B00CGYBLGA B00CGYBLGA]]

There are a few mini games and a plot that doesn't really fit. Also, the music, which I would expect to be public domain Christmas carols, is rock music?? It feels like parts were done by several different people who didn't realize they were all working on one Christmas-themed game. It is fun for a while, so feel free to try it out, especially if it is the FAOTD, but I will likely remove it from my device in a few hours, once I finish the game. It does appear that it will take more than a day to finish the entire game.

review_headline: Like the mag, dislike the format
review_body:
I have been a subscriber to This Old House magazine for a long time, and usually find it be be as interesting as the tv show is. I like the details about the projects, or houses. Love seeing what others have done as upgrades - the sharing of their readers' projects or makeovers is wonderful! I pass this magazine on to my neighbors, who also "like to look" but need to pinch their pennies.
So I tried the digital version.
This is more an expression of annoyance about magazines online than it is about This Old House mag. Even on my computer, I find having to turn it page by page a drag. On my Kindle, I get _extremely_ annoyed by the turn it page by page way of reading it, as you have to go by the pages with ads, or other stuff. If I don't remember exactly where something was, the comparison between just being able to flip to a page, vs. the go page by page!!!, is very vexing to me. I use their website to read articles all the time. THIS is just a pdf where the magazine is scanned in. Useful, but I do not find this format very readable.

review_headline: Not worth much - permissions make it a 1 star
review_body:
I thought this was a cook book app where I would have interactive recipe info. It would be nice to see recipes with the ability to see how each ingredient offsets a particular "bad" food (lowering salt needs, reducing fat, etc.), but this is really nothing more than an app to link to other websites. I could have quickly searched for any of these recipes online without paying for this app. I'm not really sure if the developer got permission to link to these sites, but assuming he/she did, it is still not an app worth more than a dime. You really have access to all of these recipes for free if your phone/ tablet has the ability to access the internet...and it must or else you couldn't download the Amazon store. As a result, it earns a total of 2 stars.

Furthermore, be aware there are some permissions that allow the app to work in the background and give permission for information exchange when you are not even using the app. This might simply be downloading ads, but why does it need ads in a paid app? Unfortunately, it may also be trying to get your info. Regardless of the reason, I don't see a need for it. I am deducting one star for this permission.

As a result, I do not recommend paying anything for this app. If you can get it as the FAOTD, you might want to take a look at it, but beware of the permissions.

I've been waiting for Candy Crush to come out on the Kindle market. My older sister owns it and is on level 170 or something. Having recently bought it, I'm on 35, but I do know a lot about the game.
Candy Crush has great graphics and somewhat of a storyline. You are helping a little girl find her way through the world of candy crush, while helping the "owner" of a specific section. With about 10 or 12 levels per section, you have five lives. When you beat a level, that life is not taken from you. When you finish a section, with the exception of the first two sections, you must complete three quests that are 24 hours apart.
Candy Crush does have a lot of in-game buying. Yes, it's trying to cheat you out of your money. But keep in mind that the game is free; they have every right to try. I know I would rather buy a free game with a lot of in-game buying options than a paid game with none. With in-game buying, you can play the game ans choose to spend your money, but you don't have to. That's another thing: the game does not need money to continue game-play. Game-play is completely free. Help with game-play is not.
Most of the bad reviews for this game are complaining about the in-game buying. These people seem to have no patience. With patience, this game is great! However, some people just end up paying because they can't wait. That's what the game is counting on.
So, to recap, this game is well-worth your non-money, and, if you decide to do in-game buying, your few dollars. Have fun!
