review_headline: Fun games, but wish they were more challenging
review_body:
I bought the pro version figuring it the best of comparable brain training programs, on price and quality. Of all the apps of this ilk, this seems to be the most like Lumosity. I scored much higher on this app (all 90th percentile or higher) than I did when I first started playing other similar games. The selection of games are a lot of fun and a good mental workout!

Edit 11/12:

After having this app for a few days, I have a few new observations I'd like to add.

My biggest critique is of the game \\"Abstraction.\\" There are several words that have multiple meanings that could be interpreted as either abstract or concrete. \\"Sloth\\", for example, as used by this game refers to the adjective synonymous with laziness and not to the animal. There are a few other words that have double meanings that could go either way.

I also wish the games were more challenging or that they would increase in difficulty over time. Several of the games I scored 100% on my first try, and don't really see the value of playing them ever again. The whole point of these games is to improve your cognitive skills, right? Once you get a perfect score, what's the value in continuing to play the same game?

After playing this app for 4 days, I have managed to increase all my scores so that now I am over 95% on every game; on 13 of them I rank in the 100th percentile. Game designers, if you read this, please offer updates! Please provide more games or make the existing ones more challenging.

product_title: Preschool All-In-One Learning - Bubble School Adventure Basic Skills A to Z: Learn to Read and Count with Animals and 220 Interactive Flash Cards – Educational Toy for Baby, Toddler & Kindergarten Explorers by Abby Monkey® Games for Kids
review_body:
Preschool All-in-One is a great game for toddlers around 2-4. It concentrates on colors and letters, so it may be too easy for older kids. It's not that older kids wouldn't enjoy completing the tasks-- I know they would because I sat and played with it for a while. If you want the educational benefit, it's best to buy this when they are very young. That is one of the advantages to low cost phone apps. They don't cost very much, and you get a tremendous benefit for your child. Pets, colors, and letters are free with the light version. Everything is pictures, so they don't have to know how to read, or have to rely on an adult to make it work. The graphics are animal heavy, so they are learning about different animals, too, plus they are dog gone cute! I went ahead and purchased the full app. It unlocks the bulk of the app, with letters, numbers, shapes, colors, toys, animals, fruits, vegetables and more. The animals are both zoo and farm animals.

review_headline: Great for those with speech issues & kids learning to read!
review_body:
I read several reviews about how great this app is for those who have physical difficulties speaking. No one in my family has that issue, but I do have a child in the pre-reading stages, as well as an early reader. For the youngest one, this app lets her copy letters from her picture books to the screen and then \\"read\\" words. We are playing a game of sight words like this. I will read the story and when we get to a sight word, like \\"the\\" she will type it in to the app and then say what she thinks it is and the app confirms her great skill.

The older elementary child is having fun practicing his typing while working on his reading, too. If he finds a word he can't read, the app will help him.

This is a fun app with a great stated purpose of helping those with speech difficulties, but it also assists little ones as they learn to read. It is a worthwhile purchase if you have anyone in your family in those circumstances. The voice is not annoying and the app is very accurate.

This game is based on an interesting premise--form a chain of words from a supplied list all linked to the adjacent word in some way such as synonyms, antonyms or going together (home and run). Unfortunately, as it's played, it becomes impossibly difficult very quickly. The chains rapidly become more and more elaborate, finally becoming lengthy trees with various branches, and too many of the associations are arbitrary... words could easily be linked with a half dozen of the other words, but according to the game, only one solution is possible for each puzzle.

The game has five difficulty levels, depending on how many words are already inserted into the tree to begin with... at the toughest level, you have to place every single word in the chain. There are also fifty puzzles in each level of increasing levels of difficulty as well, depending on how elaborate the tree is. Even at the easiest difficulty level, most people will have a tough time getting halfway through without a lot of guessing and retracing steps.

The game offers good value for the money in terms of number of puzzles, and it can be replayed since word lists change from one puzzle to the next, but it's going to be far too frustrating for most people (including myself).

review_headline: Once this is available for Kindle --- Great Game (w/ IAP)
review_body:
I know it's not available yet for U.S. Kindle users (it is available at Google Play) but when it is hopefully this review will help determine if you want to buy or not.

The game features a cartoony version of the He-Man cartoon from the 80s on a side scrolling button masher that should please both nostalgic parents and their children. Controls can be tough at times since they are virtual (meaning on the screen) and if you have a smaller screen your fingers will block some of the view and on bigger screens your hands may be uncomfortably far apart. There are a ton of 80s TV show references that keep fans smiling. Still, this is a very fun game so turn of IAP in your App Store settings and enjoy.

review_headline: A very good YouTube video downloader
review_body:
This is the best video download for YouTube I've seen yet. And the TubeMate website CORRECTLY says there are lots of fake clones of this application (ALL the versions on Google Play for instance), and not only do most of the clones not work, they are in fact Trojan horses for various forms of maliware and adware. This application DOES have adds, but I for one do not find them intrusive as they only appear within the application at the top of the screen, and this both keeps the app free plus doesn't slow the app down. ALSO in over 2GB of downloads I've seen so far ZERO porn adds. Not sure why others have, perhaps they should look at their own web-browsing history as to the reaso as adds areally usually targeted based on user activity.

As for the pros with this app, 1-you get fast download speed that downloads in the background allowing multitasking (you can track the progress in the menu download history), 2-ability to do up to 2 downloads simultaneously, 3-ability to select different download quality's (the Max based on the source video quality), this allows one to save space by selecting lower quality video if you don't have a lot of space (it usually still looks great BTW), 4-both app-specific and general YouTube search options, 5-enhanced fast download for devices that can support it (as an option from preferences), 6-a multitude of options to customize your user experience (most of which are shown to you when you first use the app in a short and easy to understand tutoria), 7-decent video player options for the videos you've downloaded (with this or other applications), and finally 8-the ability to choose the location (internal memory or external SD card, and which specific file that you wish)) both for downloading and playback. That last one is a real time saver for me as my device only has 5GB memory, but I have a 32GB SD card, and some HD 1080P videos can be as large as 100MB or more.

review_headline: Decent hidden object quest that gets repetitive
review_body:
At first glance Hidden Objects Quest 6 has a lot of content: each of twenty-four levels has three quests that can be completed three different ways, plus a bonus quest. The trouble is that, although the quests give you different lists of items to collect, each one uses the same map and hides each object in the same place, so after you've done a couple you're going to start remembering where things are, and get bored tapping them again. Many items are also re-used in different levels, so you'll be even more familiar with (or sick of) them. And some of the items stick out from the backgrounds so thoroughly that it's barely a ~hidden~ object quest. The game tries to liven things up by giving you only object silhouettes, names of objects, scrambled names of objects, various kinds of time limit, etc., but none of this changes the gameplay enough to make each map worth doing a dozen times. Nor do a long but not very enjoyable list of achievements and extra hidden objects to find.

It doesn't help that the design is on the cheap side. The background images and some of the objects are horror-themed but not especially spooky, and the rest of the objects (soccer balls, cows) are so not scary they would spoil the mood anyway. The menus are a bit annoying as well. After you select a set of three quests there's no way to go back and switch sets without using your device's back button, which takes you all the way out of the game. And you can't pause or re-start a level in progress. These flaws, like the hilariously tacky opening screens, reveal the cheapness that the game's apparent wealth of content is designed to disguise. If you like hidden object games a lot, enough to play the same level many times with minor variations (and many reviewers evidently do), this is worth paying for. Otherwise, grab it while it's the free app of the day, but don't bother spending money on it.

UPDATE: Playing a little deeper into the game and experimenting with all the modes hasn't changed my opinion very much. It eats up time, but it isn't varied or difficult enough to make for real fun. review_headline: the first computer game I ever truly loved was Virtual Villagers
review_body:
I was a lonely, awkward Freshman in high school the first time I ever played a Virtual Villagers game. And I was hooked from the first day! I wouldn't let anyone near the computer since the second I arrived home from school. Such good memories.

I was extremely disappointed when I bought a Kindle last Christmas and discovered there wasn't a single version of Virtual Villager available.

But I waited and waited and then I came across Virtual Families. It isn't the same, but it sustained me until Virtual Villagers: Origins was finally released.

Let me just say, I absolutely LOVE this game. I live, eat, and breathe Virtual Villagers. No other game compares. Not even Sims.

There is only one tiny little problem: my golden child is sadistic. I'm not sure if this happens to anyone else, but the golden child in my game throws a party whenever someone dies. Normally, I am able to overlook it, but this time HE WENT TOO FAR.

Please listen to my tale of heartbreak.

My favorite Villager died today (October 10, 2013). He was a male named Liko. He was with me since the start of the game. There wasn't anything extraordinary about him, but he was my favorite nonetheless. He was my first ever Master Scientist and when he was about 60 something, the thought struck me that he might be close to dying, so I granted him youth for 50000 science points. (Totally worth it!) Well, he ended up being in his thirties again and all was well in my world. Time passed, now he had turned 75.
I exited the game to play something else while my villagers raked in science points and food, and I returned to find him decomposing. I didn't cry like I usually do when my favorite character or player dies, but I won't deny I was sad.
Then something horrible happened.
As his remains were being carried away by one of his fellow villagers (and possibly daughter, he was quite the ladies man, even at an old age), the golden child decidesto "make a party". The villager that was carrying his remains drops him halfway to the graveyard and starts dancing. I damn near cried at that. My heart BROKE! Yes, his gravestone was there, but his remains were dropped AND LOST FOREVER because that golden child (who looks suspiciously like the killer doll, Chucky) wanted to watch everyone dance.

I hate the golden child at this particular moment. HATE him.

Golden Child, you have ruined Liko's burial. For that you must pay.
I would even go far as saying: "My name is Cindy Herrera. You ruined my Villagers burial. Prepare to die."
But who else will replenish my food? We live in a cruel, cruel world.

R.I.P. Liko, Master Scientist, Age 75
You were a great person. A not-so-good dad, but an excellent scientist.
You will forever live on in my heart.

The only good thing is that there is a heart engraved on his headstone. I truly did love Liko and I'm glad the heart is there. It makes me feel as if the others saw i thought fondly of him and engraved a heart to show me they felt the same way... Now every time we look at his grave we'll remember the good times we had with him and how much he meant to us.
Take THAT, golden child!

Other than that incident, though, this game is a slice of heaven. It isn't perfect, but i love it.

I only have one suggestion. The older villagers should be able to tell the younger villagers stories. I started this game thinking that if you dropped an older villager onto a younger one, they would tell them a story like in Virtual Families. Instead, the little ones run away and we get the message "the villager is still too young!" Or something along those lines. I felt like a pervert the first time I read that. That poor little kid must have thought I approached him with bad intentions. I DIDN'T! I simply wanted to tell him a story. Because a life without stories would be truly boring, in my opinion.

Like I mentioned before, I've been playing Virtual Villagers since I was a teenager. I've played just about every version and I have yet to be disappointed.

Thanks for the great memories, Last Day of Work.
May they last forever!

review_headline: Great program that I will purchase, minor quirk for me
review_body:
First up, I intend to purchase the full version of this, and will post the same review on the $1.60 version. I just now realized that this is a FULL FEATURED trial, and with that said it makes sense why I couldn't find the difference between the two.

Second thing. I have did the couch-2-5k program before, and a different style training program in the past. So i've been down this road before. I'm sort of doing the couch to 5k, to couch, to 5k, to couch, to 5k. Confusing enough? OK! For this round I'm getting back into the swing of it, and since I have a relatively new *droid style phone I would give it a shot. I downloaded the official C25K app to compare. This one beats it easily, here is why. Also I'll mention some things here that you may care about, but not for me (take it or leave it).

Pros:
Very simple interface
Useful audio prompts
Useful stats
Interesting mapping program

Take it or leave it:
Facebook / Twitter integration (I don't want folks to know what i'm doing on these)
AchieveMint Rewards (I believe that this could be cool, but think it has some privacy concerns for me)

Cons:
Audio Controls: I really do not care for the audio controls. It seems \\"clunky\\" to me and not intuitive. When you are doing your run, the stats pause the music and call out your time and distance (GOOD), but when your run is over, music just stops. I would prefer to have it integrate better with an external player, OR use my iPOD instead. This results in -.75 star for me, enough to take it down to a 4 on my official rating.

Ads: I'm using the free version, so those are annoying. I HOPE they are not displayed in the full paid program.

Overall: I like the program, its worth it to me to pay the $1.60 and get the full use out of it. Give it a shot, I bet you will like it. If you are curious why I prefer this over the official C25K program, I found their interface annoying just by looking at it, and promptly removed it.at it, and promptly removed it.

The wolves approach way too fast, and the controls are really clumsy.

This could have been a really great game if the dev had considered using actual color mixing science. All you need is the 3 primary colors, red, yellow and blue to mix all other colors. Combination swipes could achieve all other secondary colors. There would be no need for "dark and light" buttons, as black and white buttons could render pink, dark red, ect. But I don't think you would even need value changes with secondary color choices.

The graphics are so-so, but with more intuitive play that wouldn't matter so much. Great idea for a game, but it totally fails. Also, I would never give this to a child to play because of the incorrect color science.

I was excited when I discovered that there was a game called \\"The Room\\". I thought to myself, \\"Finally, someone else who realizes the brilliance of Tommy Wiseau's \\"The Room\\" has based an app on the movie!\\" I imagined how the gameplay would go; would this be RPG based, like \\"Final Fantasy\\"? Maybe this would be a fighting game along the lines of \\"Mortal Kombat\\", where you could choose to be Johnny and fight Mark and various other cast members from the movie.

product_title: GTasks: To Do List | Task List
review_headline: Planner girl finally adapting to paperless planning
review_body:
I have used a planner for over 20 years. I love the feeling of checking off my to-do list. As I grew older and my responsibilities grew, the planner was essential--I simply couldn't remember everything if I didn't write it down.
I've resisted the electronic planners for sometime now. I never converted to the palm pilot and even with the smart phone craze I held tightly to my real pages.
Enter GTasks. I LOVE this app! I can write down anything and everything I can think of and if I don't get it done on the due date, it stays at the top in the overdue list where I can either change the date or get it done.
Before with my planner, I'd have to look through the weeks and find the items I didn't have time to do and move them forward, all by hand. Tedious.
Now with GTasks, everything is streamlined. I'm better organized and with my Calendar app on my phone I'm saying goodbye to my planner.
There are tons of other great ideas with GTasks. I can think of an idea, like buying glowsticks for Halloween and put it in my task list with a due date a year from now.
If you're on the fence, definitely try out this sweet app!

The product: The graphics for this game are fairly simple but the lines are clean and the colors are fun. I love that I tap the screen to daub, it feels more like playing real bingo than using a mouse on the computer. I wish there was a way to customize the daub but if there is I haven't found it yet. The game has levels based on your play for which you gain experience, with certain levels unlocking more rooms. You can purchase coins, tickets, energy and keys. Tickets are used to buy the boards for each game. Energy can give you additional items to win during game play. Keys unlock chests you earn during play. You also have additional objectives such as get 10 bingos or play 10 games which give you bonus rewards.

So far I have had a lot of fun playing this game and I do recommend it. I wouldn't recommend it for some children though, but only because of how easy it is to make in game purchases for real money. For adults or older children who understand then the ease of in game purchasing is a great feature but for younger children who don't understand in game purchases cost real money this could cause problems for the parents. So far, I've won enough bonuses that I haven't had to spend any money in game to enjoy anything. However, I've only been playing a few days and I can see at some point to keep playing I may need to make an in game purchase.

product_title: Shiver: The Vanishing Hitchhiker Collector's Edition
review_headline: This has to be the best Big Fish game out there and I have played many Big Fish games...
review_body:
I can't describe how much I loved this game. I have played many Big Fish (BF) games and this one takes the cake. Well, it might be tied for 1st place. The game took me several days (playing off and on) to complete, so the length is perfect (although I would have loved it to go on) and definitely worth the $3.00. I did not have many issues like I have had with other BF games. The HO games are perfectly proportioned (I'm not a fan of too many HO games like some of the BF games have), the graphics are excellent and I can see all the objects whether I am zoomed in or out, and the game actually gives you a little bit of a hint of what you are supposed to do at a specific scene unlike others that just leave you to guess that you were supposed to put the scissors under the pillow to get the hammer....ok...how did they figure that out? review_headline: Not Knocked Out Over This Cartooonish Attempt Of A Boxing Game
review_body:
IMPORTANT NOTE: It appears there are 2 pages for Monkey Boxing since one shows around 30 reviews and another shows like over a thousand reviews on it. I posted this review twice but deleted the second post after the first one started showing up. So there should only be one review for this game from me now posted on Amazon.

The free paid app of the day in the Amazon Appstore for August 20, 2013 is Monkey Boxing by Crescent Moon Games.

I saw the title and icon for this game Monkey Boxing and I thought this was going to be one of those rather silly games. Then I saw the huge number of 5 star ratings this thing was getting. So I thought this might actually be good. Then I happened to notice that this game is from the same app maker as Paper Monsters which I haven't reviewed yet, but it was a fairly good game. So at this point I am thinking that maybe this will be a 5 star game like mostly everyone else is giving this.

Unfortunately for me this is not a 5 star game. Not even close.

While many others may like this game, I didn't care for it hardly at all. The app maker in this case decided to go with a cosmetic approach rather than a game play approach.

You can dress your monkey in different color outfits and add different items for the monkey to wear, but it doesn't affect the game play at all.

When it comes to the actual matches, the game play is rather repetitive and totally unrealistic. You are basically either throwing punches (that always seem to conveniently land in your opponent's body) or blocking punches by putting your fists up to block the incoming punches of your opponent. You and your monkey opponent never seem to really move around in this 3D ring except left and right along a two dimensional path in the ring.

I also miss the trash talking interviews that you see before the actual fights in real boxing which is a huge element to the sport. And boxing doesn't feel like boxing without a Michael Buffer type announcer announcing the introductions.

If you really want a simple repetitive boxing game with the ability to dress up a monkey in different outfits, this might be the game for you. I just don't care for this type of game much and apparently I am in the minority here based on the number of 5 star reviews. I am just trying to give my honest opinion of this game which is going to vary from person to person.

Had the app maker put as much detail into other aspects of the sport like they did for the monkey's appearance, this might have been a 5 star game by my standards, but since this is just a repetitive punch throwing game, I have to give this only 2 stars out of a possible 5 stars.

At $2.99 this is overpriced and I would recommend Paper Monsters from the same app maker for only $0.99 instead.

review_body: Having grown up subscribing to hard copies of newspapers, and then more recently subscribing to a digital version of a paper on an e-reader, I find this to be a great app.  First of all, it is free.  Second, there's nothing to throw away at the end of the day -- eco-friendly. Third, you get the complete paper, which you don't when you subscribe to the digital version.  Digital versions don't give you ads, comics, graphics, sports standings, etc.  This app does. I also find it fairly easy to navigate once you've messed around with its features for a few days. I think it is great that the Mercury News offers their product for free via this app.  I suppose they can get better advertising rates if they can tout that people are viewing the ads via this app.  I wish more newspapers would offer their newspaper this way. review_headline: HOW TO use ES File Explorer to do Bluetooth FILE TRANSFER on Kindle Fire HD
review_body:
I got fed up with trying to maintain a connection using a USB cable between my laptop and Kindle Fire HD 8.9\\" tablet for doing image and other file transfers. You'd think a USB cable would be more reliable than Bluetooth, WiFi, etc., but that wasn't my experience. While connected via a USB cable (one provided specifically for my Kindle) I found that the connection would often drop and I'd have to fiddle with the cable trying to get it to reconnect. This would happen WAY too frequently, making file transfer a frustrating, and at times impossible, task!

So I decided to try to find a way to connect wirelessly. There's quite a few apps that will do this via WiFi, Bluetooth, etc. and as I began to review them I discovered that an app I already owned had this capability - ES File Explorer.

I had been using ES File Explorer for file management on my Kindle (works GREAT for this!), mostly deleting no longer wanted images and downloaded files. Now I know that I can also use this app to view and mange my Kindle files via Bluetooth, LAN, and FTP as well.

To connect via Bluetooth to my Dell Precision 4400 laptop (running Windows XP 64-bit), after opening the ES File Explorer app, I tapped the little icon in ES File Explorer's top-left corner and chose \\"Bluetooth\\". Then I selected the \\"New\\" icon in the top bar. The app searched and detected my laptop's Bluetooth and displayed a popup with my device name (M4400LAPTOP) and a passkey. My laptop's Bluetooth then picked up on the connection and displayed a popup with the same passkey to verify the connection. I accepted the popup on my laptop and tapped the \\"Pair\\" button in the Kindle popup. I chose \\"ActiveSync\\" as the next option.

Once the two devices were connected, I went into My Computer > My Bluetooth Places on my laptop and double-clicked the icon for my Kindle. This put me into Windows File Explorer showing the folders and files on my Kindle.

Now I could treat the files onmy Kindle Fire HD just as I'm used to doing with any other files in File Explorer - copy/paste, delete, drag-and-drop, etc.

Note: If your Kindle displays a message saying that an app wants to make your Kindle discoverable by other Bluetooth devices for 300 seconds, select \\"Yes\\". I had this happen quite a few times. Apparently the Kindle (or maybe it's the ES File Explorer app) maintains the Bluetooth connection only for a period of 5 minutes at a time. If you are in the process of copying files, they will pause until you select \\"Yes\\".

File transfer from Kindle to laptop, and visa versa, is now a quick and relatively painless experience!

Thank you, ES File Explorer developers!!!

**NOTE** USE CAUTION! You'll have access to system files! If you don't know what certain folders/files are, DO NOT move, delete, etc. You could cause your device to stop functioning properly or even make it unusable!

The only files you'll likely want to handle yourself will be located in these folders on the Kindle Fire HD 8.9\\":

Documents
Download
Pictures

Any other folders and files - MODIFY AT YOUR OWN RISK!

review_headline: Fun way to review state knowledge!
review_body:
Overall, I am impressed with this game. It asks questions about state capital, landmarks, and identification of state flags. For each question correctly answered, you make a stack of states until they are high enough to pass a dotted line on the screen. The further into the game you go, the higher that line moves. You can easily move the "stackable state" from side to side, and can even rotate it, for a better position, before hitting the "drop" button. The controls were easily mastered by my 6 year old. The only improvement I would like to see I the way states are added to your success chart...I wish that as you master the information about a state, you could earn THAT particular state, not just a random one. I know, that may seem a little nit picky, but it is th only thing that could be improved upon. It worked great on my Kindle Fire HD, with NO glitches.

I originally bought this game for my son, who is in the 6th grade and doesn't do so well in geography. When I opened the game to check it out, I was worried that he would think it was "young" for him but he loved it. He plays for longer than I would have thought, all because he wants to get to the next level to open up another mini-game.

My second grader likes it too, but needs some help with reading the questions sometime. She loves trying to stack the state so that they don't fall over (sometimes I think she purposefully places them o that they will topple over!). I also find it an enjoyable way to pass a few minutes in a waiting room, etc.

I think this would be a great game for anyone ages six and up.

Hidden object games are a lot of fun and suck you in so that time disappears - IF they're good. What you need for a good hidden object game is for the objects to be well-hidden, but identifiable. The picture (I prefer photo scenes) should be clear and large enough to search without a magnifying glass.

I wasn't expecting this cartoon-like app that had many levels to solve. What I got were objects that look like cartoon style clip art. The objects aren't hidden in a room; more like piled on top of one another so you only get a glimpse of an object. Some of them are obvious, which takes the game even further down, in my estimation. I'm not saying this is more for children, although I think it would tick them off, too. I'm saying there are much better, much more realistic, much more interesting hidden object games to enjoy.

product_title: Kindergarten Kids Word Play - Match, Sight Words, Phonics and Spelling Games
review_body:
This app has four different word/phonics games meant for children at a kindergarten level. This program has been beneficial to my children who are 5 and 3.

The first game is a matching game. On one side of the screen are 4 pictures and on the other side of the screen are 4 words to match the pictures. If you tap on the picture, the program will tell you what it is. If you tap on the word, no hint is given. Jasmine (3) has not tried this game very much, but Acacia (5) has used it quite a bit. At first, Acacia would simply guess as to which word matched the picture. After a while she started looking at the first letters of the words and using those sound clues to figure out which words corresponded to which picture.

The second game is a memory game. This one is a favorite for Jasmine. There are 8 tiles to make four matches, and the child gets to flip over two at a time to try to get a match. Each tile has a very simple word on it, such as \\"it,\\" \\"as,\\" \\"me,\\" \\"are,\\" \\"all,\\" etc, The program tells the child which word is on the first tile that is flipped over, but not the second one. The child keeps flipping over tiles, two at a time, until they've found all the matches. At first Jasmine struggled with this because it was words and not pictures, but now she's much better at paying attention to the letters on each tile and finding the matches. However, when she turns over two tiles, it frustrates her (and me) that the program only tells her which word is on the first tile. She'll frequently tap the second tile as the first tile for the next match, simply to hear which word it is.

The third game is a phonics game. A picture is shown and beside it is most of the word. For instance, there may be a picture of a cat, and beside it you see \\"__at\\". Then below the word are several letters to choose from to fill in the blank, for instance: \\"c, r, s, v\\". The child needs to drag the correct letter onto the blank. If the child simply taps on the blank space, the program will tell the child which sound goes there. This game is a bit beyond Jasmine's ability but is at the right level and very appropriate for Acacia.

The fourth game in this app is a spelling game. A picture is shown and beside it are blank spaces for each letter in the word. At the bottom are each of the letters required to make the word. If you tap the picture, it will tell you what the word is. If you tap one of the spaces, it will tell you which sound goes there. The first space is highlighted and the child has to place the letters in the blanks in order. So if the word is \\"ant\\" the child has to place the a first, the n second and the t third. However the child can tap the blank spaces in any order to hear which sound goes there. This game, like the phonics game, is a little bit beyond Jasmine's level, but it is very appropriate for Acacia, and she enjoys it.pace, the program will tell the child which sound goes there. review_headline: Great App, Could Use a Few More Tweaks
review_body:
I love having the ability to track my son's assignments, grades, and hours spent. The app is very easy to use and quite functional. For basic record keeping, it is all a person would need. Included is a field trip log and a reading log, along with a place for tasks and multiple different records/reports that can be emailed to the user for printing or saving.
The useable space when typing in assignment details is a bit small (especially when assigning high school level work). It would be nice to have a bit more room. Also - other than initially entering the curriculum when you enter the subjects t be taught, it would be nice to be able to check a box next to the specific material used for specific assignments. Meaning - I use more than one curriculum for a subject. Rather than having to note the curriculum being used each time, choosing from the curricula listed for that subject in an assignment and checking a box would be nice (clear as mud, I know).
All in all, well worth the small fee. I could find no free apps (or apps for less than $5) that could compare to this one in functionality.

review_headline: Nina Chicken is back, and better than ever!!
review_body:
I loved the first ninja chicken game, and I was devastated when I finished it. But today while I was checking the free app of the day (I have a life......) I just happened to see this, you have no idea how happy I was. I would recommend this to just about anyone. The controls are easy to use, and the goal is to collect a predetermined amount of coins, acorns, and/or lay a predetermined amount of eggs. The challenge is that you have to dodge tribal dogs, as well as other obstacles. At the end of each level there is a larger dog, and you get a choice. You can either jump or slide, and the dog will also (randomly) jump or slide. If you both jump, or both slide, you will get attacked and the dog will "win" the level, however you will still pass. If you choose differently than the dog, YOU win the level!

The only reason I don't give this game 5/5 stars is the ads. They aren't too irritating, but I just don't like them. They are easy enough to deal with though. I recommend this app, it's very nice to have when you're bored, and not a game you have to commit to. I use it as a pass-time game. :)

This one offers a selection of about 20 questions and each one has 8 readings associated with a different flower, you pick a question, then a flower and you get your answer. When you're done picking flowers and choose the final option you get a list of pleasant personality traits based (presumably) on the flowers you chose.

For a free oracle app, it's not bad. The colors are a little harsh and the idea of the author only allowing certain questions is a little odd. It does have a clear exit button though so I like it!

The graphics look awesome and the game-play, while your standard tower defense game-play, is fine. The rest of the game is sort of disappointing but there is still plenty of potential here.

First off, I'd like to see the map become a little bigger, That way the developers could add more defenses for your tower instead of just a couple of arrow shooting towers. I think the magic and health upgrades could be simpler as well. Just make it like any other tower defense game where buying the upgrades gets you more health/magic and allows it to recharge faster.

Secondly, I'd like to see more playable characters as well. 3 is just a little too slim for me, I think 5-6 would be nice, Give the players some variety when playing. Also, Didn't care much for adding troops into the game because I am already 15+ waves into the game and I have yet to use them outside of the first (tutorial) wave. So the developers should either up the difficulty, which is pretty much nonexistent in the game (far too easy in my opinion) or add more enemies so that way you have to use troops, you have to upgrade them. Because at this point I have never use them and I highly doubt that I ever will.

Overall, There is certainly potential and I think that in a couple of updates the game will be quite good. Until then it will be an average. It's not a bad game, I like it, but I'd just like to see more to it.

This is a \\"formula\\" game that doesn't make much of an effort to really shine. Very pretty pictures, but the puzzles basically consist of a bunch of not-even-themed objects semi-realistically scattered over a scene. The result looks more like a rummage sale or litter than a magical place, and there is no plot to help your suspension of disbelief by providing an explanation that you are cleaning up the place or gathering needed items, as in some similar games.

Game play is equally uninspired. As other reviewers have noted, the lack of scroll and zoom, combined with high-res images make this primarily usable on tablets and large-screen phones. If you can actually see the objects, game play is solid, if conventional. I got bored before I needed to use the hint feature, so I do not know how useful it is.

Regarding permissions and security, this app wants to start at boot, and requires an Internet permission even though there is no discernable need for it in actual game play. This combination seems suspect to me, and even if it is not data mining, I don't need a game using up battery or slowing down my restarts by running when I haven't asked it to.

review_headline: Simple, entertaining gameplay, but is repetitive with poor replay value. Developer collects "analytics."
review_body:
This is a simple game with entertaining gameplay. The graphics are good - you can zoom in and out and move the course around in 3D. The object of the game is to get the flying ships from point A to point B using fans to control the direction the ships travel. The challenge is to figure out how to get them to their destination around/over various obstacles in the way. It gets more challenging as you complete more levels, but it is not too difficult. You will get different kinds of fans as you progress, like ones that lift the ships up over the cliffs/mountains/bridges instead of just changing their direction. Unfortunately thats about all there is to it... all the levels are basically the same, they just get more complicated as you progress.

Pros:
+ Nice graphics.
+ It is entertaining to figure out how to get the ships to their destination.
+ Good tutorials and hints.
+ Music is not annoying.

Cons:
- Repetitive gameplay - all the levels are pretty similar.
- Not much replay value - once you finish a level you know exactly how it needs to be set up, so playing multiple times would get pretty boring.
- Developers collects \\"analytics\\" which are not clearly defined (they say no personal information is collected however).

product_title: NYTimes - Breaking Local, National & World News
review_body:
NOTE: This is a review of the app and the news experience it provides. This isn't a commentary on the news content or the subscription price. Use your own judgement on the news content provided: That's a personal preference. It's up to you to decide whether it's too liberal or too conservative for you.

----

I have used a lot of different news apps on my Kindle Fire, and this is my second favorite so far. (Sadly, my favorite news app was discontinued, so this one is my next best choice.)

The first thing that struck me about this app is the easy-to-read home page. The home page uses a nice clear large typeface for the headlines and a smaller font for the summaries. To the right of most of the headlines is a large photo that spans half of the column. Between each headline is a good sized white margin. The sum effect of these design elements is a list of articles that is very easy on the eyes.

The top menu bar has a drop-down list of categories similar to the categories on the NYT webpage. Because this is a major news publication, the content in each of the categories is pretty extensive. And unlike some news apps that are just news aggregators, the articles are all original NYT content.

The settings are easy to access and provide some nice options. One option that I really like is the \\"Night Mode\\" viewing. Similar to the Kindle Fire's native book reading app, you can invert the text areas so that the text is white and the background is white. I use this mode when I read in bed or on an airplane. (TIP: If you fly a lot, use the Night Mode on the plane so that your screen won't glow as brightly and won't be so visible to the flight attendants. This will buy you a few more minutes of reading time before they come around and tell everyone to turn off their electronics.)

Once you are actually reading an article, it's very easy to move on to the next/previous article by swiping the screen left or right.

One feature that I wish they had is a different landscape view. Some news apps add a list of articles to the right margin when you're in landscape view. In this app switching to landscape enlarges the photo(s) and the text margins.

All in all, this is definitely a very strong news app. It's very easy to read and easy to navigate. Well done, NYT.right.

review_headline: Very Generic Looking Maze Type Game That Has Been Done Better Elsewhere
review_body:
The free paid app of the day from the Amazon App Store for June 23, 2013 is Rotate and Roll from Solverlabs.

This is a 2D maze type game where you move round looking creatures to a specific spot on the screen by rotating the screen clockwise or counter clockwise. Games of this type have been given away as the free app of the day before in both 2D and 3D environments. One example of a 2D version is Freeze! from Frozen Gun Games which had a much more HD friendly look to it.

This game is more generic looking than most games of this type. It looks rather unappealing on my Android device. The menus use way too much blue. An example of this would be dark blue numbers printed on blue buttons with a blue background on the level selection menu of this game.

As for the game itself, it is OK but it is very difficult by around level 17 and you cannot skip to higher levels unless you have defeated all the levels prior to that level. I also thought the way the balls moved around was a bit unrealistic. If you tilt the ball to go one way which is downhill, it tends to go uphill a bit in the opposite direction before going downhill. This is also a hint on how to get pass some levels since you have to go the other way a bit before going in the direction you want to go in to gain enough momentum in the right direction. I thought I'd share that hint for the game since no hints are provided in this game.

The positives on this game seem to be the lack of ads, the lack of weblinks going to other web sites, and that there is nothing that you can accidentally purchase in a very plain generic game like this one compared to fancier games of this type.

So because the game is rather generic looking and there is a lack of certain features such as a hint feature, and that this type of game has been done better several times before, I am giving this game a 2 star out of 5 star rating.

\\"Rescue Roby\\" is a cute, animated puzzle game that is based on the laws of motion and the law of gravity. But the game is much more fun than Physics class because you don't need to solve any equations to solve the puzzles. ;)

To save Roby from the factory reject pile, you need to maneuver him into a box so he can be packed and carried away by the factory's machinery. As you remove the pieces of the puzzle board, the remaining objects in the puzzle will move according to the laws of physics. If you don't solve the puzzle the first time, you just learn from your mistake(s) and just try again!

The product description for the app states: \\"While the free version offers full access to only the first chapter, the full version of Rescue Roby unlocks all 4 unique chapters.\\" So I wasn't sure what would be included in the free app of the day package. I was happy to discover that all five chapters and 70+ levels are included with the free app of the day. They are locked when you first start playing, but they are there.

The chapters in the adventure story are:

Meet Roby (with 20 adventures that are unlocked as you go)
Twice the Fun (Locked)
Miss Understood (Locked)
Hi Tech (Locked)
Love Story (Locked)

The player tries to collect all three of the gears in each adventure. As you solve each puzzle correctly, the next level is unlocked. If you want to practice, you can go back and replay the adventures you've already solved. By re-playing the level, you have an opportunity to collect the gears that you missed. Once you've collected all three gears, you can replay the level, but you cannot add to your total gears by collecting the same gears again. The adventure scoreboard shows you which adventures you've solved, and how many gears out of the three you've collected in each adventure, so you know where to focus your efforts.

The number of gears you need to collect to unlock the next chapter is tracked from the main menu page. You're told you need x/y to advance to the next chapter (where x equals the number of gears you've earned and y equals the number you need to earn to complete the challenge). For example, you may have earned 18/60, which means you've earned 18 gears out of the 60 gears available within the current chapter. The menu page also displays the number of gears you need to earn unlock the next chapter of the book.

The animated puzzles are cute, and it is fun to figure out how to make the physics work out to solve the puzzle. The music is light; it stays in the background and doesn't interfere with my concentration while I'm solving the puzzles. The puzzles have gotten more difficult as I've moved up, and some of them require quite a bit of reasoning. But I'm looking forward to solving all of the puzzles and saving Roby, and recommend the game to kids and adults.pter is tracked from the main menu page. I love Scrabble so when I saw this, it was a no-brainer -- I had to get it.  This is a really nice implementation of the game and works well on the Kindle Fire.  I have only played it in single-player mode but I am pretty impressed with that.  It includes a feature which I have not seen on other versions but which is sort of handy (though I am a little annoyed by the implementation).  The feature is a "teacher" mode in which, after you have made your play, the game informs you of what your best play would have been.  The annoying part is the way it introduces the word, with phrases like, "Now, let me show you what you missed" or "That's good, but here's how you could have earned a few more points."  They strike me as a little condescending given that the word that I missed is usually something that no one but a confirmed Scrabble addict and expert would likely know.  On the other hand, when I really do miss a word it sounds a lot like something a real teacher would say, it's an opportunity to learn some of those fancy words for a future game (sadly, it doesn't give one the definition nor usage of the word -- I learn words much more readily when I also learn how to use them), and besides -- there's not much percentage in getting cross with an AI.  The gameplay is reasonable for touchscreen and all in all, it's a lot of fun, if you like Scrabble.

Introducing DotPW to Android devices makes sense; the touch screen of my Kindle Fire HD makes interacting with a card game feel authentic, and Magic the Gathering is the type of rare, creative game that can envelop you for dozens of hours, if not hundreds.  What's more, the addition of a deck building mode was a coup, and a long-awaited addition to the series.  What keeps this game from receiving a 5-star review, however, is an unfortunate decision Wizards made concerning the replayability of this mode.  To describe the mode first:  they allow 2 separate playthroughs, each beginning with a handful of booster packs which the player opens to reveal the cards he/she will use to create a competitive deck.  The player then progresses through a campaign wherein he/she receives additional booster packs to refine it even further.  This process is very engaging and probably contains the most value in the entire game, especially for those who have played the previous titles and are accustomed to the single player campaign mode.  The problem lies with Wizards' choice to make a bit of extra money. In order to experience this immensely fun aspect of the title more than just twice, you have to pay $2.99 (or is it $1.99...  either way the point is the same) for each additional playthrough.  While an assortment of die-hard fans will certainly be willing to pay multiple times for a chance to field a competitive deck, a better way would have been to simply offer a single slot the player could erase and replay endlessly, with the option of saving a particularly good deck for the same price it now costs to purchase a new playthrough.  Like your deck?  Save it for a small price, and then go back to playing and replaying the sealed deck mode for hours on end.  If they had decided such, more people would spend money to save their potent decks, more people would play their game for longer, and ultimately the sealed deck mode would become the driving force of the franchise in the future.  Today's gamers want the opportunity to be endlessly creative, and while the excitement of the sealed deck mode offers them the chance, the money-grasping feel of their first rendition leaves it all tasting sour.

review_headline: An improvement on the first game different enough and without some of the glitches
review_body:
I really enjoyed the first game, despite its tendency to occasionally reboot on the Kindle Fire, wiping out all progress.

The sequel does not have that reboot issue, is not a straight rehash of the original, and it has several features to keep it interesting once a player has defeated all 50 waves of zombies.

When playing the waves one uses one of three different hero characters rather than just the samurai from the first game. Each has particular strengths and weaknesses.

The allies available are expanded from the first game, and a player can acquire (by using gold coins or finding the right \\"mystery box\\" in the game) stronger \\"champion\\" versions of each ally.

There is also a multiplayer mode that allows for head to head confrontation against other players. Other players are attacked to acquire upgrades, and upgrades that have been acquired may need to be defended - be prepared for that.

Finally, there is the daily challenge. There are a limited number of these, not a brand new one every day.

The only major issue I have here is the cost to buy the Sorceress hero - $54.99.
I enjoyed this game enough to buy $20 worth of gold coins to use in the game, but the price for the sorceress is not something that I am willing to pay. That said, the sorceress character is not required, and I have had a lot of fun anyway.

review_headline: Core game is incredibly addictive; Good Android port
review_body:
Slay is a balanced and addictive game that gives a much more satisfying strategy experience than just about anything else available on Android. It seems a little pricy compared to similar games, but chances are you'll get much more value out of this game than most free or 99 cent games. For someone like me who enjoys world conquest games like Risk and Civilizations, but doesn't have much time, Slay really helps to scratch the world domination itch. http://www.hardcoredroid.com/slay-review/

As for the Android port, it gets the job done on my Kindle Fire, but the UI could be a little more intuitive. It's not clear at the beginning that you change to other sets of maps/difficulties via side swipes. Your progress on an individual map is saved if you hit the back button, but the game doesn't tell you. But once you take the time to get familiar with it, you will not be disappointed!

5 stars for the core game, 4 stars for the port = 4.5 stars (round up to 5)

review_headline: Terrific App for VFR Pilots AND a Great Bargain
review_body: This app is absolutely the best bargain in aviation software anywhere and does most of the things the $1300 Garmin Aero GPS a friend of mine has, for a tiny fraction of the price. You pick out your destination and the waypoints you plan to fly, and a line is drawn from where you are now to where you want to go.  It should be noted that this is NOT an app for IFR use. It's strictly for VFR flying only. Bearing + Distance USA has an enormous database of VOR's, VFR Reporting Points, Waypoints, NDB's and Airports to access and utilize to create your flightplan and a variety of maps to use including standard FAA VFR charts. I can't think of anything a VFR pilot would need that this app doesn't have. I've used it extensively in my flying and it's navigation capabilities are extremely accurate. Highly recommended.

review_headline: Organizing your Kindle Fire HD Carousel and apps
review_body:
This a fantastic app!! Even through the carousel is much better on the Kindle Fire HD than the previous Kindle Fire, the Kindle Fire HD Carousel would still get overloaded with apps before getting this app. I love the way you can create folders for your apps or have an app show up in 2 or more folders if that is what you want. This is helpful when it is hard to decide which folder an app should reside in. It is easy to create or rename folders and move apps to the folders. The all apps folders show which folders the apps are in. You can easily rearrange the order of folders and assign icons for your folders. Another thing I like is when to have two versions of a app (paid and the free version)you can put the app version you want to use in one folder and the other app version you no longer want to use and can't uninstall in another folder. Since getting GoToApp Full app I have saved a lot of time and energy in not having to remove previously used apps showing up on the carousel or finding a specific app. I now use GoToApp Full to access my Kindle apps and now reserve the Kindle Fire HD Carousel for items such as a book or magazine I am reading in addition to the GoToApp Full app. I wish that Amazon loaded this app when they shipped the Kindle Fire HD.

This app will not prevent an app from showing up in the carousel when the is a new app is installed or when an app is updated.

review_headline: Five Star App for Songwriters! Brilliant! *****
review_body:
I usually don't write reviews, but, this little Android application was so good that I felt I needed to share. This app allows you to create chord progressions with piano, drums, bass, organ, etc., and it actually sounds VERY GOOD! Other reviewers have gone into the details more thoroughly than I will, but, I will say that you can vary so many things about your progression, such as a choice of over a dozen piano arpeggio variations.

This program is very easy to use. You DO need to know a little chord theory, but, that's about it. I have several music-production Android apps, and this is THE ONE that sounds so good. At first I used this app to practice improvising guitar solos across different progressions, but, it is also good for vocalists, and others.

What really distinguishes this app is the quality of the sound; it has great tonal quality. Sometimes I can compose songs with nothing but this and my Klipsch headphones. It is really great.

Crafty Crates is a challenging little game. At first it looks like an all-too-familiar casual game, but it doesn't take long to realize it's not just a new version of that at all. It plays more like a cross between Bejeweled and Tetris and this still doesn't quite describe it.

Crates rise from the bottom and move at a steady pace toward the top of the screen. You may only move crates sideways, but you can match three vertically or horizontally. As the crates rise and you level, new crates are added. These new crates create new challenges in matching--the more types of crates, the quicker you have to work to make your matches. There is no penalty for making a switch that doesn't make a match and crates can be dropped into empty slots. There's a preview of upcoming crates at the bottom, if you can keep track of all of that while keeping your crates from hitting the top of the screen. A loss was far from frustrating for me--it just made me want to try again.

You compete against yourself for higher scores. I wasn't quite sure how the leveling and scoring system worked, but if that's the only complaint, I can live with it. The graphics are bright and cute. The volume of music and sound effects is controllable. A well-balanced casual game that's extremely addictive to play.

It will be a convenient tool that will allow me to get back up to speed and quickly resharpen my skills. I will be able to use this app at work.

The most useful feature for me, however, is that it gives me a more portable device for performing quick \\"what if\\" analysis calculations. I usually plug the numbers into an Excel spreadsheet. But that can be inconvenient and it ties me to my desk. This is much nicer!

Finally, on a practical note, I will use this in my day-to-day life, especially when shopping. (Update - the app includes a calculator.)

review_headline: Decades of revealed doctrine, in many different languages, in your pocket
review_body: If you download all the content, it's almost like carrying a copy of the lds.org website in your pocket. Okay, not that much. But the amount of content available is enormous, from the scriptures to general conference going back decades to an entire suite of church manuals, and having it in several different languages is a big plus. Tapping on footnotes in the scriptures will take you to the referenced passage. The ability to highlight passages in the app and then sync it with your lds.org account is not something I currently use, but I can see how it would be useful. It is also regularly updated with the monthly editions of the church magazines. A really great resource to keep handy with you.

review_headline: kind of enjoyable to use, but ads are obnoxious
review_body:
The variety of brush styles is fun to play with. Drawing with my finger was more responsive than I'd expected (this was on a Google 7 tablet). The permissions seem reasonable enough (the network perms would be needed for any app that provides posting to Facebook or displays a stream of ads, as this one does).

But those ads -- they're up at the top and fairly out of the way, but they are constantly scrolling and popping a new one up, and it gets REALLY distracting. Maybe it wouldn't be so bad in a fast action game, but when you're drawing, you want calm and a chance to reflect on what to do next -- an opportunity you just don't get with this app.

And when you exit, it splashes a full-screen version of one of the ads, just as an extra little unpleasantness.

Sad to say, I'll probably uninstall and hope that a less-pushy drawing app comes along.

The only reason I gave this app 3 stars was because I did like playing it. I'm not very good with crosswords, though, so I may be a bit jaded. I thought it was weird the clues were in the puzzle. It took me a moment to realize that the clues were normally in the squares that would be black in normal squares. Even then, some clues that went across also went down, so sometimes it was hard to guess how many letters were in one word at a glance. However, what was more annoying was the fact that because some went down, it was hard to try to guess some words. But, with the clues that said it was like (enter number), there were no numbers on the squares so you have to click the clue to get the number.

I didn't like the movement of the puzzle either. Zooming in and out was fine and so was moving it up and down. But, when entering a clue, you can't move the puzzle. It made having the game zoomed out so you can see the whole crossword annoying when in the bottom half.

I think there are quite a few things this developer can do to make the game a lot more fun. Then there was the ads. I don't mind bottom/top ads in games, but when you get popup ads in the game--a paid game, it's not only annoying, it's pointless. Free games have ads because it helps make the game free--but when people pay for a game, then there's no need for ads because the developer is making money already.

This is a great Sudoku app for Android. I already had Sudoku Works on my Kindle so when this app showed up for my Android phone, I had to have it. It is similar but doesn't have all the features of the Kindle version. The app offers an unnumbered Daily puzzle of Medium difficulty and individually selectable numbered puzzles in five degrees of difficulty from Very Easy to Devious. The Help directions are easy to follow and you can select options (or not) to make play as close to paper and pencil as possible or to give you enough help so that you can solve a puzzle without really thinking.

The major problem, and the reason I can't give it five stars, is how it handles puzzles after they have been started and/or completed and how performance is recorded. If you suspend a puzzle, you cannot then switch to work on another puzzle and you can't abandon it except by showing the solution, going to the main menu and clicking Completed, and then deleting it from the list. You would expect suspended puzzles to be put on the Resume queue. Instead, the 20 most recently played puzzles (according to the Help) are available there to be continued or removed. However, any of the Completed Puzzles can be Restarted to play again or removed from that list. Additionally, the Resume queue lists some puzzles multiple times with the same Time and Started data and some puzzles with questionable Time data. If you remove every puzzle from the Resume queue, the next time you start the app there will be a whole new list of puzzles to select.

The Time figures recorded in the Completed list make complete sense. 2:22 for a Very Easy puzzle and 29:48 for a Devious puzzle are reasonable figures. But 410:12:11 in the Resume queue for a Devious puzzle, started the previous day, is a mystery to me. Furthermore, the performance data doesn't record the completion time at all. What I'm really interested in is when I completed a puzzle (date and time) and how long I spent solving it.

It's an annoyance. I just basically ignore the Resume button since the puzzles on that list can be accessed from the Completed puzzles list. If Oak would fix this so that it made sense, this app would get five stars from me. Since it is optimized for the Kindle Fire, that may be a reason it doesn't work as well on the phone. Otherwise, is a fun app.

review_headline: I was surprised by how much I like this one!
review_body: Yahtzee is one of my favorite games of all time. This one is an interesting take on traditional Yahtzee with the addition of a sixth dice - a concept I was resistant to as I'm a creature of habit and I love traditional Yahtzee. Then I started playing and much to my surprise found this one to be a lot of fun. It takes a bit to get used to the new scoring system (ie: a "full house" is 4x2 instead of the traditional 3x2) but once you've got the scoring figured out it's not bad. I like how each number on the dice has its own unique color so they're easy to spot on smaller screens. The interface is not overly cluttered and game play is easy. I've gotten quite a bit of play out of this one. Great game.

*My experience with this game is on a Kindle Fire HD*
The game is a great way to pass a little time. They keep it interesting by giving you mission and specific things to grab for. There's also a list of collections, which can be turned in for advantages such as double coins and more energy.
You are limited to 20 grabs. As you earn points and complete missions, your rewarded with extras. The grabs also regenerate one grab every 50 seconds (this is while in-game. When your not playing it's one grab every 15 minutes) I can typically get about 30 mins of play time before I run out of grabs. At that point you have the option to either buy more or wait for them to build back up. I personally refuse to spend real money on it, so I wait until it fills back up.
The biggest downfall is their placement of ads. Just a little while ago, I was playing the game, and I opened up my collections tab. And right at the top was an ad for Geiko, covering the 'back' button! So I have no way to get back to the play screen. I'm waiting a bit to see if it goes away. If not, I'll be editing this review and giving them 1 star.
Lastly, I did have the game crash once. I had to remove it and add it back on. It was pretty frustrating, because I lost all my progress.
Overall, the game is amusing. If your just looking to kill some time here and there, then this might be something you'd enjoy. But if your someone who likes to spend hours playing, and focuses on leveling up, I'd pass on this one.

review_headline: Forget the mystery - it's all about the puzzles
review_body:
First off, this game is enjoyable, but not as a Crime Adventure. It has lots of visual puzzles, which mostly involve finding objects on the screen while a clock ticks down. There are also a few scrambled word puzzles, and jigsaw type puzzles. Solving each of these puzzles allows you to see a little more of a story (with many misspelled words). I was hoping for a Nancy Drew type game, where you look for clues that are relevant to the story and help you solve a mystery, but that's not what this game does. The story is incidental to this game and the player has no choices to make or inferences to make. That said, the puzzles are progressively more challenging, and once you stop caring about the story you can have a good time.

Pros: exercises your powers of observation and jigsaw puzzle skills
Cons: No detective skills needed. Many misspelled words in story.

review_headline: if you just want a simple stopwatch, look no further!
review_body:
I needed something for my Kindle Fire with a stopwatch function...I searched on Amazon only to find that there are 1000's of apps that can or also function like a timer. The problem here is that I know today that my new app has the stopwach function - but what are the odds I'll remember that in a month or two? or six?? No mistakes with this little guy!!
Its strongest selling point is its simplicity - it has all the features that a basic hand-held stopwatch would have - and very little else. You can customize it plenty, but you won't get bogged down with millions of options you'll probably never use.
Also, I love how it can run in the background - I can set it up and turn my Kindle off altogether, then turn it back on hours later to check it - all while running other apps simultaneously.

review_headline: it use to be 5 star, but recent upgrade slowed game waaaay down.
review_body:
There are some very good things, some great things, some just OK things, and some bad things about this game.

I'll start with the great.

The artistry is fantastic. The animations are clever. The little extras made this game very entertaining. For instance, one must visit other villages to earn hearts to buy special items that can only be bought with hearts. And while you are visiting neighbors, you have an opportunity to make coins by playing \\"Where's Waldo \\" except you're looking for Scrat. He hides behind palms, or in plain sight, and when you find him quickly you are rewarded more coins. The amount you win depends on the neighbors level. You win 100 coins multiplied by the level number. For example, find Scrat in a level 50,and win 5000 coins. Find him quickly and win 2500 PLUS the 5000. HOWEVER...here's the bad. I haven't been able to connect with anyone I have tried to friend. I have tried over 20 times to friend my sister and we haven't connected..ever. I've tried game loft live connect...nothing. I visit MANY villages, get lots of coins...but I haven't gotten any gifts or likes in return. I am level 62.
Furthermore, the update that now includes the underground DinoWorld has slowed and bogged down all aspects of game, making it tedious instead of fun. Difficult to rearrange animals and decorations because moving buttons don't work.

- Doesn't work, this is the biggest issue. I'll have 20% of my battery remaining, but 4 of the 6 hearts are full*.
- Can't alter the size, the size is either 1x1 or 1x2, this makes the gauge very small and ugly.
- Have to delete the widget just to change anything, this is very annoying.

If you are after something like this, I highly suggest the Battery Health Bar on the Google Play Store, it's accurate, lets you add up to 20 hearts and a plethora of styles. Best of all, IT'S FREE.

*Now, a very big issue here is that each heart segment only breaks down to half a heart, so it's either a full or half which results in a total of 12 segments (if you're using the 1x2). Even if the meter was accurate, that means each segment would have a very wide range, which is not desirable.

So if you want a battery meter, get the Battery Health Bar. So much better and cooler (copy and paste 'Battery Health Bar' into Google).

product_title: MY LITTLE PONY - Friendship is Magic
review_headline: Fun game - But Dont Buy Gems
review_body:
The game is entertaining if not very imaginative. The core of the game requires building stores and staffing them with ponies to earn bits. With bits you can buy more stores and more ponies - though certain ponies require gems that cost real money.

There are several flaws with the game. First certain ponies that are required to complete the game must be purchased with real money. Second the two pony training games are extremely repetitive - even my 4 year old daughter got tired of them after two weeks. Thirdly the elements of harmony required to complete the game accrue incredibly slowly - it will take months to complete this game.

All of these flaws could be overlooked except for the fact that it periodically loses game state when you close the game. This could be as simple as losing the last bits you collected or as bad as losing gems you just bought.

In the latest case I lost the entire Ponyville I had helped my daughter build over several weeks - a large investment of time and perhaps thirty dollars. What a waste.

The app also has a community feature where I can see who is meditating with me at the same time all over the world. I can encourage them, and they can encourage me.

There are different singing bowl sounds to sound the beginning, intervals, or ending of the meditation, and all can be set to my desired sound and volume.

This is a fantastic App for children (and even adults if they like these kind of games). The graphics are very realistic and extremely cute. When you start out, you begin with hamsters and guinea pigs and then you move on to bunnies, and so on. You begin by getting water for the animals, then you feed them, remove waste and a host of other things.

NEVER HAVE TO BUY VIRTUAL CREDITS!

First of all and maybe best of all, this App does not require purchase of credits to play the game. How refreshing! No worries about children running up a tab on your Amazon account (either by accident or on purpose). Folks won't feel deprived if they can't afford special items/privileges that must be purchased.

TEACHES RESPONSIBILITY

I think this App is appropriate for children because it teaches responsibility. It might be tedious for some folks. The concept is to regularly take care of your animals to prepare them for adoption.

GETTING AROUND/GRAPHICS

It takes some getting used to to get familiar with the 3D rooms, animal pens, water well, etc. 3D graphics are excellent. I suggest that the developers create a map to help players discover where things are.

DECORATIONS/MULTIPLE LANGUAGES

This App has updates every so often that add seasonal decorations. This App can be played in several languages, so there is a tremendous global appeal factor there.

DAILY PLAY

There is a limit as to how long a player may continue to play (daily till 4:00 pm). Some reviewers do not like this limit, but I think it is very wise/thoughtful of developers because your eager children will not be playing at all hours.

FINAL OPINION:

Overall this is a beautiful App. It could be tedious for some, but the tasks are simple. This App teaches kindness and responsibility. Perfect for your aspiring veterinarian!!rfect for your aspiring veterinarian!!

this is my second mahalo guitar-learning app with instructor jen trani. i LOVE this series of apps. they are very easy to use and navigate, and the instruction is systematic and broken down into very manageable pieces. each chapter contains a number of lessons and you can either watch the embedded youtube videos or download the videos as you need them, and then remove them from the device when you no longer do. you can mark each lesson as \\"complete\\" so it's very easy to keep track of your progress.

\\"master rhythm guitar\\" is a really wonderful, thorough overview of rhythm guitar. jen starts by breaking down rhythm and teaching you how to count and how to understand different time signatures (although she uses chord charts and tab, and never makes you actually read music.) after that, she teaches various rhythm techniques such as anticipation, scratching, palm muting, etc. then the techniques are applied to a wide variety of different styles.

this app is helping me to master the basics and get a taste of what all different rhythms are like to play. my understanding of rhythm and my playing ability have improved noticeably from systematically working through the lessons in this app. i can work through one to six of them in a day, and i practice what i learn in each one until i have it down, before moving on. my confidence has grown a lot, and so has my ability to just pick up the guitar and start strumming out of the blue.

i am also (simultaneously) working through \\"learn fingerpicking\\" (also with jen trani) and i plan to move on to the guitar soloing app after i've finished these two courses (or maybe before i finish.) for two dollars you really cannot go wrong using this app. i have taken online guitar lessons from a number of different instructors and i will tell you that jen trani is definitely one of the best! i have also taken \\"real\\" guitar lessons, but those have drawbacks too. sometimes teachers are intimidating, or they don't teach in a systematic way at all. jen is definitely not intimidating, and she manages to teach to different levels at the same time. i only wish there were more of these guitar courses with her.teach in a systematic way at all. jen is definitely not intimidating, and she manages to teach to different levels at the same time. i only wish there were more of these guitar courses with her.

review_body:
I sort of wish I never downloaded this. It's a cute game, but it sucks you into to forking out major bucks. If you want to recruit certain girls, you have to have gems to unlock them. So I get some and then the only way to recruit her is to buy things that can ONLY be bought with more gems and outrageous amounts at that. I totally wasted money buying gems to unlock a girl because there's no way I'm spending $20-$100 to recruit one girl for a game. Get real developers. There should at least be a way to recruit a \\"special\\" girl with play money once you unlock her. I feel robbed.

EDIT: After months of playing this game I decided to quit. There are so many bugs it has become unplayable. The Pocket Gems developers are woefully neglectful of Kindle users. Others who have this app on Apple devices have many features Kindle users do not have. My last bug issue was reported over a month ago and still hasn't been fixed. Due to this this lack of attention to Kindle users I've dropped my rating to one star. It's a shame because I really did enjoy several features of the game. It has potential if the developers take time to fix and update this app for Kindle users. Until then don't bother with this game. Money you spent WILL be wasted!

review_headline: App won't authenticate! Customer support won't help!!!
review_body:
Since I've been a Newsweek subscriber for years, I decided to stick with them when they transitioned to the all-digital format. I dutifully installed the Kindle app, obtained my user name/password and successfully read the first digital issue (albeit through a rather klunky Kindle interface that is an obvious "version 1.0"). However, the second time I tried to login to the Kindle app, using the same user name/password, I got an "Authentication Failed" message! I checked and double-checked my password. It was correct. I tried changing the password through the apps "Change Password" feature. I got an email confirmation with a new password. After typing in the new password, I still got the extremely useless "Authentication Failed" message! I emailed customer support over a week ago and, other than an automated reply, have heard NOTHING back!

This app, and the customer "support" backing it, is completely atrocious! (Even if this "Authentication Failed" issue gets solved, why on earth does the app make me type in my entire user name/password each time!?! Can't it "remember" my credentials like every other app?!
