product_title: Calorie Counter and Diet Tracker by MyFitnessPal
review_body: Those are the three E's of my fitness pal Calorie Counter. I installed it on my Kindle, but I can also use it on my laptop without worrying about syncing.  The account logs in automatically, but works just as fine when I'm offline with a smaller set of food.  I was surprised how expansive their food list is.  I think fellow users enter the data.  I'm not sure how accurate that makes it, but so far I haven't cared.  I'm not into tracking every little calorie. I can easily find a food choice that is "close enough" to the food I want to record, and I keep track with little trouble.  The best feature is that when you're done logging the day, the Calorie counter will tell you how much you will weigh in 5 weeks if every day were like that day.  VERY helpful in understanding how my little food deviations from the plan impact my ability to lose weight.  Also helpful is the ability to quickly see the impact of food choices on projected weight loss and satisfying my appetite.  I think I could eat just as much, but by choosing other foods, still lose weight.  I was very encouraged by this app, and my wife and other coworkers are now using it too.  You'll like it.

review_headline: Horrible Execution of Digital Content - Shame
review_body:
I have been a subscriber of Newsweek for the past 5 years, and for the most part found the publication interesting and worth the money. This joke of a electronic version of Newsweek is neither.

Each \\"digital magazine\\" is a simple page-by-page scan. This, along with an interface apparently designed by a high school freshman who just learned about making \\"e-zines\\", means several very bad things:
1) The files are extremely large (75mb+ / issue)
2) There is no pinch to zoom (which for my 4\\" smartphone screen is a no-go)
3) You can't resize/reflow the text since it's an image
4) The tiny little nav buttons at the top are so small I literally could not click them
5) Going from page to page is laggy

Sad to say I will be canceling my subscription. You were awesome, Newsweek. Until this piece of crap app I felt sorry that you were going away. Now I say good riddance.

While this is probably a worthwhile app if you live in one of the major metropolitan areas the app focuses on, if you live just outside those areas the results you get may be... interesting.  For example, I never knew it was possible to actually walk from my current home in Virginia (south of Washington D.C.) to my last home in Maryland (just north of the D.C. line) and cover the entire 62.4 miles in just a little over 18 hours, but according to this app, I can!  For some strange reason the app utterly ignores the Virginia Railway Express (VRE) commuter trains even though you tell it to use trains and subways.  And even then, once it gets you to an area where you can get a subway, bus, or other public transportation, it ignores them and has you continue walking.  In my theoretical trip above, it ignored the VRE and had me walk up US 1 to D.C., then ignored the Metro and the buses and had me walk all the way to Silver Spring, MD.  Very, very odd!  But, if you start your trip inside one of the areas the app covers it seems to work perfectly.  It gave correct directions for trips within NYC (where I lived and worked for more than 35 years), and correct info for trips inside Washington, D.C.  Take its recommendations/directions from outside the built-in areas with a large grain of salt... maybe an entire salt lick...

It seems there is quite a bit of information available that the reader must known how to access rather than just being intergrated with whatever bible is being read. Am I missing something? Perhaps I am spoiled by MySword on my mobile which intergrates navigation to other documents and back to your spot in the bible seemlessly with ribbons at the top and bottom of the screen. This game is pretty simple. Tap somewhere on the screen to shoot. It's similar to the old arcade shooting game Time Crisis. You spend a lot of time in cover and pop out to shoot enemies. At the same time, the enemies are shooting at you, but they are poor shots, like Storm Troopers in Star Wars. Going back to the Time Crisis analogy, only certain shots will hit you, and those are surrounded by giant red rings, obvious "Danger! Danger! Duck and cover!" signs. So stop shooting and you go back in cover and the shot misses you. Or you can time your shot right to hit the enemy shot to deflect it. You also reload your gun by going into cover. When you get hit, you lose armor. You are wearing a helmet and an armor vest. That means you can take two hits. Take another and you die. Certain "rescue the hostage" scenarios can replenish your armor, or give you other perks. There are 4 modes of gameplay, basic story version, you proceed through missions to a boss fight then go on to another location where you go through missions to a boss fight, and one more time. You can rank up by obtaining achievements. You also earn coins while playing. You spend coins to buy new weapons, costumes, and supplies, like "continues" and super ammo. Overall, a very fun an entertaining game.

Here are a few tips for the basic game mode:
1 - The shotgun is a good deal, relatively cheap and powerful, downside is one shot then reload.
2 - If you die, don't bother using the continue if you are not on a boss fight. It costs 500 coins. Just start again at the beginning of the mission. In the long run you'll earn more coins to buy better guns and perks to make fighting the boss easier.
3 - Save your superarmor perks for the boss fights. This combined with a powerful gun makes the boss fights much easier.

This is a great crosswords app! Granted, these puzzles aren't really difficult, but there are enough tough(ish) clues to keep it interesting. It is British English, as noted by other reviewers, but that only adds to the interest. (If you want US English, this developer makes a version like that, as well.) At this time, there are 300 puzzles (great deal for 99 cents) and the developer says there may be even more to come, at no charge. (I have seen from other reviews, that they have already done this once, or twice.) The puzzles are separated into \\"packs\\" and the puzzles seem to get a bit harder as one advances through the pack.

The game play is very simple and there are options to check answers and to show how you want clues displayed, etc. The graphics are fine - nothing flashy, but I am actually thankful for that. There are just two little things that I wish were different. Sometimes, I get a message that my \\"unplayed\\" puzzles are \\"locked.\\" To get around this, exit the game and come back. Also, I wish they could lift the keyboard up a bit, as I sometimes hit icons on the menu bar at the bottom. Those are just two small concerns, not even enough to remove a star from the rating. This is a great game that I highly recommend.

review_headline: Fantastic! Single or Multiplayer, It's Just Plain Ol' Fun!  Finally, Something Original
review_body: There's sooooooo many copycat games out there that just aren't worth the download, let alone all the effort that goes into programming them in the first place.  Caps takes a simple game we all know, and elevates it to the next level, which is exactly what a good app needs to do.  The graphics look really good; I believe they were hand drawn, because clearly a lot of thought and time went into planning each and every level.  The game is challenging, without being needlessly cumbersome.  The controls work very well -- you can adjust the force behind your shots, so they can be subtle or slide across the table with full force. Playing against the computer actually works really well. The computer player is no slouch, but if you think it through, he is beatable, so that keeps the game challenging and interesting. The higher the level, the more interesting the table top gets, with different obstacles and objects. It's fun to knock them off the table. It would be neat though if they added another element of watching the stuff smash when it fell off the table and hit the floor. But that's beside the point, just playing against your opponent and trying to get their caps off the table before yours, is fun enough, in and of itself. You can even customize the designs on your caps with the extra graphics. Playing against online opponents works well too. And best of all, people usually play caps in real life when they're drunk, but with this app, you don't have to deal with any annoying alcoholics, well, at least not in person anyway. This is a real fun app; and with all the crappy ones out there, it's nice to find a good one every now and again.

review_headline: Bubbles Touch? More Like Marble Explosions...
review_body: I downloaded this game as a Free App of the Day, because I've always liked bubble popper games and I figured it was worth a try. However, despite the name \\"Bubbles Touch\\", it's not really like bubbles touching... It's more like stone balls EXPLODING in your face. Which isn't a bad thing; it's definitely a good thing! I just can't understand why the developers are selling it as a classic bubble popper when it's so much more. The mechanics are like a bubble popper, sure, and the object is to clear the screen. However, the balls roll and clink together more like solid stone balls than bubbles (which is awesome) and they don't pop, so much as they literally explode (which is even awesomer). The bonuses don't come from exploding the balls that hold the bonuses... they come from exploding the ball chains ABOVE the bonus balls, so they will fall down (intact!) into your reservoir. Took me a few levels to really catch on to the way that plays out, but I find it much more challenging and a great addition to this game! So I nabbed this game, figuring it would be a typical bubble popping game - and got something far more interesting! Definitely worth the $1 price the game usually goes for.

Best alarm I have found.
So many settings! It is overwhelming at first, but once you get it dialed in, it is amazing.
I have mine start 5 mins before I want to wake up, it begins with tiny trickles of water and slowly gets louder over the 5 mins (the screen also starts to slowly get brighter). At the alarm time, I have mine start playing the theme from Braveheart, nice and flutey, not jarring at all. If I haven't turned it off after 5 mins after the alarm time, the "safe alarm" begins, which is the typical buzzer sound and max volume. Yikes!
Using it for almost a year now. Husband likes it too, he used to always hit snooze 3 times in a row as he "progressively woke up". Now that he wakes up gradually (it's like you don't register that there is sound, you just slowly come to), he gets up at the first alarm and is noticeably less groggy. I know it would be the same with any gradual alarm system, but this one is the best of the 5 or so that I tried.

review_headline: Controls Not Optimal And Unclear Objective Make This One Just OK
review_body:
So Amazon's Cyber Monday Deals Week is winding down and today we get Duke Nukem 3D as today's choice for the free app of the day.

I got this app free today, and I will mention that I have not played Duke Nukem before. The reason I mention this is because there is usually an expectation that this Android version of this game will match that of the other original versions. In most cases, the original will probably be superior to the recreation. In this case it most likely is as this type of game would probably be more suited for joystick play.

Like at least one of the other reviewers pointed out, they should have had the 2nd virtual joystick as the default setting since it makes it much easier to move around and see around you.

Another major problem I have is that there is a lack of instructions to this game such as what are you trying to accomplish besides killing any mutated people or whatever they are supposed to be. Is there someone you are trying to rescue? Are you trying to survive until a certain time? There is no clear objective in this game that I can find.

With the physical limitations come mental limitations. I am no longer on the job and using my mind on a minute to minute basis. I hardly use it at all due to not working plus the part of my illness that zaps my energy and leaves me unable to even read for a few minutes. review_headline: A simple but fun space defense game that you will enjoy for a short time killer!
review_body:
Game Play:
When game play starts you choose your players faction (one of three) and your ship design (one of three). Each ship has an advantage like shields or power. If the tutorial is on then you can start. You click on a ship on the right to target an enemy or click on an object in a sector grid. Shoot at a target with either phasers (Phasers use a lot of the ship's power) or torpedoes using buttons located on the left and right of the screen. Enemies have a red dot and allies have a green dot.

On the left of the screen you have a button for Galaxy that shows you the number of enemies in the sector. Don't forget to loot the ships you destroy by tapping them. As you play your mission button will flash. You may have to go and help a ship that is under attack.

This game is a cross between battleship and a grid defense game. You are seeking out enemies to destroy but in reality you are getting a distress call so many times you are basically just rescuing other friendly ships. Right before you are destroyed you almost always destroy the enemy ship. One key is that after you fire your weapons then quickly move the ship to avoid incoming torpedoes. Phasers cannot be avoided as they are instantaneously hitting you. Do not shoot the suns, planets of other objects as the resulting possible explosion can damage your ship or destroy it. You can hail and go to supply stations and replenish supplies to repair your ship. You can also visit planets to gain supplies or take shore leave. You can get power from a nearby nebula.

The graphics are nice but basic. And the sound effects and voices are clear and understandable.

Main screen:
* Launch
* Settings - enter your name or leave it as Human, sounds, tutorial, missions enabled, torpedo collision with objects and set difficulty level from 1 to 9.
* Reset
* Abort - exit

What I like:
The concept of a star trek game is nice and the game is simple enough to play and master. You get so many distress calls that you are kept busy saving your allies.

I also like that there are no permissions in the game.

What I don't like:
The game is almost too simple and it quickly becomes repetitive in what you are doing.

Summary:
The game is a time killer but not high action and children will probably not care for it. After you clear out some sectors it does get repetitive. I rate this game as a 4 star simple time killer but it will not become my favorite game. I like the fact it has no permissions and is small so it doesn't use a lot of memory space.

This is a good concept but it is so simply designed. It could easily be upgraded with better graphics and more action and become a much improved game. It is free so you should get it and play a few rounds. It is at least worth that much fun for you Star Trek fans.

review_headline: Good retro graphics but with some control issues when playing on a touch screen!
review_body:
Game play:
The first thing you see is a notice that this game uses Amazon Game Circle but you can select it to be off, just do not turn it on if you don't want it.

There are multiple scenarios like;
* Weapon of Mass Destruction 54 levels
* The Blocks Cometh 30 levels
* Welcome to the Jungle 30 levels
* Enter the Dragon 30 levels
* The Impossible Missions 18 levels
* Lite Missions 7 levels

Every scenario has the first level unlocked so you can begin there. The graphics are simple like the old Atari style. The object is to kill all of the scientists and the fights are very gory and bloody with flying heads and blood. The second level already increases the difficulty factor a lot. In addition if you have the ghosts on then as soon as the man starts running all of your failed attempts start running and jumping on the screen and cluttering the game playing area. They are very distracting. Turn off the ghost in the settings to stop seeing them.

You also get armed guards who shoot to kill so get them first, avoid them if possible or die.

Main screen:
* Start game
* Statistics
* Settings - Ghosts, Gore, Auto-retry, music volume, SFX volume.
* More games - provides you links to Twitter, Facebook, email, Amazon App Store, and League of Evil Free download
* ? - credits

What I like:
The game action is OK but the controls are hard to master as the touch screen itself is hard to hold the device while pressing on both sides of the screen. The game is playable but for me too repetitious. There are a lot of levels and they do change the challenge quite a bit. The graphics are simple but adequate and more of a retro concept.

What I don't like:
The main issue for me was using a touch screen as a controller for this type of game. The developer has done the best job he possibly could but for me it is just awkward. This game with a joystick and monitor would be great but having to hold the device and use the controls adds to the difficulty and frustration of the game. If this game were on a screen and you had a joystick you wouldn't have to be holding the screen at the same time.

This is a pretty fast action game as you have to focus with minimal distractions. The game also got very hard quickly and I cannot imagine playing through over 160 levels. It is so easy to die that you will get frustrated.

Don't forget to turn off your WIFI because of the links to the social media sites and Amazon if you let your children play this game. If you have a phone then put your phone into airplane mode so the transmitter is turned off. You might also turn off the gore in the settings.

Summary:
The game play is good but gory but of course you can turn off the gore. Do yourself a favor and turn off the ghost option also. It just clutters the screen in my opinion and makes the game hard to play.

Graphics = good retro 5 stars
Action = good 4 stars
Using a touch screen as the control interface = 3 stars
Frustration factor = 3 stars

review_headline: Best Kindle Fire productivity app I have found!

review_headline: Good single or multiple student opposite flashcards, but takes up a lot of space
review_body:
Opposites Fun Deck provides you with access to all of Super Duper Opposite flashcards on you Android device. Like many of the recent Super Duper apps, this one provides the student with a choice of 2 words (e.g., \\"full\\" or \\"empty\\") to complete a sentence.
All of the Super Duper flashcard apps provide a high quality audio of the flashcard option if it is touched. Their apps work great for single student or multiple students at the same time. The data can be sent in an email when completed. The data for the email is created in an html file which is saved on the device/SD card. This app is currently sending the data as an html attachment and not within the email.
For some reason this app is not storing itself on the SD card of my devices. It takes up over 14 MB of space on your device. All of the other Super Duper flashcard apps I have tested store most of app on the SD card by default, so if you have an device with and SD card, you have more room for other apps and stuff. Kindle Fires do not have SD cards so it doesn't matter for them.
I am giving this app 3 stars until it is updated to send the data within the email and store itself on the SD card; otherwise it works well. I would recommend using this app for preschool and lower elementary students.

review_headline: Essential Kindle reading app, but some suggestions
review_body:
I read my Kindle books via my tablet computers and smartphone. The Kindle reading app is therefore the only way I access my library.

For the most part, the Kindle reading app gives me the essentials for which I've given it 3 stars:
- Download and list my Kindle library.
- Read books.
- Change font size.
- Bookmark and notes.

However, I have some suggestions that might really make it stand out.

SUGGESTIONS

- Give us the ability to choose any background and any text color. The app provides only 3 color options: white on black, black on sepia, black on white. Why limit the options? I mostly read at night while my wife sleeps, so I'm limited to white on black. Sepia and black on white are WAY too bright. Yet, white on black is still very high contrast, and my tablet casts a good amount of light around the room. Furthermore, it still fatigues my eyes, and my wife refuses to give up her e-ink Kindle reader for this very purpose. If I could select any background and text color, I could pick a black background and a neutral or dark gray for the text, or a middle to dark blue for the text. It would be so much easier on my eyes, cast less light in the room, and I might even be able to talk my wife into a tablet computer.

- Give me a way to rename my books. If I'm reading a massive 10 book series, the Kindle titles are all over the charts. If I could give the books my own names (or \\"nicknames\\"), I could ensure they would list easily in the Kindle app browser in the proper alpha-numeric order. This would also be a great thing to do in the Kindle library itself (outside the app). Let me rename or nickname my books and sort by the nickname.

- Give me a much better way of organizing my Kindle library. Currently I have a massive list and can search it. Let me place certain titles into subfolders and then be able to restrict access to the folders (either by visibility or password protection). My wife and I share titles on our account now, but we have some more adult-oriented selections in the list. When the kids get older and start reading, we can't let them access our library. This is more of a suggestion for the general Kindle library than the app specifically, but an important one I think.

The Kindle app should be mature enough to allow for some options like this. review_headline: Great texting tool for what's missing from the iPad
review_body:
HeyWire is a great texting app that provides some of what should already be included in the iPad. How presumptuous of Apple to think that EVERYONE has an Apple product. And their iMessage app only texts to other apple users. This is where HeyWire comes in. It isn't perfect, but it's free and will allow you to text anyone in your Contact database. There are some issues that I wish they would clean up. One is that the text limit is rather small (160 char.) and if you exceed that, HeyWire wil split the message into pieces, sometimes putting the end of your text before other parts, so it's hard for the reader to figure out.
Another nice feature is that the app is available for multiple systems. I downloaded it onto my Samsung tab (android) and it works fine also. The only thing is that you have to completely close the app on the unit that you are NOT going to use. I.e. - if you normally use HeyWire on you iPad, you have to completely close it on the iPad before I can use it on my Samsung. An understandable constraint.
If Heywire would simply number their 'splits' it would be MOST HELPFUL. I use a work around and send a series of short texts, so the recipients won''t have too much mind gams to put the puzzle back together. HeyWire could also make the limit HARD, so you'd have to send multiple texts if you have a lot to say.
If you want to get rid of the ads, you need to pay a reasonable $5.00 one time. I've done that and have trouble free texting with this product. I also have Text Plus Gold and it's not as good, so I use this amost always.
It's a great app for free (or short money for the ad free version). Just wish they would issue a couple of updates to make it a little prettier and smoother to use.

The game is good, however, I cannot continue to play it. Devs only have an incentive to add IAPs when there is a strong enough incentive for users to make the purchases. Users typically only have such a strong incentive when devs design a game to become impossible OR painfully redundant if the user doesn't make such purchases.

Once I have paid for an app, I must be able to enjoy t the full extent of the provided app/software, without further payment. Demos are games that may be enjoyed to a limited extent, at which time the user may replay redundantly, or make a purchase in order to continue. Games with IAPs may be enjoyed to a limited extent, at which time the user may replay redundantly, or make a purchase in order to continue, because they are designed to hinder the user from progressing in the game without making the necessary additional purchases. Thus, games with IAPs ARE MERELY DEMOS with a different name.

I will happily pay more for the app up front for an app that does not have IAPs. But charging a price up front, AND THEN charging even more, is absurd and IS NOT what I contracted for when I made my original purchase!

review_headline: An interesting and fun match three game combined with a word game!
review_body:
Game Play:

This is a typical match 3 game where you match 3 or more letters and clear them from the board. If you clear multiple sets of letters a letter is added to the mystery word and the bottom of the page. Matching 4 letters makes a super letter that will explode and clear an area of the board the next time you match it. Matching five letters will create a multi-letter that will delete all of the same letters from the board that you move the multi-letter onto. At the same time you can guess words and spell them out on the bottom of the screen. There is a pause button, a hint button and a button to switch to the match 3 mode.

As you match letters, some will fall off of the board and onto the word below and begin to fill in the blank spaces. If you feel that you know the word you can touch a letter and then touch where it goes. If you are correct the word disappears from the bottom of the screen. You can only do this so many times in the game before the game tells you that you are out of guesses. I was surprised and I selected and placed 8 letters correctly but I touch one letter wrong and it told me I was out of guesses. (It may have been 10) The more letters you match with a single move the more letters that fall into the words show below and the faster you solve the level.

The object is to spell out the words at the bottom of the screen before you use too many moves or use too many guesses. The words at the bottom of the screen are quite large and can be 14 or more letters long. There is a help screen to get you started but I still felt that learning how to play took practice as the rules were not clear in all cases.

There are three modes of play in the game and the classic mode lets you complete words and earn points, the action mode has a timer and you play against the clock and the endless mode just lets you continue playing. Each mode has three levels of difficulty from Normal, Hard and Easy.

There is a setup mode in the game play screen and you can adjust the volume, Sound FX, and select the language for the dictionary. You can also set the appearance of the screen color.

What I like:

The game plays smoothly and is fun and the light jazz in the background is pleasant and not distracting during a game in which you have to concentrate. I liked the combination of the match 3 style of game and the word game combined and it made you think more than just a simple match three game.

What I don't like:

Amazon lists OpenFeint in the game's features but it is not in the game. I like that it has been removed and I hope it stays that way in all future upgrades.

The instructions were just OK and even after playing the game I don't know how many turns (Quesses) I get.

While the game claims to have over 500,000 words I got the same word, microwaveable, twice in the same game. This double word issue occurred twice and I thought that was strange.

I do not like having an open network permission and Kindle state on a simple match three style game that is single player. While they could be there for benign reasons the can also be remnants of having OpenFeint in the game.

Summary:
Overall it is fun and I actually like it more than most other match 3 games because of the addition of solving the word portion of the game. The instructions were a little weak but I got through the games ok. I liked the music as it was light jazz and you almost didn't know it was there.

Game play was a five star rating and I really enjoyed it. It moved fast and easy. I loved the classing mode the best.

If you, like myself, were looking for a portable version of minecraft for pc, you'll be disappointed. While I understood that it wasn't going to be exactly like the main game, I was surprised how limited your inventory and world is.

While I surmise that the game will be eventually updated to have a bigger world, more items, etc. at the moment its really only suitable for us who haven't played the PC version of the game. The world itself is only about 256x256 blocks, so really no reason to explore and resources are very limited (sorry no redstone for you...). Also, for me at least, every time I made a world I would be given tiny islands making everything feel even more blah (not to mention that 90% of mobs and beasts are swimming at any given time).

However, the controls work once you get used to them, and crafting is a lot easier than the PC version. Survival is harder for more reasons than it should be, and touch controls are almost worthless in combat situations.

Bottom line: while the game has a MC feel, it doesn't even come close to the current version. If you haven't played minecraft before this will introduce the basics. If you just want to have a quick MC fix while out and about, this will help a bit. But if you are already a MC veteran or played it on PC and want near PC resources you'll most likely stop playing once you hit the invisible wall.

review_headline: Basic calendar but the alarm needs a big improvement
review_body:
I chose this calendar app because I wanted one that could be accessed offline. J2Cal is a basic calendar with \\"day\\", \\"week\\" and \\"month\\" views and a \\"today\\" option that allows users to see the day's appointments, notes and tasks all together and at a glance.
There are not many options to customize the calendar looks. However, there is a 24-hour mode if you don't like the default time slots that start at 6:00 a.m. and end at 10:00 p.m. Also, you can set a default alarm for new appointments, pick an alarm sound and snooze duration from 3 minutes to 45 minutes long. There is also a handy search function for appointments only. It will not look in the notes or tasks fields. I'm not sure how the word filter works and I have not tried the e-mail and the manage data (importing from or exporting data to the SD card) features yet.

When you are in \\"month\\" view, a black dot on the date will indicate that you have an appointment set up for that day. You can't see what you typed in until you get to the \\"day\\" view though. Setting the alarm to remind you of your appointments is easy. And it works but once the alarm has gotten your attention, there's no button to turn it off! I even deleted the appointment but the alarm kept going on (it was set to go on for 3 minutes, the shortest option available). Finally, I turned off my tablet and that took care of it. Needless to say, I don't want to turn off my tablet every time I use the calendar alarm so I decided to set it back to \\"Silence\\" and do without this feature. I hope the developer will correct the omission and add a button or option that will allow users to turn off the alarm at will.

review_headline: A great addition to Call of Mini!
review_body:
This is a sequel to the hit, \\"Call of Mini: Zombies\\" which I also loved, although right now that is not available for the new Kindle Fire HD, hopefully the developers come up with an update to that so I can enjoy both of these games! This sequel stays completely true to the original. If you played the first Call of Mini: Zombies game, you will reconize the enviroment right away. They kept the original zombies (Added new ones too... For example, giants!) Even the survivors that you try and save are from the original game. You will encounter surgeons, even the default character from Call of Mini: Zombies. It's nice to see that they haven't strayed too far from the first game.

As the title says, this is a sniper game. You are safe and sound on a building, or a scalford, or anything else that an expert marksman would find confortable. The point of the game is not to let even ONE zombie into the safe house. Plus, if you accidentally kill too many survivors, it's game over too. You'll get bonus points for the more survivors that arrive to the safe house. It's an addicting formula. It's not like Contract Killer: Zombies, infact, it's a million times better and funner.

You will, however find it a little difficult to smoothly aim and shoot. I don't know what goes on with the fire button. It's fine when you are using the sniper rife, but when you siwtch to the automatic weapon, half of the fire button is missing, which makes it so I hardly ever use it. And there are times when the zombie is right in my cross hairs, and I fire, and all it does is zomm me back out. I expect with some simple training on how to hold the Kindle Fire, this won't be a problem. And for the most part, it's not a major deal. After all, these are zombies, and they are an easy target to pick off.

All in all, it's a fun game. The developers are known for providing important updates to their games, so the game will only get better. Although, the game is leaving a little more to be desired. I don't know if I am expecting too much from a tablet game, but it would be fantastic to merge Call of Mini: Zombies, and Call of Mini: Sniper together, and add a sniper character to the online game, and protect real players as they fight zombies. But sadly, there isn't an online mode on this game. But what can you expect? It's a sniper game, not much to work with for an online element, except for previously mentioned. It's a great addition to Call of Mini, and this series is quickly becoming a favorite of mine.

I only wish I could play Call of Mini: Zombies on my new Kindle Fire HD! It is however, still available for the original Kindle Fire. So if you haven't checked that out, check it out! And then buy this one if you enjoy it.e to be desired. review_headline: Pretty Awesome Game, Permissions Not So Much
review_body:
I am so excited right now!

Let me tell you. About two months ago the EA Sports version of Tetris was the app of the week at Starbucks, and I decided to grab one to see how it would play on my ipod. Then I came to Amazon to see the price, and I was a little iffy (I can be pretty cheap). But I always wanted to know how it would compare to the screen of my Kindle Fire. And low and behold, it's the FAOTD!

For the time being, there are only two game modes, which are marathon and magic. There hasn't been anything I've seen readily enough for me to complain about. It's awesome to play on my KF. Though it is a tad different from the original, but I think I just have nostalgia at the moment and am recalling the times I played this on my gameboy (or rather my sister's or brother's gameboy).

So far so good, and I will note if complaints arise.

ETA So the permissions are pretty iffy, and reading some of the reviews of people's experiences with EA Sports is pretty disheartening in relation to this game. So for the excessive and intrusive permissions I'm going to have to know my review down a peg. I'm not sure how these permissions would relate per device (ie if it treats a KF the same as an Android phone) - that I will have to look more into. But I'm definitely going to brush up on the permission fold.

review_headline: A beautiful graphics maze game that is challenging to play!
review_body:
This game is listed as being a sequel to the original game. The Seven Stars of the Big Dipper have disappeared as they are hidden by an evil monster and it is your job to find your way through the maze and save the seven stars. Along the way you collect objects to win more points and try to travel the maze designed by the monster. The graphics are good in this game which is a maze layout that you have to roll the ball through an avoid falling off the path or being knocked off by an obstacle. The mazes and the obstacles can get very intense and this physics based game is fun. The game concept is an old one but the method in which the developers have used the beautifully designed 3D graphics of my Kindle Fire adds to the gaming experience.

You are able to calibrate your device to improve the responsiveness of your devices sensors. This appears to be a major upgrade over the original game release. It allows you to store the app onto your SD memory. That is good, if you have a memory card, as the game is listed as a massive 55.1 MB but it actually installed at 60.08 MB.

There is a link to the Amazon apps store through an ad for their new game. The game instructions are in poorly written English but it is better than my Chinese. :) There is a settings button under the \\"Gear\\" icon to adjust the controls. There is also an exit button on the home screen which is the one with the \\"X\\" in it.

During game play it told me to hold the RH side of the screen to turn right which I found strange and wondered why not just tilt the Kindle Fire. I pressed the button but then the viewing aspect of the game was reversed and I was looking behind the ball while rolling forward and I couldn't see where I was going. I touched the RH side of the screen to return to seeing the game properly but I ran out of time as the clock was running while I was looking behind the ball. It is tough to play a maze when you can't see ahead of you. Replaying the same level it did exactly the same thing so this must be built into the game to increase the challenge so be aware that eventually you will see forward again. Just tough it out and keep playing. When it says to hold to turn right or left you are better off to do light taps and that worked much better for me.

Touching the magnifying glass lets you zoom out to see where you are in the maze but I couldn't hold it too long as I needed the detail of the zoomed in screen to make sure that I didn't fall off the maze. Many sections of the path have no walls to keep you from falling. If you hold the magnifying glass too long you have to re-tap it to go back to the regular screen.

To summarize as far as I have gotten, the game graphics are spectacular and the physics motion and control in very good. The maze is difficult to get through primarily due to the changing vision perspective that the game provides to you. It makes it tricky and challenging but I liked the game. review_headline: Well made, once you figure out how to get into the game.
review_body:
Very high quality. Graphics, while retro, are quite stunning. Game play is smooth, very little issues there. Music is, again, retro, but again, very high quality.

Two negatives for me:

First, when you start the app, you get slapped in the face with a wall of ads. After recovering from the shock and disorientation, I located the play game button at the bottom, which appeared to be just another ad.

Second, I'm not a fan of virtual buttons. I prefer virtual d-pads, as I've always simply drug my finger around. On a physical controller like this emulates, that works. With virtual buttons, I kept missing the arrows. The option to move the buttons helped, but it still isn't my preference.

-1 star for obnoxious wall of ads slapping you in the face. Otherwise, a quite well made, and quite beautiful app. Dev really needs to add a description of more than four words; I almost didn't download for that reason.

I was looking for a game for my Kindle Fire that was similar to Every Word on Kindle Keyboard, or the original TextTwist. This game is not it. I wish I would have paid attention to the other reviews, but I was feeling hopeful.

As other reviewers have mentioned, I would prefer that all word possibilities would be listed rather than just a handful of the possibilities. I would also prefer that the words you find be listed in alphabetical order, so you can figure out the words you've missed. I particularly dislike that many of the words listed as solutions don't even seem to be words...I can't find them in my dictionary, anyway.

On the plus side, some of the new games are fun, such as letter mania and lightning.

Overall, if you're looking for something like the original TextTwist on Kindle Fire, keep looking. I wish I hadn't paid $2 for this disappointing version.

5 stars for the level of addiction this game has had on me.

This is a pipe game NOT like others. You DON'T have a timed board with filling water, having to throw down randomly generated pieces. Instead, you have various types of junctions which have to be arranged so ALL are used in the water flow. It started quite easily, then got tougher once pieces started to be hidden (they shunt water, but you have to figure out their actual orientation by logic).

The game is a little old, so I don't know if it'll ever be updated ... but it'd be nice if a newer version was playable full-screen on tablets (this only gives phone resolution, filling up the middle of my Kindle Fire). And hide ALL of the types of pipe!

Also ... does anyone know how long this games goes on? The description mentions 5 diffculty levels, which I can see in the way the tiles are played ... but I'm up past level 150 now, and think that things just got a bit harder. Could be my imagination, as I'm now seeing pipes everywhere I look ....

review_headline: Book Collections improved but I still can't recommend it
review_body:
I've looked at version 2.1.1.0 and while they've improved some of the features I didn't like in my prior review (and I'll note that later in the review), this is still not the app for me. If you only read on one device, do not make highlights or notes, and don't mind the over six clicks to get back to your place in the book, or, if having collections outweights those limitations, this is the app for you. For me, not so much. However, as the developer did make some important improvements, I've upgraded my review to two stars from one.

My review, edited to reflect the update:

I'm sorry to say that this app, for me, while impressive, is still not quite ready for prime time. It can do everything that the developers claim:
* you can put books into collections (or folders, as that's what they are called within the app).
* You can open Kindle books from within the app.
* And you can edit the information (the meta-data) shown for the books.

In the updated version, you can now:
* rearrange the folders once you've created them. Tap on the folder and you get an \\"up\\" option and a \\"down\\" option, which allows you to move one line at a time. You can also move to the top of the list or the bottom of the list. It's a bit cumbersome, but doable.
* move multiple books into a folder at once.
* have a book in multiple collections, as you can on a Kindle.
* sort by title or author name

What you still can't do (at least that I haven't been able to figure out so far)
* sort your folders or books by \\"most recent.\\"
* And if you've read a book through the \\"Kindle Reader\\" that is used by the the app, the fact that you've read it isn't reflected on the Carousel or in the Books tab from the Fire home page. (An admittedly minor nit; these are not in order by importance.)
* Set bookmarks with the \\"Kindle Reader\\" that is used by the app.
* Change fonts or font size within the \\"Kindle Reader\\" that is used by the app. EDIT: Apparently, if you highlight a word, then choose \\"Full Definition,\\" you will have access to the fonts menu and be able to change the font size for the book. Other options in the font menu can also be applied, though they may or may not be visible in the book itself when you return from the definiton. I had mixed results; but the attributes I selected were applied to the book when I returned to it.
* You can supposedly highlight, get definitions and add notes. However, my highlights and notes were not accessible when looking at the same book through the Books tab, and even worse, not there when I returned to the book using the reader in the Book Collections app.

This is what I've found so far. If there's a way to do any of this, or if I have an aberrant version of the app, I'd love to hear it!

I wanted to like this app. But I lose many of the features that make reading on my Kindle such a delight: the ability to change font size, to see my highlights after I've made them, to sync my location across devices, and to easily go back to my place in the book.

I still can't recommend this app, though this version is definitely improved. review_headline: Excellent for Kindle Fire, Kindle Fire HD, and HDX users
review_body:
There's a lot to like about [[ASIN:B007VUCAVO Battery HD Pro]]. It's designed for Android 2.1 devices, but since I've only used it with the Kindle Fire HD and the 1st generation Kindle Fire, you may want to look at other reviews if you have a different Android device. This review has been updated from my original review of 7/14/2012 to add the Kindle Fire HD, as I've installed it on that model to calibrate the battery.

This tight little app takes up only 5.1MB memory (now 6.7MB in version 1.36, updated) and will download on less than 60 seconds. What makes this app so good is that once it's installed and calibrated, you'll know instantly how much time you have for whatever it is that you'll be doing, in hours and minutes:

◆ Battery health
◆ Music playback
◆ Video playback
◆ Reading books (of course!)
◆ Internet browsing
◆ Time left to recharge
◆ 2D and 3D games
◆ Temperature and voltage
◆ Battery Technology

This is just a partial listing, and other Android devices (smartphones, etc) may find additional options. The large visual battery color can be customized, as can the notification settings and the charge level alerts. Calibration of of the Kindle device is highly recommended, as it will help \\"tune\\" the battery. The calibration menu reminds you to unplug the charger, lets you know if you have the necessary charge level for calibration, notes that a Wi-Fi connection is required (at least on the Kindle Fire with that connection), and to not use the device during calibration, which will take 60 to 90 minutes.

There are two versions of this app available here: the one that I'm reviewing and the [[ASIN:B007VUA7VO Battery HD]] app, which is a freebie. I started with the free version, and then upgraded to the one here in my review. The only difference that I could find is that the [[ASIN:B007VUCAVO Battery HD Pro]] app has no advertising. The ads in the freebie are not irritating, and are very small, but when I find a very good and useful piece of software, it's worth purchasing, if only to encourage the developers. And if you start with the freebie, then later upgraded, your settings and calibrations can be imported easily.

[Updated 1/23/2014]

I bought the [[ASIN:B00BWYQ9YE Kindle Fire HDX 7\\"]] in 12/2013, and based on prior experience with other Kindle Fire tablets, this was the first app that I installed on that device. Speaking personally, I've found it to be an essential app, and one well worth considering for any user.

Whichever one you choose, Battery HD or Battery HD Pro, you'll find an excellent 5-star utility app for the new Kindle Fire HDX series, the Kindle Fire HD or for the original Kindle Fire.

review_headline: Better Than Average Tower Defense Game
review_body:
This is a good looking game! The HD graphics are top notch and look very smooth on my Tablets.

The game makes a reasonable attempt at a plot with a fairly predictable,yet, reasonably engaging story about aliens attacking. Nothing groundbreaking, but , still better than no storyline.

The gameplay is fairly bland. The basic, ultra-repetitive "Tower Defense" game mechanic that drives this game is exactly what you would expect from this kind of game. Events transpire a little too slowly in the game for it to ever feelexciting,however,the thin plotline and better than average graphics are enough incentive to drive a player to complete the game.

This would be a solid 4 star game were it not for the integrated IAP, which certainly does not belong in a paid app,but,also would utterly nullify any challenge or enjoyment the game might offer if purchased.

The IAP garbage that this greedy scumbag double-dipper of a developer has integrated into this otherwise decent game does NOT sell anything that cannot be earned through gameplay, and the game is not balanced in a way that tries to force the user to commit IAP, so, it is not gamebreaking.

review_headline: In-App purchases wrecked what could have been a good game (and it uses OpenFeint without telling us).
review_body:
***Update***: This app also has OpenFeint. Turn off your internet connection and you will get the OpenFeint offline message when you start this app. That would account for the huge data usage I mentioned at the bottom of my review. So, this app connects us to OpenFeint and doesn't even tell us. Is it also creating OpenFeint accounts for our devices? I'm guessing this issues will change this app from a disliked app to a hated app.

Original review:
Too bad, I was going to rate this app high. But I have to agree with the other reviewers here that this app is an example of pure greed. Paying again for something you already had? Really? If it was a free game, then the in-app purchases would be justified. But it's not a free game! A paid app should be a total app--you should get all the functionality, all the bells and whistles, all the time--you shouldn't have to pay again to play the game the same way you did when you first bought it.

The In-App purchases are:
$0.99 for 5 more Shields after you used up the initial 10. (Which doesn't even get you back to the original 10.)
$0.99 for 5 more Slowmotions after you used up the initial 10. (Again, only half of what you started with.)
$1.99 to unlock the Rescue level of the Story mode, if you don't want to complete the Run level first.

But here's a helpful hint (if you don't mind wiping out your scores): if you clear the apps data section, the initial 10 Shields and 10 Slowmotions will be restored. (Hey, a way to stick it to the man--or the developer in this case. LOL)

It's too bad really because it's not a bad game. Its graphics are crisp and move very smoothly. The controls are responsive and the gameplay is actually fun. Though, there were a few times when the app did quit without prompting with the Exit (No/Yes) screen first, which was irritating.

The multiplayer mode is a bit silly, especially on phones. Though, I would think itwould be pretty tough to play on a Kindle as well--can you really see 4 guys huddled around that device madly tapping on the screen?

And the description is wrong. There are only two game modes, not three (Story and Endless). There is no \\"Practice\\" mode.

As a side note, the data usage is sort of sucky: even after moving this app to the SD card it still uses 1.23MB of internal storage. And after playing just a little, data usage is 5.70MB (a total of 6.93MB).

To summarize: Greed wrecks a good app.

This app is pretty much what it claims to be. Solid gameplay, familiar map, but without some features that would improve replay value. You can alter the number of computer and human players, as well as computer skill levels, but it resets to default after each game. No keeping your favorite setup for easy replay. Also, there is no option for choosing countries manually or placing your initial armies. This can leave you with very poor starting positions exacerbated by poor AI army placement.

Aside from that, it still is a fun game, with lots of replay value. A few additions like cards, more maps, or small rule changes (like alliances or random versus player selected starting countries) would make this an easy five star game.

One warning for would be players: defense is favored heavily in small battles, just as in real Risk. Aggressive play early in the game likely will not be rewarded.

review_headline: Not As Good As The Original : (
review_body:
I am a HUGE Word to Word fan but was disappointed in this game. It is like a bad movie sequel. Some of the categories seem like after thoughts. For example, Romance2 and Animals2, and the Musicals category is just listed twice, without the \\"2\\". With all the themes in the world to chose from, you'd think they would have all original categories. Also, words repeat themselves in the categories several times, and some of the words are not words at all but things like \\"we were made\\" answer: \\"to fit together\\". Really!!

The puzzles are not very challenging (Richard...Gere, Julia...Roberts) and easily solvable, some in less than 15 seconds. There are significantly fewer puzzles than the original, 240 as opposed to 400. They added music, which I find distracting, (you can mute it), and changed the background to blue, which isn't as easy to see. It seems like this app was made hastily, and there are a lot of pop culture references, which will quickly out date themselves. This game is lacking the creativity and originality that made the first Word to Word so spectacular.

UPDATE 10/2014 The developers did update the app and removed the second \\"MUSICALS\\" category and replaced it with \\"CARS\\".

Maps With Me is a fantastic app for using a digital map without requiring an internet connection. I used it recently on a business trip to supplement my driving directions. While I only have access to the free version (using on a Kindle Fire) the application still works great - I treat it as a replacement for my paper maps (having the ability to zoom in to a specific location and being able to read the street names easily is much preferred to folding out a big paper map taking up too much space). The app is missing exit numbers (for interstates and highways) but I'm confident that the creators will be adding this feature within a couple months. Also searching for addresses and possibly offline directions may be on the way as well.

I give this app 5 stars for ease of use and the great detailed maps - Maps with me is not a GPS step-by-step directional system (at least not yet for Kindle Fire users) but simply a paper replacement - I recommend this for people for don't like to rely on always having an internet connection or always being connected to a satellite. Great app and I know it will get even better with time as it becomes more popular.

review_headline: Warning! Latest version is basically spyware!
review_body:
This WAS a five-star app. But now it is nothing more than trojan-horse spyware.

Do you want to pay $15 for spyware? Neither do I. I've been using the previous version which did not spy on all its customers.

This software wants to know what you've been running on your device, both currently and before launching. It also wants to start up with your phone, so it can gather this information.

Look at the permissions:
* Get information about the currently or recently running tasks: a thumbnail representation of the tasks, what activities are running in it, etc.
* Request authtokens from the AccountManager
* Access the list of accounts in the Accounts Service
* Get notified that the operating system has finished booting
* Manage the list of accounts in the AccountManager

Basically, this wants to access both your Amazon accounts and your Google accounts. But it is WORSE than this: now it wants to MODIFY your accounts! That's bad, folks.

It also wants access to your Gmail. Why?

Protect yourself by asking:
* What business does this app have messing with your accounts?
* What business does this app have with monitoring what you do with your Android device?
* What business does this app have reading your email?

Do yourself a favor and skip this suite in favor of a company that does not spy on its paying customers.

review_headline: Finally, a Pogoplug app for the Fire
review_body:
I am just so happy they finally came out with a Pogoplug app for the Kindle Fire. It works well enough with my [[ASIN:B006I5MKZY Pogoplug Series 4 Multimedia Sharing Device]]. My video streams smoothly. The pics take some time to load, and swiping from one to the next takes large swipes and is a little sticky, but I'm just happy to be able to see them.

There is a \\"print\\" option, but I'm not sure how to make that work. It doesn't recognize iPrint and there's no option for setting it up. \\"Share\\" lets me send links to my photos to Facebook and Twitter and I can email the link to friends. Sharing to iPrint doesn't work.

review_headline: Despite great controls this game isn't meant for handhelds
review_body:
The Good: Excellent visuals, captures the creepy atmosphere of the series, new story and protagonist, great control scheme

The Bad: Nothing new at all, combat doesn't translate as smoothly on the touch screen, too many enemies are thrown at you, story doesn't really go anywhere

Don't mistake this as just a port from the original game. This is a whole new adventure with a new protagonist named Vandal that is trying to help stop the Necromorphs from getting aboard like Isaac did in the first game. The story doesn't really progress too much and there isn't much here except a twist ending, and a few creepy scenes where Vandal seems to be hallucinating, but other than that don't expect anything grand.

The gameplay is still the same with alternate fire for each of the four weapons you use. The Necromorphs are all the same from the first game as well as using the store, upgrading weapons with power nodes, and even zero gravity and vacuum areas. That's also the main problem is that this game feels old for longtime fans who have played every Dead Space game. Only four weapons? No new Necromorphs? Nothing here is new except the levels, and story, but even that isn't much. My main problem with the game is that it throws too much action at you for the small screen to handle. Not in a way of technical problems, but you can't maneuver as fluidly with touch controls as you can a gamepad or keyboard and mouse. Sure the controls are mapped smartly like tilting the device for alt fire selection, shaking up to jump in zero gravity, and tapping the icons on Vandal's armor for stasis, but it doesn't work as well as a gamepad.

I died many times just because I couldn't keep track of everything on-screen and couldn't react as fast as I'm used to. When you are in a lockdown area and several Necromorphs come at you I just couldn't shoot, reload, use stasis, turn around, melee, as fast as I could and you will use all of those several times in a shoot out. Despite this major flaw everything else works, and the game looks great using next generation phone technology to pull off the creepy lighting and atmosphere the series is known for.

In the end you get some replay value with New Game+, 5 minutes to kill, and an endless mode, but due to the high difficulty and overwhelming combat you may call it quits after one play through. If you are a longtime Dead Space vet this is perfect for a quick 5-6 hour Dead Space fix on the go, but newcomers will get a taste of what the console versions await.t out. Here's a tip, ALWAYS read reviews about something on Amazon.com and make an informed decision. I have seen ridiculous comments on Amazon before, but most of the time, you can get sound advice about a product. Some people will complain about a \\"color\\" of something and give a negative review. That's just silly.

In any case, it is interesting that Amazon gives apps away that DO NOT have very good ratings. I love what Amazon does, and it is a great place to acquire things. HOWEVER, someone needs to be a little more proactive in insuring that the customers are protected against digital media and apps.

review_headline: Modern day Version of Atari's Space Invaders
review_body:
I love the bright neon color graphics on my Kindle Fire. This game reminds me of how I'd spend HOURS playing Space Invaders or Galaga on my Atari back in High School.
A storyline follows the game throughout each level. This can be skipped but, it is useful at the start of the game, as the as it gives information for the upcoming levels. Some of the storyline is even a bit comical but, if you prefer to skip the story, this can become tedious & annoying, especially if you find yourself needing to restart the level....more than once.
Although, I love the game itself, I personally had difficultly maneuvering my ship on my K-Fire, from left to right, as well as firing at the same time, I was unable to get my ship to go or, do quite what I wanted it to do. A joystick with dual controls might prove to be a better feature.
I was also unsure what my upgraded weapons were for, what they could do & for how long. As well as, when exactly to use them.
A couple of upgrades for a joystick w/ dual controls & the ability to turn off the story after a level (regardless if a levels' win or loss) only then, this game will be sure to keep me from my housework for hours!

review_headline: Nothing like it elsewhere, fastest I have ever gone from free demo to buying an app
review_body:
[[VIDEOID:mo32LFRLSARPV7D]]I only realized this app existed earlier today when I updated my Roku remote app by Reno. I AM IN LOVE WITH THIS APP. I have added a video to show it in use with my Le Pan II running Android 3.2. I can easily stream photos, music, and movies from my tablet to my Roku. I have been waiting for this type of function for 6 months and this does almost everything I want already. As I mentioned in the remote review, this app also contains Reno's very good Roku remote, so it has added value (though there are a few aesthetic reasons to still have the other remote too). As far as I can tell no other app offers this content function for Roku on Android up to now.

**Benefits of this app for Roku users with Android:

Streaming content (obviously).

Built in Roku remote that has: channel button easy access, keyboard for typing in searches, Wifi connection for line of sight issues/practical jokes on people, lit remote for use in low light conditions, cheaper than buying a replacement remote if physical one breaks.

Compatibility:
I used my Le Pan II tablet to stream with Android 3.2 Honeycomb. I tested this on all 3 generations of Roku. The oldest, my N1000 did not play the video streaming but did play music and photos. My Roku 2050X was what shows in the video and ran everything. I also tested on the latest gen Roku 2 3000X and it played everything including video. I have a Netgear wireless N router, in case the question comes up.

Additional thoughts:
***The videos I recorded with my tablet stuttered and buffered a lot, but that is mentioned in the app description. The video you see me play is one I added that is .mp4 format. I also checked a .wmv file and it played fine, and I think .mkv works fine too and likely others.

The picture quality was pretty nice; it matched the quality of the files as I see them on my tablet. I do not have a lot of HD files, but those maytax the stream and stutter.

The only other thing I would like is the ability to stream webpages and embedded video from them to the Roku, as of now that is not an option, but I hope Reno may add it in the future.

Final note: Thank you Dev, love your excellent work. Keep it up!

review_headline: Finally, a music app that's actually capable
review_body:
Fiinally, an app that allows some diversity in music programming! Note the word programming instead of performance. As the manual notes and I paraphrase: the Aneroid OS does not allow for fast latency making it currently impossible play notes without delay. In fact, the keyboards are there to get the "feel" for programming patches and is why there are note programming screens for each synthesis/sampler component.

As far as performance goes the sound is of high quality. There are enough components such as multi-filters with resonance and some degree of assignable modulation.

Samplers have start/stop points that can make to creative fun besides having much of the same sound design tools as the synths.

As others have noted the interface takes some getting used to. All in all Caustic 2 is by far the best music app I've purchased for Kindle Fire.

There are areas that needdm improvement imo. That's one of the reasons I purchased it.

PROS:
1. good sounding with many synthesis, drum, and sampling units
2. quick learning curve
3. a large arrangement of sound editing tools
4. paid version features work as advertised

CONS:
1. user interface while quick to learn is unintuitive at times
2. understanding Aneroid has latency issues it's hard to believe there isn't a way of working alternative perfomance systems such as grids or x/y screen mapping
3. changing paradigms is fine if they serve the User but they don't seem to as Caustic currently exists. That's a 2nd reason I invested in it
4. more of everything, bring in modulation matrixes, 3 osc Synths, add more types of oscs as well as unique ones such as wavetable (small samples that contain a couple to 128 unique sample fragments such as the Waldorf Blofeld hardware synthesis, also, granular syynthesis (samples chopped into grains and reassembled) great for time synching among other unique and unusual effects. Lastly Additive synthesis, the building of waves into highly evocative sounds as well as very crisp, clean DX7 sounds.

As is Caustic puts quite a bit into a sequencing, synthesis/sampling app. It is well worth its full price and is a maturing program that, while not totally unique, does more than anything to create music in Android land. It also seems likely to keep developing and improving.

review_headline: An eggciting, different kind of game - 4 1/2 stars
review_body:
Overall: 4 1/2 stars

Originality: 5 stars

Eggsplosive is one of the silliest games I've played on my Kindle Fire. It's also one of the more original games that I've seen. Basically, you touch overfed chickens, which then explode, spewing out eggs and giblets, which kill any cows and pigs that are wandering around the barnyard. (If you're not familiar with giblets, they're the edible offal of chickens, and that's probably more than you want to know.) It's actually a pretty eggciting game.

Game Play: 4 1/2 stars

Game play is very simple. On every barnyard scene, there are one or two chickens and several cows and pigs. When you touch the screen near a chicken, the chicken explodes and sends eggs and giblets flying around. When the eggs and giblets hit a cow or pig, the cow or pig dies.

The goal is to kill a specified minimum number of cows and pigs on the screen using only the chickens that you have for that level (usually only one). If you don't kill every cow and pig, you have to replay the level. There are ten Standard levels, which have to be played in order. Clearing all ten levels unlocks ten Skill levels. Some levels are pretty easy, but others are a real challenge. In about an hour, I cleared every level, with scores of 141,306 (Standard) and 92,245 (Skill).

The chickens, cows, and pigs are wandering around, never standing still. The trick is to time the explosions (okay, they're \\"eggsplosions\\") based on the location of the chicken(s), and take advantage of hay bales which cause the eggs and giblets to ricochet. There were a few levels that I initially thought were impossible to clear, but I kept trying and eventually figured out the solution.

Eggsplosive is hardly Angry Birds or Where's My Water?, but it's a fun game that's more challenging than it appears at first glance.

Replayability: 4 stars

A timer is running, and your score for each level depends on the time taken. For that reason, replaying the game may get you a higher score.e taken. For that reason, replaying the game may get you a higher score.

I have sent an email to Amazon hoping that they can help (although I don't look at it as their issue) because I don't think I have any other non-drastic options (a system refresh is the only thing I can think to resolve this).

review_headline: QuickOffice Pro and Docs to Go offer little enhancements
review_body: Got this on sale for $5 right before getting the other 2 suites. Still a great purchase. The document and spreadsheet interface is great on both my tablet (Iconia a500) and phone (G2). Superior to the other popular office apps.  However, QuickOffice (pro or trial) does a much better job rendering PDFs quickly and has a more functional interface. Additionally, OfficeSuite is not well integrated with cloud retrevial, and does not allow documents to be saved into PDF format. Combined this means while it has all the formatting you want the ability to convert it into a polished file without all the "word" markup is a cumbersome process.  I look forward to cloud support and the ability save as PDF. Without that, it is not a stand-alone product, but still one worth having.

This is my most indispensable app - almost flawless in form and function...almost.  Your online tripcase account can be fed directly by most major online booking sites.  I use Carlson-Wagonlit for work.  The main screen presents every aspect of your trip in chronological order, clearly and concisely notifying when there are airline gate changes, delays, terminal and gate of connecting flights, one-tap links to contact info, maps, weather for each leg of your journey, rental car, hotel, etc.  I get quicker updates in TripCase than I do from the airlines or gate announcements.  The separate tools page for each trip allows you to quickly and easily locate alternate flights, currency converter, general flight schedules, maps, phone and contact for all aspects of your trip, allows social media publishing straight from the tools screen, seat maps for your flights, allows manual or automatic itinerary sharing, trip directions for driving, weather, traffic alerts, and even bonus offers that might apply to your itinerary (like double miles if you use avis with united, etc.).  There is, however, an Achilles heel: the expense tool is frustrating and ill-conceived.  It's selectable categories, etc. are on \\"rollers\\" that are poorly done, you must specify your currency for every expense (no default), must manually input the date each time, the amount defaults to the alpha keyboard instead of a numeric one...you get the idea.  The real strength of this app is how much it does for you in the background.  I've changed itineraries and flights at the last minute and it never skips a beat. You NEVER have to search for necessary info.  I won't ever travel again without TripCase along for the ride.

review_headline: Great for emergencies in Geneva or Zurich...
review_body:
I don't want to appear too picky, but given that you've hit two separate areas where I have some professional experience, I think this bears mentioning. I'm a former paramedic and EMT/Red Cross CPR, BLS, and Advanced First Aid Instructor; I also worked for the U.N. at the Palais des Nations in Genève, Switzerland.

Which is why l found myself wondering as to whether or not you saw this app as the \\"Swiss Army knife\\" of emergency response applications, with something for every conceivable emergency. I mean, why else would your app's symbol be a Swiss national flag?

A white cross on a red border is the symbol of the small quadri-lingual European country, and has nothing to do with emergency response. A RED cross on a white background has been the symbol for emergency medical response since the 19th Century-- it's what was on the armband of American combat medics up until the last 2/3ds of the Vietnam war.

While that's cool trivia, it's not what would have been anyone's idea of good marketing ploy. Rather than rallying around Switzerland (?), I would encourage you to reverse the colors, and make the app's symbol a red cross.

review_headline: I give it two stars because it was a great 25 days!
review_body: I would have easily given it five stars if it had worked past my buying the full key.  I used the trial Touchdown for 25 days and it was fun and performed flawlessly.  I bought and downloaded the full key upgrade from Amazon and ran it on my Fire.  Following deployment all areas of Touchdown synchronization continued to function except email.  The email screen was blank and the diagnostics log indicated 0 mail content downloaded even though real-time synchronization status showed successful email traffic.  I messed with it for a couple of days more including deleting and reinstalling the software and wiping the database several times.  I also worked some with NitroDesk support.  Nothing brought back email functionality, but my contacts, tasks, and appointments continued to synchronize.  Strange too, I could send email from the fire and they would deliver successfully.  This appears to be a problem within Touchdown where it does not recognize and display valid incoming or outgoing email traffic.  I had no choice but to have the paid key removed by Amazon.  Oddly, as soon as the paid key was removed the trial version started to function again and emails started to flow again.  There appears to be more to the key enable program then a simple license upgrade and it appears to be broken in some way that is not favorable to my setup.  So even if you use the trial version successfully that is no guarantee that the full license version will run correctly.  I can only suggest that if you buy the paid key you apply it immediately after purchase so as to test it before the very short Amazon warrantee period runs out.

review_headline: Bad controls + unforgiving game play = bad game
review_body: I gave this game two stars because I like the graphics and art style.  That being said, the controls were unreasonably difficult. During the tutorial it'd ask me to 'turn left for 3 seconds' or 'lean back for three seconds' but wouldn't register if I was even a tiny bit off and if you weren't perfect in the tutorial then it busted you back to the beginning. When I did finally get the controls I kept missing the landing island, which is the size of the head of a pin when you're job is to aim for it a mile away. The one time I finally landed on island I didn't understand the landing instructions and splatted on the bulls eye. Tutorial failed, start over.  So I quit the tutorial and tried a real mission- I might add that figuring out what mission is what is very difficult since they're all just random numbers splayed on a wall- And I proceeded fail that too. I had no idea what I was suppose to do and I received no promps or aid. I still missed the stupid island which just felt embarrassing because of the aforementioned poorly designed controls.  In short: Nice graphics, but controls need serious work and the gameplay needs to be easier. Or failing easier gameplay, easier to understand.  Give this game a pass people, wait for a sequel or a rerelease that fixes a lot of the issues with this game.

review_headline: Best app I've seen for the Kindle Fire
review_body:
This is the best app I've seen for the Kindle Fire so far. It only took me a minute to figure out how to navigate through the magazine with it.

THESE ARE SOME OF THE NICE FEATURES:

1) EW has its own menu on the bottom of the screen, and in addition, at the top of the screen they have colored tabs in some sections, so you can jump from say, the MOVIE section to the BOOK section.

2) In many articles, the top part of the screen is frozen, and the bottom part (with the text of the article) is scrollable. So, don't forget to scroll down to see the whole article.

3) The touch screen seems to be more responsive than in other applications. It only took the lightest tap to change pages.

The only things I miss are the ability to bookmark articles and look up words in a dictionary, like it do with Kindle Books. But this is a magazine, afterall, so I give it 5 stars.
